“As well as a single overview of pensions in one place, a dashboard will show pensions that people may have lost touch with.

“While this is only part of the important work to ensure people have the retirement savings they need, it is a vital part of making planning for later life easier.”

Tom Selby, public policy director at AJ Bell, said: “Automatic enrolment has been one of the great public policy successes of recent decades, ensuring millions of employees are building at least some level of pension savings for retirement.

“But as people move jobs throughout their working lives, they often leave old workplace pensions behind, and over time it’s easy to lose track of them.”

open image in gallery About 2.5 million lost pots are thought to be held by people aged under 55 ( Alamy/PA )

Mr Selby added: “While the average pot value may not sound life-changing on its own, £6,000 can make a significant difference to someone’s retirement income.

“That figure rises to £10,000 among those aged over 55 – people who will likely be thinking about retirement in the not-too-distant future – and that is just an average, meaning many will hold much larger forgotten sums.”

He said customers using AJ Bell’s own pension-finding tool have tracked down accounts worth an average of £18,500 when adding up the combined value of pots found by each individual customer, “while some have used the service to find and combine pots worth over £1 million”.

Mr Selby said: “Combining pensions isn’t necessarily the right move for everyone and savers should take the time to shop around for the right provider, taking into account factors such as charges, choice, flexibility and service.

“Some older-style pensions can have valuable guarantees attached that will be lost on transfer, so checking whether this is the case is also crucial.

“For those who aren’t sure, it may be worth speaking to a financial adviser or reading up free resources like those on Money Helper.

“Whether you ultimately decide to combine pensions or not, the first step is to get a handle on what you’ve got and where it is invested.”

Mr Selby said services such as the Pension Tracing Service and pension finding tools can already help to reunite people with lost pension pots.

News.title: Britain on track to lose one pub a day in 2026 as cost pressures bite
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Britain is on track to lose one pub a day in 2026 after almost 300 closed in the first nine months of this year, according to industry data.

The figures come from the British Beer and Pub Association (BBPA), which counted 295 closures between the start of January and the end of September.

The trade body expects the losses to continue at a pace of one pub a day through 2026, reaching an estimated 360 venue closures.

England accounted for the bulk of the closures recorded so far, with 226 pubs closing over the period. Scotland lost 64 pubs, while five closed in Wales.

Within England, the South West was not the hardest hit: the South East recorded 42 closures and the North West 39.

The BBPA believes the closures will cost the industry about 5,000 jobs, with more than half of those roles currently filled by under-25s.

Trade industry bosses urged Andy Burnham to tackle other taxes and labour costs impacting business ( Reuters )

Pub operators have linked the latest raft of closures to the high tax burden and regulatory costs affecting the sector, despite recent business rates discounts for pubs.

The pub sector has benefited from a 15 per cent discount to business rates for the current tax year, with a 20 per cent cut from next year.

Trade industry bosses said recent support will be a significant help but urged Prime Minister Andy Burnham to tackle other taxes and labour costs impacting business.

In a statement, Emma McClarkin, chief executive of the BBPA, said: “When a local closes, the damage is felt far and wide.

“It’s not just workers, communities, our heritage and high streets who lose out when a pub closes – the Treasury loses, on average, £200,000 in tax receipts every time a local calls last orders.

“The Prime Minister has pledged that the cavalry is coming, which is why we’re asking Government to tackle the root of the problem through a permanently fair and sustainable rates burden, freezing beer duty, increasing draught relief and reviewing employment costs for under-25s.

“This will mean we can carry on keeping people in jobs, boosting the economy, and being at the heart of communities.”

News.title: Max Verstappen is back and Mercedes are already worried
News.content:
Kimi Antonelli, third: “It was a very tough race out there but really happy with a podium at the end, I managed to take advantage of the fight between Lewis and Lando. To take P3 is a great result from the team, very happy with that.”

He is told that he can clinch the title at the next race:

“Can I, really? Let’s not worry about that. Let’s try to do the best weekend possible and finish the job.”

Charles Leclerc, second: “We were quite strong at the beginning of the race and then we started degrading at the end of the first stint. I pushed a lot at the beginning of the last stint and then degraded a bit more than the others. I gave it all and I don’t regret anything.

“I don’t think there’s anything more we could do but be a bit more aggressive at the start. It’s true that we brought some small new parts to the car which maybe helped us to do a little step forward but it’s enough. Today I think we had a good pace overall.”

Max Verstappen, winner: “It’s taken a while but I think this race was very good. We had pace when we needed to have it on the soft tyre and the medium. Very happy to win here. You always try to do your best and luckily [the start] it was just good enough.

“I think the last few races have been really positive for us. It’s great to see and we have a lot of motivation in the team to try to deliver even more results... hopefully we can have a bit more fun until the end of the year.”

News.title: The cheats prosper: Man City thrash 10-man Liverpool
News.content:
Just when the Premier League and the world outside of east Manchester and Abu Dhabi needed Liverpool to step up, to strike back, to make a point, they faltered. Maybe it was unfair to expect them to do so, given the circumstances. But unfairness, lack of clarity and uncertainty are all prevailing moods in English football at present.

How we had rubbed our hands in anticipation of Manchester City having to play their first league fixture here at Anfield after being found guilty of industrial-scale fraud with 114 of the 115 financial charges being proven against them.

It felt apt that it was at the home of Liverpool, who, along with Arsenal, possess the strongest sense of grievance at having been denied trophies and glory by City’s cheating. As expected, there were banners everywhere at Anfield. “A generation of supporters cheated,” one read and it summed up the depth of the anger.

News.title: Three tasks to get your home ready for autumn, according to a professional cleaner
News.content:
When I was sweating away this summer, I never thought the weather would turn, but it’s almost time to crank up our radiators and crack out the big duvet.

They’re the tasks no one likes doing, but luckily for you, I’ve worked as a cleaner for more than a decade. I’ve discovered some shortcuts to make the hated jobs that bit easier.

Tip one: Keep your summer duvet fresh in storage

If, like me, you want to get your winter duvet out, your summer one needs to be cleaned and packed away to keep it fresh come spring.

Start by spot cleaning any stains. You can just use a standard household fabric stain remover for this. If you want to wash your duvet, most domestic washing machines aren’t big enough to fit a double, let alone a king or a super king. Your best bet is to take them down to the laundrette and follow the care instructions on the label.

News.title: Resurgent Verstappen on fire in the Singapore smog
News.content:
Welcome to our live coverage for the sprint race for the 2026 Singapore Grand Prix from the Marina Bay Circuit. Given the way the championship standings are, it looks like Kimi Antonelli has one hand on the drivers’ title. That means that the most significant thing is the battle for individual race victories. That includes grands prix, but also sprint races, like we have today.

Formula One is very keen on sprint races, increasing their number significantly next year, but we have never had one in Singapore before. We will find out today whether there was good reason for it. I suppose the logic is that even a processional sprint race is better than a free practice session and that having two qualifying sessions on a street circuit such as this is exciting, too.

Still, although he might be strolling towards the championship, he and Mercedes are not the dominant force they were at the start of the season when he won five in a row having finished second in the opening race. In fact, in the last 10 grands prix, Antonelli has won three and Russell two. With Max Verstappen’s win in Malaysia last weekend it meant each of Red Bull, McLaren, Ferrari and Mercedes have won races this season.

It is Verstappen who is in strong form in an upgraded Red Bull, as he snuck pole position from George Russell by just over a tenth of a second. He was followed by Charles Leclerc in the Ferrari and then Oscar Piastri in the McLaren. Antonelli, in the upgraded Mercedes, found things more difficult, finishing down in seventh nearly 0.7sec off the pace.

Anyway, the sprint gets under way in about 30 minutes and we will be here for all the updates from that, as well as qualifying later today.

News.title: Majestic All Blacks copy Springbok playbook to dismantle Australia
News.content:
Good morning and welcome to our live coverage of this Bledisloe Cup Test as New Zealand host Australia at Eden Park in Auckland.

The All Blacks are enduring one of the toughest periods in their history, having suffered three successive Test defeats against South Africa in August and September, which saw the Springboks claim the inaugural Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry series tour. Dave Rennie’s men are under immense pressure to avoid a fourth consecutive Test defeat for the first time since 1998.

You could argue there’s never been a better opportunity for Australia to beat New Zealand at Eden Park. The Wallabies are enjoying a six-Test unbeaten run – their longest such streak since 2017, with five games in this rejuvenated period coming under new head coach Les Kiss. In their most recent outing, Australia secured an extraordinary 42-38 victory over a much-changed South Africa side in Perth, despite being reduced to 11 players at one point.

Australia will feel further encouraged due to several key absences for New Zealand, as Ardie Savea, Ruben Love, Richie Mo’unga, Caleb Clarke, Fehi Fineanganofo, Billy Proctor and Anton Lienert-Brown are all out injured. In a reshuffle for the All Blacks, Damian McKenzie will begin at fly-half for the first time in 2026. Other notable inclusions for the home side see all three Barrett brothers, Codie Taylor, Tupou Vaa’i, Cam Roigard and Will Jordan starting.

Meanwhile, the visitors are without the suspended Hunter Paisami, with Isaac Henry taking his place at centre. The likes of Ryan Lonergan, Len Ikitau, Harry Wilson, Ben Donaldson and Max Jorgensen, who were all key to the triumph against the Springboks, retain their starting spots.

All the statistics overwhelmingly favour New Zealand. The All Blacks have not lost any edition of the Bledisloe Cup since 2002, winning 51 series to Australia’s 12, and are unbeaten at Eden Park since 1994, when they lost to France. Australia are winless at Eden Park since 1986, tasting defeat there 30 times in 34 games, and have lost their last 11 Tests against New Zealand.

However, given the landscape heading into this historic rivalry between these two heavyweights, it genuinely feels like anything could happen.

Kick-off is at 7:10am.

News.title: Black British Business Awards 2026 winners revealed
News.content:
The chief executive of Dr. Martens has been named the Black British Business Person of the Year at the 2026 Black British Business Awards (BBBAwards).

Ije Nwokorie, who became chief of Dr. Martens in January last year and is the only black chief executive in the FTSE 250, was awarded in recognition of his role shaping Dr. Martens’ growth strategy.

He is recognised inside Dr. Martens for his strong communication with staff, according to the judges.

Before joining Dr. Martens, Mr Nwokorie spent more than 11 years at Wolff Olins, the marketing giant, before working as a senior director at Apple.

Born in the US but brought up from age six against the backdrop of post-civil-war Nigeria, Mr Nwokorie has described how he and his family went from the lifestyle trappings of 1960s America to a small Nigerian village and a home with no running water.

On winning the award, Mr Nwokorie said: “This recognition means a lot to me. While this award bears my name, it reflects the talent, dedication and generosity of the incredible teammates, mentors and leaders who have shaped me as a person and a professional.

“It is a powerful reminder that there is nothing more important in our leadership journeys than the time we invest to help others thrive.”

Alongside his executive career, he has served as a trustee at Charity: water for nearly a decade and held board roles at cultural and humanitarian organisations including the Institute of International Visual Arts and Malaria No More UK.

He also served as chairman of trustees for the Chineke! Orchestra, a British orchestra championing change and the first in Europe to feature a majority of black and ethnically diverse musicians.

The Black British Business Awards started in 2014 to celebrate the achievements of black people in British business. The Telegraph is the national media partner for the awards.

Mr Nwokorie was presented with the award at an exclusive ceremony sponsored by JPMorgan Chase at London’s Hilton Park Lane hotel.

Speaking at the ceremony, Sophie Chandauka, the executive founder of the awards, said: “You lend the BBBAwards credibility not simply to celebrate excellence, but to ensure the best and brightest from all communities get a fair shot. That commitment has made the BBBAwards the UK’s premium awards programme for black business achievement.”

A spokesman for JPMorgan Chase said: “We couldn’t be prouder to support and celebrate such an outstanding breadth of black British talent.

“Their accomplishments continue to inspire future generations and demonstrate the exceptional value they bring to businesses, communities and the wider UK economy.”

This year’s winners are as follows:

Black British Business Person of the Year: Ije Nwokorie, chief executive of Dr Martens

Arts and Media Rising Star: Sheniece Charway, artist partnership manager [EMEA], YouTube/Google

Arts and Media Senior Leader: Amie Parker-Williams, director, digital commissioning and production, Paramount

Entrepreneur Rising Star: Dr Elsa Zekeng, founder and chief executive, SökerData

Entrepreneur Senior Leader: Antonia Okonma Shittu, founder and chief executive, A-List Lace Hair

Financial Services Rising Star: Nana Agyemang, proposition delivery manager, Barclays

Financial Services Senior Leader: Melissa Max-Macarthy, formerly managing director, head of strategy and innovation, retail banking, NatWest Group

Professional Services Rising Star: Jack Van Cooten, senior manager – external vendors and data, Oliver Wyman

Professional Services Senior Leader: Laurie-Anne Power KC, barrister, 25 Bedford Row

Retail and Hospitality Senior Leader: Leona De Graft, vice-president of global ecommerce, Levi Strauss and Co

Retail and Hospitality Rising Star: Rickey Devonish, head of apprenticeships and emerging talent, JD Group

Sports.title: Police officer injured as Saints and Pompey fans tear down fences after fierce derby clash – as four arrested
Sports.content:
Next

A POLICE officer has been injured and four arrests made after disorder broke out between rival fans at the south coast derby clash.

Riot police and officers on horseback were brought in as part of a huge operation to disperse crowds outside St Mary’s Stadium when fans started taunting each other.



Supporters of Southampton and Portsmouth tried to clash following Southampton’s 1-0 victory.

Segregation fences were torn down but were prevented from getting in contact with one another by police and stewards.



Hampshire Police confirmed that one officer had suffered a minor injury and had been treated.

The force added an investigation had been launched and investigators would review all footage to identify those involved.

Cops made four arrests.

Before kick-off, a 20-year-old man from Southampton and an 18-year-old man from Ringwood were arrested on suspicion of possessing a flare.



Afterwards, a 38-year-old man from Southampton was arrested on suspicion of obstructing the highway as Portsmouth supporter coaches left the city.

A fourth man, who was not attending the game, was arrested by cops patrolling Hoglands Park before the match, who identified a man they believed was carrying stolen soft drinks.

Meanwhile, 50-year-old man from Southampton, who was also not attending the game, was stopped and during a search, a knuckle duster was found.

He has been arrested on suspicion of shoplifting and possessing an offensive weapon in public.

Simon Dodds, assistant chief constable and gold commander for the policing operation, claimed it was “another really successful policing operation” despite the trouble.



He said: “We have seen almost 30,000 fans get to and from the game safely.

“Sadly, there were a minority of fans who tried to find an opportunity to cause disruption, but our teams on the ground, supported by club stewards, were able to act decisively and take control of the situation.”

ACC Dodds added: “I would like to thank the professionalism of our officers and staff who worked alongside both clubs to make sure this was another safe game for all.

“Unfortunately, the actions of that small number of fans did cause a delay to the away coaches leaving the ground, but I’m pleased that no one was seriously injured and the coaches left the city safely.”

A spokesperson for the force said: “Investigators will now review all available footage, including from body-worn cameras, video filmed by our evidence gathering teams, CCTV and drones to identify those involved.



“An investigation is now underway into these incidents.”

Sports.title: Anfield hit fever pitch in outpouring of anger with chants & banners.. but ruthless Man City left Kop choking on insults
Sports.content:
Next

IT WAS the day Anfield was going to speak.

Not, this time, just for Liverpool. But for many, many others.



With the Oasis-inspired banners that spelt out accusation after accusation. The jeers and boos. The raucous blasts of “cheats”.

A visceral, guttural, raucous, fever-pitched outpouring of righteous pre-match anger and disdain.



We got it, too. But all for nothing, to no avail.

For this turned into the day that City spoke, even louder, sending a message that nobody could ignore.

Winning at a canter, after stunning finishes from Erling Haaland, Jeremy Doku and Rayan Cherki, to leave the Kop choking on its insults, feeding off the emotion to show cold, hard ruthlessness.

With Enzo Maresca wreathed in smiles as he encouraged the travelling fans to keep waving their inflatable bananas.



His players beaming, arms raised, triumphant, sticking two fingers up to all those who would see them humbled.

A sixth straight Prem win, seven on the spin in all competitions, showing that, no matter what is thrown at them, on or off the pitch, this City dressing room plans to carry on regardless.

SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

Signalling that, whether rival fans like it or not, until the entire disciplinary process comes to an end, football will simply have to get used to it.

Those smiles, that sense of resolve, exhibited the same joy as Haaland’s dad Alf-Inge did in the middle of the City fans after his son’s superb opener.

And if City do not break after all that has been flung their way over recent days, you wonder if anything other than the authorities will be able to stop them.



After all, Anfield away, in the wake of the damning conclusions of the independent commission that weighed its verdict for almost two years, should surely have been the one venue where City would stumble and fall.

Walking into a maelstrom inside, even if the backdoor route allowed them to dodge the screams, bedlam and pyro billowing out red smoke on their way to the stadium.

On the back of all that has been hurled at them, that fury and indignation. With the threat of unprecedented punishments hanging like the gallows rope.

Instead, they laughed, quite literally, in the face of it all.

Weathering the early storm – whether reverberating out of the stands or from Andoni Iraola’s side.



Ignoring all the noise, those banners that turned the Gallagher brothers’ lyrics against the club they love.



Producing, once again, a masterclass, pouncing like a lion on a stricken wildebeest once Ryan Gravenberch’s second yellow in 15 minutes saw Liverpool reduced to 10 men, spitting out the bones once they had devoured the meat.

It does not bother them, it seems, what the rest of football thinks.

That Jamie Carragher, calling again for City’s Abu Dhabi ownership to be stripped of the club, insisted: “It wasn’t 11 v 11. The difference was they had 18 to 20 top players.

“They wouldn’t have won as many trophies as they did because they wouldn’t have had that quality of player.”

Or that Roy Keane claimed: “You want to win it honestly, no cheating.



“If I was a player at United and these stories had come out I’d be disgusted at any dodgy dealings going on or somebody cooking the books.

“We point fingers at other leagues. And when it happens in the English league, there has to be punishment.”



That, unless City win their appeal – or successfully overturn the verdict at a subsequent legal tribunal – is for the future.

Yesterday was about the here and now, the outpouring of vitriol that washed over City like water off a duck’s back.

There was plenty of it, too. Aside from the catcalls and jeers, the banner with Pep Guardiola, Haaland and Co dressed up in prison uniforms, under the message “114 charges – guilty”.

But the City fans have adopted the same attitude of defiance.



They might been greeted by a banner declaring “we won the lot without cheating” as they came off the M62, but outside, waving their inflatable bananas – a throwback to the Imre Varadi-inspired craze of the 90s – it was song -time.

To the tune of “Love really hurts without you”, they sang: “Khaldoon, City’s in love with you” and adding: “We’re not a****, that we’ve been charged!”

Khaldoon Al Mubarak was not spotted, although chief exec Ferran Soriano led the City delegation. For the fans, it was about a show of unity, against everything they knew was coming.

As the City players emerged, led by Ruben Dias, for their pre-match warm-ups, there was no filter from the brutal bellow.



All around, too, the banners, Oasis lyrics twisted and turned into accusations and predictions – “All of your stars, are fading away” and “And after all, you really robbed us all” – and, of course, on repeat, “you cheating b, we know what you are”.

Then as the two teams walked out, a wall of pure unrelenting indignant sound, reverberating and cascading around, Dias laying down the law to his men in the huddle after the City fans had booed the Prem anthem.



Once the game began, every Liverpool tackle brought a roar, Anfield a bearpit, chants of “going down” filling the void when the game settled after a frantic, frenzied but ultimately incident-free opening half.

But these City players are made of sterner stuff, even if this is likely to be just the first time they face a chorus of disapproval.

Once Graveberch walked, City turned up their own heat. Comprehensive and convincing. Simply too good.

None of them can expect to win a popularity contest outside the M11 postcode.

But, like the fans, they are used to turning their backs on things. And getting on with “business as usual”.

Sports.title: Matthias Jaissle tells Besiktas to forget about signing reborn Newcastle star ahead of Coventry clash
Sports.content:

BESIKTAS have been told to forget all about Joe Willock.

The Turkish club’s president Serdal Adali recently vowed to sign the Newcastle star in January after claiming he had just missed out on the 27-year-old this summer.



The ex-Arsenal midfielder’s Toon future looked over as he entered the final 12 months of his contract having barely featured under Eddie Howe last term.

Besiktas made him their top transfer target, with Adali claiming he “brought Willock’s whole family to Istanbul” and they “even picked out a house” ahead of a move.



But new Newcastle boss Matthias Jaissle quickly became a huge fan of the ace himself, and under his instruction, the Mags rejected a £17m offer.

Having been reassured by the German head coach that he was a big part of his Toon plans, Willock has responded in style to Jaissle’s show of faith.

Newcastle’s top scorer heads to Coventry on Monday looking to add to his three-goal haul.

And his manager does not believe the fresh chat from Besiktas will have any impact on his new talisman.

Responding to Adali’s latest comments, Jaissle said: “Yeah, I hear that every day. I think he’s talking about it also every day!

“It’s our player. We’re really happy with him, and I think you see that also on the pitch. He’s a top, top player; he can deliver unbelievable performances, and I see even more potential with him, so we are happy that he’s here.”



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

Jaissle knows that Willock’s future remains up in the air unless a new extension can be agreed. But he would love to see the Mags get it sorted as quickly as possible.

He said: “Yeah, you can definitely imagine that, with how highly I’m talking about him, so there’s not the worry from our side.”

Jaissle, meanwhile, cannot wait to pit his wits against “pure legend” Frank Lampard.

The ex-Chelsea and England midfielder’s Coventry side’s confidence is sky high having secured their first victory since promotion to the Premier League last time out at Nottingham Forest.



Jaissle, 38, revealed Lampard was a player he aspired to be while he was coming through the ranks himself in Germany but joked his lack of ability never provided the opportunity for them to meet on the pitch.

And even though he has been impressed by Coventry, he hopes it will be him who leaves the Coventry Building Society Arena smiling.

He added: “Unfortunately no, I was not playing against him. That’s due to my missed qualities.

“A pure legend, what he delivered as a player, unbelievable, also for the national team. So someone you of course always looked up to as a player.

Sports.title: Dead man walking Michael Carrick looks grey & tired as Man Utd flatline… but almost every player is letting boss down
Sports.content:
Next

MICHAEL CARRICK had a face like thunder when he marched into the press conference room at Old Trafford on Saturday night.

His stride was not quite that of a dead man walking.



But the majority of Manchester United supporters who trudged out the ground after seeing ten-man Tottenham grab an injury-time equaliser know this team is flatlining.

Carrick, 45, was tanned and relaxed when he took over in January, having holidayed in Barbados over Christmas and New Year. Now he is frayed and grey.



It happens to them all.

The seasons have changed and the Manchester climate has left United’s under-the-cosh coaches with a particularly careworn appearance.

We all know how this is going to end.

It is a case of when, not if, Carrick leaves and the head coach has ample self-awareness to brace himself for the inevitable.

This is not a knee-jerk. The Red Devils drew 1-1 with the bottom side at kick-off for the second match running — after being held 1-1 at Fulham last month — and they were the inferior side.

That was despite leading 1-0 through Bryan Mbeumo and Spurs having Rodrigo Bentancur sent off for a headbutt on Luke Shaw after 78 minutes.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

Dominic Solanke’s late, late equaliser was the least the visitors deserved.

Carrick stated on the eve of the fixture United had to show more “fire”.

He is the club’s least fiery manager since Dave Sexton, so it did not sound like the rallying cry it looked like in black and white.



It was no surprise then when they failed to show intensity against Spurs.

Yet Carrick said: “No, I don’t think it was that. It looks like that in the end and I understand why you say that.

“We don’t want to start games like that, no one wants to start games like that.

“It was challenging for the players, but they worked through it and got themselves in a good position, which is the most disappointing thing — not seeing the game out.”

United have not recovered from the opening weekend farce at newly-promoted Hull, a 2-0 defeat that had Carrick’s fingerprints all over it.



He went past the point of no return with the League Cup collapse against Brighton.

For a distinguished midfielder, Carrick has failed to settle on a suitable starting duo in the middle of the park.

Andrey Santos, billed as a “dream” by Carrick in pre-season, has not started since that Hull horror show.



Youri Tielemans, an opportunistic purchase from Aston Villa after a deal for Ederson collapsed, looks older than his 29 years.

United cannot say they were not warned after Tielemans confessed his body “switched off” during the World Cup.

The team’s start has been so pitiful they are almost pining for the overrated Casemiro, a 34-year-old with his feet up in the MLS retirement home in Miami. To absolutely no surprise, his heir, Carlos Baleba, sparked a brief improvement in the second half against Robert De Zerbi’s Spurs.

Santos, a £50m Chelsea benchwarmer, never looked smart business and that is not on Carrick. Director of football Jason Wilcox appears out of his depth and he settled with the easy decision of up- grading Carrick’s job title.

It was an understandable call but better coaches were available.



United had momentum after last term’s third-place finish but it was convenient for them to settle with the compliant caretaker.

As underwhelming as United’s restrained transfer window was, they ended it with a stronger squad than the one they finished with last term.

The buck stops with the manager but almost every player is letting Carrick down.



Keeper Senne Lammens is wilting, Harry Maguire looks leaden, Kobbie Mainoo is dawdling and Bruno Fernandes is regressing to the desperate depths of Ralf Rangnick’s five months as an interim.

It is not Carrick’s style to pass the buck and he stressed: “No, I don’t feel let down. Because you can make mistakes and things go against you.

“I’ve made mistakes in games — but I don’t feel let down by them for making a mistake.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“We’ve just got to all help each other be better, and it’s on me to help them and guide them through it.”

Striding as purposefully as Carrick would be a start. But it feels too late.

Sports.title: ‘This is really bad for the Premier League’ – Man Utd icon Gary Neville fears for football as City batter Liverpool
Sports.content:
Next

GARY NEVILLE has warned Manchester City’s ongoing guilty verdict is “really bad for the Premier League” following their stunning win over Liverpool.

The former Manchester United defender admitted he struggled to praise City’s performance without thinking about the uncertainty surrounding the club’s future.



Enzo Maresca’s side thrashed Liverpool 3-0 at Anfield to maintain their perfect start to the Premier League season.

Erling Haaland, Jeremy Doku and Rayan Cherki were all on target after Ryan Gravenberch was sent off in the second half.



But City’s impressive victory came against a dramatic backdrop, after the Etihad club were found guilty of more than 100 breaches of the Prem’s financial rules during a nine-season period.

The club have appealed the decision and are awaiting the outcome, with potentially severe punishments hanging over the club.

And Neville believes the uncertainty is casting a huge shadow over English football.

Speaking on Sky Sports, he said: “To come and win at Anfield is really difficult and we should be eulogising over them without a but or any hesitation.

“But there is that thing in the back of your mind that they’ve done a brilliant job here today.

“They’ve obviously dominated the game in the last 20 minutes from the red card onwards. They’ve dug in.”



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

However, Neville’s biggest concern was what could happen if the guilty verdict is upheld in the coming months.

He added: “If these guilty verdicts obviously are confirmed in January, February, that Manchester City are not going to be in the position that they’re in and there’s going to be a huge cloud hanging over the whole league.

“And this is not good for the Premier League right now. That’s what I’ve just recognised today.

“This is really bad for the Premier League and it’s going to continue for a few months.”

City were greeted by a hostile Anfield crowd, with Liverpool supporters displaying banners and chanting about the financial scandal.



But the controversy failed to distract Maresca’s men, who secured their sixth consecutive league victory to move three points clear at the top of the table.

Sports.title: Gary Neville picks out brutal Man City chant which will 'catch on' around Premier League grounds
Sports.content:
Gary Neville picks out brutal Man City chant which will 'catch on' around Premier League grounds

Manchester City rose above the noise to beat Liverpool 3-0 and maintain their unbeaten start to the Premier League season - but Gary Neville had a message for Enzo Maresca’s side

View 3 Images Gary Neville (Image: (James Gill - Danehouse/Getty Images))

Gary Neville has told Manchester City’s players that they will continue to face chants of “cheats”. And the former England international also believes a “huge cloud” will hang over the Premier League for months to come.

‌



‌



Enzo Maresca’s side were berated with chants of "cheats" as they returned to action for the first time against Liverpool since they were found guilty of more than 100 breaches of the Premier League’s financial rules during a nine-season period.

‌



Ryan Gravenberch’s dismissal for two bookings just after the hour changed the course of the game as City scored three times through Erling Haaland, Jeremy Doku and Rayan Cherki to maintain their unbeaten start to the season. But as those on the Kop chanted “cheats” as the game entered its final few minutes, and Neville, speaking on Sky’s commentary, said: "That is brutal. The players out there are being called cheats.

‌



“That's one of the worst things you can be called. That one could catch on across the grounds and across the country until the punishment does come in.”

“To come and win at Anfield is really difficult. We should be eulogising over them without a ‘but’ or any hesitation. But there is that thing in the back in your mind, they’ve done a brilliant job here today, they’ve obviously dominated the game in the last 20 minutes, from the red card onwards.

“They’ve dug in, players like (Gianluigi) Donnarumma, (Ruben) Dias, (Elliot) Anderson, in that first half were excellent and stood strong as a group, senior players.

“This is not good for the Premier League right now, that’s what I’ve just recognised today – this is really bad for the Premier League. And it’s going to continue for a few months.”

City deny any wrongdoing and forward Haaland said post-match: "Every single person part of Man City, and every fan, this is a lovely moment that will stay with us for a long time. It was tough, it was hard but we showed amazing character from back to front. So proud of everyone.

"It's always tough to come here, if you look at the record it's tough. With the Pep and Klopp era it was tough for both teams, always has been.

“Important to stay strong mentally, stick together and do what you can do something about and the thing we can do something about is to play good football and fight together. That's the only thing we can do."

While team-mate Elliot Anderson hailed his side’s courage, saying: “I think we’ve shown real togetherness and fight. It’s a tough place to come and it’s challenging and we really stuck together out there, fought for each other and played well as well. I think we’ve shown courage here."

Manchester City's victory over Liverpool in the Premier League forced Gary Neville into making a clear Sky Sports request

City fans fill Anfield away end with bananas

Gary Neville has told Sky Sports to take him off Manchester City games until the outcome of their appeal against breaching Premier League financial rules is known. Neville was on co-commentary for City's win against Liverpool at Anfield and found it difficult to dish out praise as the points may end up meaning nothing.

‌



‌



In a hostile atmosphere, City delivered a professional display and quitened the home crowd before taking immediate advantage of Ryan Gravenberch's red card card midway through the first half.

‌



Erling Haaland, Jeremy Doku and Rayan Cherki all found the back of the net in a blistering 13 minutes from Enzo Maresca's side. Despite winning in some style, it was Elliot Anderson that left Neville impressed.

‌



Man City players booed off at Anfield

However, he had refrained from issuing huge praise due to the ongoing financial charges case which later saw him make quite the request to Sky Sports.

He said on Sky Sports: "This is the first Manchester City game that I have done today since the charges or guilty verdicts were handed out a few weeks ago.

‌



"We were just doing the podcast then and said if you could take me off Manchester City games moving forward for the next few months until the verdicts have been heard, I would be absolutely delighted.

"To come and win at Anfield is really difficult, we should be eulogising over them without a but or any hesitation, but there is that thing in the back of your mind.

"At the end of the game it is quite hard because you are imagining basically if these guilty verdicts are confirmed in January or February then Manchester City are not going to be in the position they are in and there is going to be a huge cloud hanging over the whole league, which is not good for the Premier League right now and that is what I have just recognised today. Really bad for the Premier League and it is going to continue for a few months."

The appeals process has already been initiated, though it could be a considerable period before a definitive conclusion is reached. The sanctions hearing is also ongoing, with their potential penalty likely to be revealed first.

Neville said: "That's the problem for the Man City staff, players and supporters, they are blameless in all of this. The stain, stigma, reputational damage that hits them, it's nothing to do with them but they have to face it on the pitch, in the stadium, week after week."

Sports.title: Andoni Iraola slams Ryan Gravenberch red card decision and bemoans Man City 'uncertainty'
Sports.content:
Andoni Iraola slams Ryan Gravenberch red card decision and bemoans Man City 'uncertainty'

Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola insists Ryan Gravenberch should not have been booked for his first yellow card and had his say on the ongoing Manchester City situation

Iraola speaks after Man City beat Liverpool 3-0

Andoni Iraola insisted Ryan Gravenberch should never have been sent off - and then insisted “uncertainty is not good for anyone.”

‌



‌



Liverpool boss Iraola claimed the whole game changed after Gravenberch’s second yellow card for a pull back on Jeremy Doku soon after he was booked for a foul on Elliot Anderson.

‌



Gravenberch got his marching orders when the score was goalless but then Manchester City ran away with it after goals from Erling Haaland, Jeremy Doku and Rayan Cherki.

‌



Iraola said: “I think the analysis is quite clear, no? I think we played two different games: one until the red card, and one from the red card until the end.

“I think the first foul of Ryan is never a yellow card, never. These kinds of games, just a stomp on the big toe, or something minor. He doesn't even call the foul straight away. He leaves it, I think Andersen does a couple of steps then decides to go down.

Sports.title: Jamie Carragher and Gary Neville agree on Ryan Gravenberch Liverpool red card vs Man City
Sports.content:
Jamie Carragher and Gary Neville agree on Ryan Gravenberch Liverpool red card vs Man City

Ryan Gravenberch was controversially sent off in the Premier League clash between Manchester City and Liverpool

Man City depicted as cheats outside of Anfield

Jamie Carragher and Gary Neville were in agreement that it was harsh for Ryan Gravenberch to be sent off for two yellow card offences. During the second half of Liverpool's Premier League clash against Manchester City, he was penalised with two cautions for a late tackle on Elliot Anderson and pull-back on Jeremy Doku

‌



‌



However, Carragher and Neville were both not convinced that he should have been dismissed. The former said on Sky Sports: "It feels really harsh when you think of the two challenges. The first challenge was not a card and the referee was far too quick to get the card out."

‌



"The first was the same, the referee was so quick to get a yellow out. Neville then added: "That is very, very soft." Gravenberch was quite clearly upset as he trudged off the pitch with Andoni Iraola swiftly readying Trey Nyoni to come in and fill the midfield void.

‌



Before he could actually be introduced, though, Erling Haaland put City into the lead within three minutes of the red card. Doku then fired in a superb second for the visitors with the Belgian ultimately changing the game in his side's favour after replacing Iliman Ndiaye in the 56th minute.

Prior to Gravenberch's dismissal, he was one of many that forced Gianluigi Donnarumma into a strong save with Lewis Koumas and Alexis Mac Allister also going close.

Two goals down and at a man disadvantage, the game looked to have been decided in just six minutes but City later made absolute sure of the points.

In a move where every City star touched the ball, which included a clever flick from Josko Gvardiol and Rayan Cherki sitting down Jeremie Frimpong prior, the latter swept in a third under Alisson.

On the goal, Carragher said: "Well we can talk about Manchester City, players that they've brought in, the money that they've spent, when they have spent money, whether its legal or not, they've bought good players. He [Cherki] is one of them.

‌

"Absolute quality since he come into the squad, what a goal that is. The less said about Frimpong the better, he is all over the place, wow."

The victory maintains City's winning start to the season but any points from now are under a cloud following their guilty verdict for 114 financial charges, as pointed out by Neville.

City continue to protest their innocence and have appealed against the outcome reached by the independent panel.

Gianluigi Donnarumma and his goalkeeping understudy Geronimo Rulli had got a taste of things to come, when running out warm up to loud boos and geers.

The focus of attention was inside the ground closer to kick off. But outside Anfield, Scouse vendors had seized the chance to profit from City's downfall.

Roy Keane has given a particularly forthright response to Manchester City’s charges ahead of their clash with Liverpool at Anfield and sent a strong message to players of the Premier League side

View 2 Images Roy Keane has issued his verdict on Man City's guilty verdict (Image: Sky Sports)

Roy Keane has suggested he would be ‘disgusted’ if he was a Manchester City player following their landmark verdict. City were found guilty of 114 of the 115 charges put towards them by an independent commission.

‌



‌



The club has already submitted an appeal and that will be heard during a separate hearing. And while Keane has absolved the club’s stars of any blame, he has said that they should feel particularly let down by City’s behaviour during the period that they were charged for.

‌





‌



Speaking ahead of City’s trip to Liverpool on Sunday afternoon, he said: “This is nothing against the players or supporters, this is an ownership issue. If you’re going after the big prizes, we’ve been fortunate to pick one or two up. You want to do it honestly.

“You want to look back at your career and think we did everything. You win some games, you lose some games.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

“You can’t be looking back at what Man City have done and found guilty of, I know there’s an appeal. We’ve been sitting here and praising Man City and saying they’re amazing and bringing in amazing players. And Pep turning really good players into superstars.

“But the way they were doing it, that’s the issue, nothing on the players. If I was a player and there were stories about stuff we were doing at Manchester United, I’d be disgusted. I’d be disgusted if there were any dodgy dealings and anyone cooking the books

‌



"Some people think this is a bit strong, but I wouldn't feel like I've earned a league title if there was something dodgy going on in the background. Absolutely not.

View 2 Images Keane has suggested City's players should feel 'disgusted' (Image: Getty Images)

“We talk about lads going out and giving their all and picking up injuries but that is your job, that’s what you’re supposed to do when you’re giving it your all.

‌



"You just hope everyone is else is on the same page and being honest and everyone else is trying to do it the proper way.

“I hear a lot of ex-players saying that Man City players gave it their all, we know that. That’s not the issue. But they had unbelievable players on the bench to come on and make them stronger and get them over the line against teams like Liverpool who are pushing each other.

“That’s what top-level football is about, we had it with Arsenal. You hope there is honesty. That's where respect comes into the game

Article continues below

“We’re footballing people. It’s difficult for us to talk about legal stuff, we play the game because we love it and are passionate about it but you’ve got to also have a bit of honesty.”

Jonny Clayton claimed the Swiss Darts Trophy with an 8-4 victory over Luke Humphries in the final in Basel, Switzerland.

It marks Clayton's first European title of 2026, his first ranking title of the year and his fourth Euro Tour win overall.

The victory for Clayton also books the Welshman his spot at the Grand Slam of Darts in November.

Sports.title: Hits & Misses: Anderson and Wirtz offering opposite value for money
Sports.content:
Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player FREE TO WATCH: Highlights from Liverpool's match against Manchester City in the Premier League

Manchester City's siege mentality won out at Liverpool. Their quality with a man over telling, if not quite so obvious when both sides had a full complement of players for an hour of the game.

Absolutely everything good about City in their 3-0 win was summed up by the classy performance of Elliot Anderson.

Not for the first time since his mega-money move from Nottingham Forest, the midfielder's mastery on the ball was matched by his maturity off it. A "bargain" at £116m, according to Jamie Carragher, every bit capable, in his own way, of exerting as much control and influence on games as Rodri did in this role.

While the spotlight shines ever brighter on City as a club, and forensics pour over their spending, Anderson remains the picture of calm. Everything a manager would want in a modern-day holding midfielder: a robust runner, aggressive tackler and clever distributor. "He dominates big games," says Gary Neville.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Gary Neville says Elliot Andersen looks a real top performer and has quickly proven he is worth every penny that Manchester City have spent on him

Rarely fazed by the occasion, Anderson has won at Anfield two years running - with two different sides. Of course the way Forest went about success last term shared few similarities with City's more technical display. The only common denominator? Elliot Anderson.

Laura Hunter

Florian Wirtz played his part with the pressing and the constant movement that was a hallmark of Liverpool's up-tempo approach that made life so difficult for Manchester City for an hour at Anfield. But that bit of magic that the supporters wanted was missing.

Rayan Cherki provided that for City's third and final goal, by which point Wirtz was sat on the Liverpool bench having been substituted. Another big game in which the Germany international was unable to provide the spark for his side.

Wirtz's goals for Liverpool December 27th 2025 – Premier League – Wolves (h)

January 4th 2026 – Premier League – Fulham (a)

January 12th 2026 – FA Cup – Barnsley (h)

January 17th 2026 – Premier League – Burnley (h)

January 28th 2026 – Champions League – Qarabag (h)

January 31st 2026 – Premier League – Newcastle (h)

April 25th 2026 – Premier League – Crystal Palace (h)

Too many loose touches and loose passes, one or two tackles shirked. Victor Munoz and Lewis Koumas are easy for supporters to embrace with their bustling styles but Wirtz is a player who glides across the turf and he needs end product to justify his role.

Wirtz lost possession 17 times Florian Wirtz lost possession 17 times in Liverpool's 3-0 home defeat to Manchester City, more than any other player.

There was one shot lashed wide with the game goalless and better options to his left. It is no goals for Wirtz this season and just one in his last 16 Premier League appearances. Another opportunity missed for a classy player still seemingly unable to impose himself.

Adam Bate

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player FREE TO WATCH: Highlights from the Premier League match between Crystal Palace and Nottingham Forest

Crystal Palace have shown signs of rediscovering their attacking spark under Pierre Sage, with their 3-1 comeback win over Nottingham Forest the latest example.

The Eagles have now scored three or more goals in two of their last four league games - as often as they managed across their previous 37 Premier League matches combined.

Goals and entertaining football were a problem during Oliver Glasner's latter days in charge, as Palace struggled to balance their domestic and European commitments.

There is an early sense of a throwback to the more free-scoring side that flourished under the Austrian in his first season, when their pace, movement and attacking combinations made them a threat to anyone.

It is still early in Sage's tenure, and two high-scoring performances do not guarantee a lasting change. But Palace look to be playing with greater freedom and confidence, with Daichi Kamada, Jefferson Lerma and Yeremy Pino all finding the net against Forest.

If Sage can sustain that attacking momentum while tightening up a defence that has been vulnerable this season, there are encouraging signs of a more dangerous Palace taking shape.

William Bitibiri

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the Premier League match between Hull and Everton

Everton are unbeaten after six matches for just the third time in the Premier League era. In 2006/07 and 2013/14 they finished sixth and then fifth from this position.

It is a testament to the hard work of David Moyes, who has returned to challenging circumstances in his second Everton spell, that he has got the club back to looking upwards.

For the last five seasons, Everton have been in the bottom half, often battling relegation. Now, it seems, they have a genuine chance to push up the table and dare to dream bigger.

However, it is hard to see how Moyes can drag them into Europe with Thierno Barry as his only striker. The 23-year-old scored in the end in the 2-2 draw at Hull, but, according to Opta, he needed five big chances to find the back of the net. At least two of those had to go in.

If Everton are to qualify for Europe, they will need a striker who wins them points. At Hull, you could argue they had a striker who cost them points.

Barry, who is Everton's top scorer since the start of last season in the Premier League (11 goals), is improving all the time, but the current situation is unfair on him and his manager. Right now he cannot be depended on consistently.

The Frenchman, who has started all eight of Everton's matches this season, appeared to pull up with cramp towards the end at Hull and Moyes had no choice but to replace him with Charly Alcaraz, who is a midfielder by trade.

There was only four minutes plus stoppage time to go, but it almost felt as if Everton were forced to give up on chasing a late winner. This was a match that was there for the taking.

The plan, of course, was to have Folarin Balogun in the squad. However, his move from Monaco collapsed at the last minute on Deadline Day.

The obvious solution would be to go back in for a striker in January. It remains to be seen how the uncertainty at ownership level will impact their plans. Moyes needs - and deserves - another striker to have a proper chance at a push for Europe.

Zinny Boswell

Mohamed Belloumi is making the difference for Hull City - even when he is tired.

The Algeria winger was benched for the first time this season against Everton after telling head coach Sergej Jakirovic on Friday that he was fatigued after playing three times for his country during the international break.

Belloumi still made a crucial impact on Sunday, netting Hull's equaliser to earn them a point. He has been pivotal in the club's good start, scoring or assisting five of their eight Premier League goals this season.

The 24-year-old was signed from Portuguese side Farense in August 2024 and scored only five goals in 35 Championship appearances over two seasons, but, at a higher level, his pace and fearless dribbling has made a significant contribution already.

Belloumi will return to being the first name on their teamsheet at Fulham next weekend and, if his early-season form is anything to go by, defences will have plenty more to worry about.

David Richardson

Sports.title: How Antonelli could win F1 world title as soon as the next race
Sports.content:
Kimi Antonelli could become Formula 1's youngest world champion as early as the next race - the United States Grand Prix - on October 25.

Mercedes' Antonelli increased his lead at the top of the Drivers' Championship to a season-high 102 points with a third-place finish in the Singapore Grand Prix.

George Russell remains second in the standings but a ninth-place finish after engine penalties had left him starting at the back of the grid dropped him beyond a century of points behind his team-mate for the first time, while Lewis Hamilton's late slide off the podium leaves the Ferrari driver 111 points off the pace in third place.

With such a large lead and with a scheduled six races left in the 2026 season, the world title now looks a formality for the 20-year-old Italian in just his second year of F1 to usurp Sebastian Vettel as the sport's youngest title winner.

A first chance - albeit an outside one - to clinch the crown will arrive as soon as the next race at Austin's Circuit of the Americas, live on Sky Sports F1…

Image: How it stands after the Singapore Grand Prix

How Antonelli could win the title at the United States GP

There will be five scheduled races left - Mexico, Brazil, Las Vegas, Qatar and Abu Dhabi - after the United States Grand Prix takes place on Sunday October 25 and a maximum of 125 points left to play for.

To win the title in Austin, Antonelli needs to increase his championship lead by 23 points. For that to happen he must win the grand prix AND then hope both Russell and Hamilton do not score sufficient points to stay within 124 points of him going to Mexico.

The permutations for Antonelli to become champion in Austin are:

Antonelli wins the race (25 points)

and

Russell finishes ninth or lower (2 points or less)

and

Hamilton finishes fifth or lower (10 points or less)

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player George Russell takes over from Antonelli's engineer during the Sprint rain delay in Singapore

Were Antonelli to win the race and Russell finish ninth, Antonelli would hold a 125-point lead over his team-mate with exactly 125 points left to play for. But that would still be enough for Antonelli to become champion, provided Hamilton was also still outside the top four in the race.

That is because victory in Austin would be the the Italian's ninth of the year and with Russell on three wins the Briton would only be able to get to a maximum of eight in the five races left. Antonelli would therefore be guaranteed the title on results countback, with race wins the first tiebreaker in event of an end-of-season points tie.

What about the other drivers still in mathematical contention?

Max Verstappen (119 points back), Charles Leclerc (125 points back) and Lando Norris (139 points back) all remain in mathematical title contention too after Singapore but would all be automatically knocked out by an Antonelli win in Austin wherever they finished that race.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Toto Wolff hits back at accusations that Mercedes favour Antonelli over Russell

'If I don't do my job well, then the result won't come' - Antonelli vows to stay focused

Antonelli is now within touching distance of an incredible historic achievement but stressed after Singapore that he cannot afford to let that fact distract him from his performance in Austin.

"I know it's very close, I know it's there, but I just need to make sure that I keep doing the best I can," he said.

"You know, the mindset is always the same, to go out there and win and perform the best way I can. I think this weekend [in Singapore] I haven't particularly driven that well. I felt like I could have done a better job, but I feel confident that, you know, a week to reset and I'm really looking forward to being back in Austin.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the 2026 Singapore Grand Prix

"But, at the end of the day, if I don't do my job well, then the result won't come. So in order to achieve what I want, I need to perform, as simple as that."

Sports.title: Man City defiant and top of the table - but Anfield delivers its own verdict
Sports.content:
The chant from The Kop went up early. "You haven't won a trophy since 1976." It was a reference to Manchester City's League Cup triumph, the last major honour that the club picked up prior to the period of ownership that now finds itself under such scrutiny.

As it is, City remain top of the table having won six games from six. But this victory will not quieten the noise. They departed to boos and the accusations of cheating that were a feature of the day.

Liverpool, three times runners-up to Manchester City in 2014, 2019 and 2022, made for perfect but hostile hosts, with the Anfield crowd perhaps the ideal outlet for the emotions, a proxy for supporters everywhere. It was an atmosphere like no other.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Man City arrive at Anfield ahead of their Premier League match against Liverpool - their first since being found guilty of all charges related to serious breaches of Premier League financial rules by an independent commission

The enterprising flag and scarf sellers in Liverpool were certainly prepared, with an unusual emphasis on the visitors, this being City's first game since an independent commission judged that they broke Premier League rules between 2009 and 2018.

City are appealing that verdict and continue to deny any wrongdoing.

But the court of opinion is making its voice heard too. Anfield has made up its mind. The banners referred to "a generation of supporters cheated" and a playful take on Wonderwall with the amended line that "you really robbed us all".

Even the choice of songs over the public-address system appeared to be pointed. Before kick-off at Anfield, we had Blame by Calvin Harris and a blast of The Joker and the Thief by Wolfmother. Upon the final whistle, it was Little Lies by Fleetwood Mac.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Roy Keane shares his thoughts on Manchester City following the club being found guilty of all charges related to serious breaches of Premier League financial rules by an independent commission

As expected, City's supporters opted for defiance in the face of the criticism. The boos for the Premier League anthem are nothing new but carried extra resonance. The banner declaring that 'In Khaldoon we trust' an eye-opening indication of the devotion of some.

Others preferred to shift the focus from their current predicament. There was more than a hint of nostalgia in a nod to the fact that there is far more to their club than how their rivals perceive them. Poznan dances and inflatable bananas served as a symbol of that.

The latter custom, one that dates back to Imre Varadi - 'Imre Banana' to the fans in the late '80s - is a reminder that City were always really here. This remains a proud club. The message being sent is that the downs are part of their story just as much as the ups.

Image: Man City fans wave inflatable bananas during their win over Liverpool at Anfield

But the overriding emotions inside the stadium belonged to the majority, those wearing Liverpool red, and the reality is that City and these charges are part of their story too. Anyone allowing the mind to wander at Anfield on Sunday could not escape that history.

Glance down to the spot on the turf where Steven Gerrard slipped to let in Demba Ba in 2014. Liverpool lost that game to Chelsea but lost that title to City. How can this ruling not change the tone and temperature of that regret? Sadness is now tinged with anger.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Micah Richards says he is devastated and confused by Manchester City's guilty ruling and claims that, as a player during the period in question, his integrity is being questioned

And so, for Liverpool, this is not only about City's trophies not being 'real' but those phantom triumphs of their own. "Until you've repaid the dreams you bought for your lies you'll be castaway alone under stormy skies." A banner in the Sir Kenny Dalglish Stand.

This game itself was a reminder that these matters are ongoing. The charges are historic but the consequences are part of the present.

A strange afternoon had a strange ending too - The Kop chanted 'going down' while the league table shows that City are top.

"That is the backdrop to not knowing where these points and this season is going," rued Gary Neville on commentary. "There is going to be a 'but' all the way."

Resolution cannot come soon enough.

Sports.title: 'Barely a foul' - Carra criticises 'shocking' Gravenberch red card decision
Sports.content:
Ryan Gravenberch's sending off in Liverpool's 3-0 home defeat to Manchester City was a "shocking decision" by referee Chris Kavanagh, according to Sky Sports pundit Jamie Carragher.

Gravenberch, the standout player for an hour, was shown red after receiving a second yellow for a challenge on Jeremy Doku with the game tied at 0-0 in a flashpoint that turned the game, which had been finely poised, in City's favour.

Erling Haaland's opener came just two minutes and 37 seconds after Gravenberch was dismissed, and within six minutes Doku had doubled City's advantage before Rayan Cherki added a third with 12 minutes to play.

Gravenberch had picked up his first caution shortly after the restart for a foul on City midfielder Elliot Anderson, which Sky Sports pundit Carragher described as a "nothing challenge".

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player FREE TO WATCH: Highlights from Liverpool’s match against Manchester City in the Premier League.

"It's such a poor decision by the referee," Carragher said after the game. "The thing that frustrates me is that he wasn't going to give a yellow card. He only gives it when he thinks Anderson is hurt.

"That has nothing to do with whether a foul should or should not be a yellow card."

He added: "It's barely a foul. It's a shocking decision."

"It feels really harsh when you think of the two challenges," Carragher said of Gravenberch's sending off on co-commentary.

"The first one was not a yellow card. It was so harsh for a nothing challenge on Anderson, and the referee was far too quick to get the yellow card out."

Sky Sports' Gary Neville, also on co-commentary, said Gravenberch's second yellow was "very soft", before adding: "The only thing I would say is, knowing you're on a yellow and wrong side of Doku, does he need to make the challenge?

"He's given the referee a dilemma."

'Liverpool looked like they had four sent off'

Manchester City had an xG of 0.16 before Gravenberch's sending off but dominated once Liverpool were down to 10 men.

Sky Sports pundit Roy Keane felt Gravenberch's dissmissal turned the match in City's favour but criticised Liverpool's response to the red card.

"I don't see how he can get a yellow card for that," Keane said of Gravenberch's first booking. "The whole game then changes.

"Liverpool struggled with the physicality. There were spaces everywhere. Liverpool looked like they had four men sent off. City were controlling it. For the first hour it was a tight game."

Daniel Sturridge was in full agreement and said the decision to award Gravenberch's first yellow card was "a joke".

"The game changed on the red card. We have to be truthful about that," Sturridge said on Sky Sports. "City delivered after the red card changed the game. Prior to that, it was very even."

Sky Sports' Micah Richards was equally puzzled about the first booking the Liverpool midfielder received. "That is soft. How is that a yellow card? I don't understand," said Richards.

Sports.title: Greaves ends Women's Series season with record-breaking win
Sports.content:
Beau Greaves ended her 2026 PDC Women's Series season with a record-breaking streak of victories on the way to two tournament wins at Event 23 and 24 in Wigan.

Greaves - who had already claimed back-to-back titles in Event 21 and 22 on Saturday - averaged 98.75 on the way to her third successive competition title at Event 23, marking the highest event-winning average in the history of the Women's Series.

The Yorkshire native - who has won 17 out of a possible 24 Women's Series events this year - won all of her first four matches by a 4-0 scoreline, posting a stunning 103.66 average in her victory against Steph Clark.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Chris Murphy suggests Beau Greaves should be given more opportunities to play against the men after she once again won the Women's World Matchplay.

She lost her first legs of the day in her 5-2 victory against Gemma Hayter in the quarter-finals, before beating Fallon Sherrock - who confirmed her own return to the World Darts Championship on Saturday - in the semi-final.

Her 5-3 victory against Jade Gofford in the final confirmed her first title of the day, before beating Laura van den Berg, Sara Walton, Vicky Martin and Lauren Bloomfield to reach the quarter-finals of event 24.

Image: Sherrock and Greaves will both compete at Alexandra Palace

Wins against Kirsty Hutchinson and 20-year-old Italian Aurora Fochesato confirmed her second title of the day and her fourth of the weekend to cap off a successful 2026 season.

"I felt good," Greaves said. "I was chuffed with the first competition. I had some good averages and then I played steady enough in the second event.

"I knew I hadn't been playing at my best recently, but I've had some good moments today and I'm ready to build on it and take this into the back end of the year."

The Wigan double-header also saw Vicky Pruim claim the final spot on offer to compete in the World Darts Championship through the Women's Series rankings, joining Greaves, Sherrock, Hayter and Lisa Ashton.
