In spite of that, Babb's memories of the tournament are largely positive.

"I enjoyed it, I have to admit! I'd rather play in the searing heat than a wet Tuesday night in Hull," he says.

"I was a fit lad and it was quite easy for me playing alongside Paul McGrath, who was imperious in that tournament. I learned a lot from him and how he conserved his energy.

"I felt I got stronger because I got used to it. I guess our 0-0 draw against Norway would probably attest to the heat and the style of play.

"It all comes down to the individual. Footballers are supreme athletes now and they leave nothing to chance, so I think they'll cope a lot better than we did in the mid-90s."

The methods may have moved on since Charlton was throwing water onto the pitch, but Babb's memories from USA '94 provide a reminder this World Cup will be a battle against more than just the opposition.

Sports.title: The £13,128 ticket: Tyson Fury vs Anthony Joshua is sport's most expensive standard seat EVER as fans complain they are half a million places back in online queues
Sports.content:
The £13,128 ticket: Tyson Fury vs Anthony Joshua is sport's most expensive standard seat EVER as fans complain they are half a million places back in online queues

Tyson Fury vs Anthony Joshua tickets have reached £13,128 at the top end of the scale, as more than half a million fans joined an online queue for one of the most eagerly anticipated fights in boxing history.

The most expensive seats for the December 11 showdown in Cardiff cost more than those for some of the world's biggest sporting events, eclipsing the top face-value price of £6,300 for the 2026 Super Bowl and World Cup ticket prices of £8,333.

Tickets for Fury vs Joshua went on sale at midday on Friday, with Saudi Arabia's Turki Alalshikh keen to ensure fans had an accessible entry point, reflected in the starting price of £88.50 including fees.

The top-tier tickets, priced at £13,128, sold out within just 45 minutes, underlining the extraordinary demand for the December 11 showdown.

The figures do not include VIP packages, hotel and travel packages, group bookings or concession prices, and all tickets remain subject to availability.

Demand for the fight was immediately apparent, with more than half a million people waiting in the online queue as fans raced to secure seats for the long-awaited clash.

Tyson Fury vs Anthony Joshua tickets have been priced from £88.50 to a staggering £13,128, as fans prepare to snap up seats for the long-awaited heavyweight showdown

Fury and Joshua's fight is due to take place on December 11 in Cardiff with the showdown set to begin at 1am so Netflix subscribers can stream it at peak time in America

The fight will take place at Cardiff's Principality Stadium on December 11, bringing an end to years of speculation over a meeting between the two former world heavyweight champions.

Fury and Joshua have been linked with a blockbuster contest for more than a decade, with negotiations repeatedly failing to produce the long-awaited clash.

Now, the British rivals are finally set to share a professional ring in a contest that could prove defining for both men's careers.

Fury, 38, returned to the ring in April after another retirement announcement, beating Arslanbek Makhmudov on points. The former WBC heavyweight champion has won 36 of his 39 professional contests, with two defeats and one draw.

Joshua, 36, won Olympic gold at London 2012 before becoming a two-time unified heavyweight world champion. He has recorded 30 victories, including 27 knockouts, alongside four defeats.

Joshua's most recent high-profile outing came in December 2025, when he stopped Jake Paul, before returning to the ring in July 2026 to defeat Kristian Prenga by second-round knockout.

The December showdown will give both men the chance to settle their long-running rivalry and claim a defining victory in front of a huge crowd.

The Principality Stadium can accommodate up to 80,000 spectators for major events, while Netflix is set to stream the contest globally.

The December showdown will give both men the chance to settle their long-running rivalry and claim a defining victory in front of a huge crowd

Fury against Joshua was almost the fight that got away, with the heavyweights now set to sort out differences that should have been settled a decade ago

Main-event ring walks are expected at approximately 1am local time on Saturday, December 12, although the final schedule remains subject to confirmation.

As for those in attendance, Turki Alalshikh had been keen to ensure there was an accessible entry point for fans, with tickets starting at £88.50 including fees.

At the top end of the scale, tickets cost a staggering £13,128, putting them among the most expensive publicly listed prices for a major boxing event.

The figure is not without precedent in a sport where premium seats can command eye-watering sums.

When Floyd Mayweather and Manny Pacquiao met in 2015, official tickets cost up to $10,000 (£6,700), while resale listings subsequently reached around £94,000 after the initial allocation sold out in less than a minute.

Meanwhile, a premium hospitality package for Mike Tyson's 2024 bout with Jake Paul was advertised at $2million (£1.57m) for 10 tickets and an exclusive ringside experience.

Some individual ringside seats were also listed on the secondary market at $50,000 (£39,000).

The highest-priced ticket previously listed for a British boxing event was a VIP ringside seat for Anthony Joshua's 2017 showdown with Wladimir Klitschko at Wembley, which was advertised for £202,400 on resale platform Viagogo.

However, that figure was an asking price rather than a confirmed sale. Around 90,000 fans attended the fight, which saw Joshua stop Klitschko in the 11th round.

Meanwhile, face-value prices for inner-ringside seats at Tyson Fury's 2022 fight against Dillian Whyte at Wembley reached £2,250.

Sports.title: Mike Tyson says he delivered letter to Trump from Diddy from behind bars in bombshell claim as he opens up on friendship with disgraced rapper
Sports.content:
Mike Tyson says he delivered letter to Trump from Diddy from behind bars in bombshell claim as he opens up on friendship with disgraced rapper

Boxing legend Mike Tyson revealed that he hand delivered a letter from his friend Sean 'Diddy' Combs to President Donald Trump in a recent meeting.

In an appearance on SiriusXM radio show 'Andy Cohen Live,' the former fighter spoke at length about his friendship with the disgraced music mogul who is serving a 50-month prison sentence for a sex-crimes conviction.

Tyson said he is 'friendly with Puff' – using one of Combs' many stage names – before Cohen asked him if the boxer was 'surprised by what happened with him?'

'Listen, I was surprised that they went through so many lengths to get him,' the athlete replied.

'They used a 110-year-old rule to get him – that case 110 years ago, but they used it to get him. Can you imagine that?'

After being convicted on this charge, Tyson said that he spoke with Combs from jail – where he asked 'Iron Mike' to deliver a message to the President.

Mike Tyson says he was asked to deliver a letter from Diddy to President Donald Trump

Diddy - born Sean Combs - wrote Trump a letter from jail asking the President for a pardon

'And did you give a letter to the president from him?' Cohen inquired, to which Tyson replied: 'I did what he told me to do, yeah.'

In January, President Trump confirmed that he received a letter from Combs asking for a pardon. Trump did not reveal how he received the letter, but said that he wouldn't grant the request.

The '110-year-old' rule Tyson referred to was the 1910 Mann Act, a law that criminalizes the transporting of 'any woman or girl for the purpose of prostitution or debauchery, or for any other immoral purpose.'

Combs faced accusations of leading a criminal enterprise where he allegedly coerced victims to participate in debaucherous sex parties – nicknamed 'freak offs' – which occasionally involved travel across state lines and international borders.

After a two month trial, Combs was acquitted of trafficking and racketeering, a jury cited the Mann Act when finding him guilty of two counts of transportation to engage in prostitution.

Combs has denied all allegations of sexual misconduct and has attempted to appeal his conviction.

He is currently being held at FCI Fort Dix in New Jersey and still faces upwards of 70 civil lawsuits throughout the country.

In January, Trump said he got a letter from Combs but said he wouldn't pardon him

Combs is serving 50 months in prison on two counts of transportation to engage in prostitution

Join the discussion Should celebrities be able to use their connections to seek pardons for serious crimes?

Combs' release date has moved multiple times since his incarceration due to his alleged misdeeds behind bars.

An NBC News report revealed it was pushed back from January 21, 2028 to March 2, 2028 after he allegedly made fellow inmates cook and clean for him, give him massages and received access to outside alcohol and a cellphone.

In an August 2025 interview, Trump addressed Combs' conviction in an interview with Newsmax.

'I was very friendly with him. I got along with him great,' the President said at the time.

'[He] seemed like a nice guy,' Trump continued. 'I didn't know him well, but when I ran for office he was very hostile.'

Sports.title: 'He's not a p***y President': Mike Tyson launches wild defense of Trump and says president has overcome problems only 'black' people face
Sports.content:
Donald Trump is 'not a p***y President,' according to his longtime friend and boxing legend Mike Tyson.

Speaking on the latest episode of Piers Morgan Uncensored, Tyson discussed his history with Trump, whom he first met as a young heavyweight in the 1980s as the future President was making a name for himself in New York and Atlantic City real estate.

'I voted for him,' the 60-year-old Tyson told Morgan. 'I ran the streets for him. You know, me getting votes… I'm very proud of him. He's somebody that everybody should be proud of.'

Tyson doesn't have many remaining personal ties to his early days in the ring. The boxing legend's famed trainer, Cus D'Amato, died in 1985, his turbulent marriage to actress Robin Givens ended four years later and Tyson's fragile business relationship with promoter Don King finally ruptured in the late 1990s.

But for all of the turnover surrounding Tyson, Trump has been a constant for the former heavyweight champion. Not only did Tyson fight at Trump's hotels and casinos, later adding the real estate mogul to his unofficial entourage, but the two remained friends throughout the ups and downs of their later lives.

And it's those obstacles that make Trump an admirable figure in the eyes of Tyson: 'Listen, if you didn't know who Donald Trump was and you didn't know his name, you would think he's Black.'

Speaking on the latest episode of Piers Morgan Uncensored, Mike Tyson discussed his history with President Trump, whom he first met as a young heavyweight in the 1980s

Trump and Tyson attend the Ultimate Fighting Championship (UFC) 287 in April of 2023

Donald Trump and Mike Tyson attend March of Dimes Gourmet Gala Benefit in 1989

According to Tyson, it's Trump's perseverance in the face of multiple bankruptcies and sexual misconduct allegations that have made him a formidable figure.

'When he went for President, he was bankrupt... He owed taxes, he owed so much money,' Tyson said, somewhat erroneously.

While Trump's businesses did declare bankruptcy six times, the last filing came in 2009, well before his successful 2016 White House run.

But it's not just the financial problems that give Trump credibility in Tyson's eyes. Tyson was also impressed with the way Trump survived multiple waves of sexual misconduct claims.

'All this sex abuse and all that stuff that he went through,' Tyson continued. 'People don't normally go that well. They normally have a nervous breakdown. He handled it. And that's why everyone has to respect him. Just from the way he handled his court procedures… I don't care if you hate his guts… you have to respect that. Just off the bat.'

Trump has never been convicted of any sexual misconduct, although in May of 2023, a federal jury found him liable in a civil trial for sexually abusing and defaming writer E. Jean Carroll. A later trial resulted in a federal jury ordering Trump to pay an additional $83.3 million on top of the initial $5 million penalty he was ordered to pay Carroll.

Previously, Trump supported Tyson in the face of sexual misconduct claims. When Tyson was convicted of rape in Indiana in 1992, the future President told NBC the boxer was 'railroaded in the case' and questioned the victim's story.

While heavyweight champ Mike Tyson steals a kiss from his wife Robin Givens (R), real estate developer Donald Trump and Givens' mother Ruth Roper (L), talk to the media in 1988

Tyson chats with an attorney during a court hearing aimed at ending his contract with manager Bill Cayton. Sitting with Tyson's wife Robin Givens and her mother Ruth is Donald Trump

Donald Trump, Mike Tyson and Fred Trump attend a press conference at the Plaza Hotel

Donald Trump, Mike Tyson and Don King attend Gourmet Gala Benefit for March of Dimes on November 21, 1989 at the Plaza Hotel. King and Tyson later broke their business ties

Trump went so far as to publicly suggest Tyson should be allowed to dodge prison by giving 'millions and millions' of dollars to the victim.

'What has happened to him, the conviction, is already punitive,' Trump told the New York Post in 1992. 'The victim has had the satisfaction of humbling him and being vindicated.'

Speaking with Morgan, Tyson did not address the support he received from Trump in 1992.

He did, however, discuss the assassination attempt Trump survived in Pennsylvania on the campaign trail in 2024 by explaining he is 'not a p**** President.'

As for his immediate future, Tyson's planned exhibition with Floyd Mayweather Jr. is currently on hold after the former heavyweight broke his hand in May. Another complicating factor is a lawsuit against Mayweather by the promoter, CSI Sports.

In his previous return to the ring in 2024, Tyson was easily defeated by cruiserweight Jake Paul, who scored a unanimous decision victory that was watched by an estimated 60 million households on Netflix.

Sports.title: Tyson Fury vs Anthony Joshua braced for dramatic 1am start time under new proposal to Cardiff Council - and the Gypsy King wants to walk out flanked by Donald Trump!
Sports.content:
The highly-anticipated bout between Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua could be set for a 1am start time at the Principality Stadium, Cardiff, in December.

That's after Cardiff Council received an application stating the ring walks are planned to start gone midnight, with proposals for the stadium to stay open until 3.30am.

According to the BBC, Millennium Stadium Plc has applied to change its premises licence to allow the fight to take place late 'on a very limited one-off occasion'.

Fury has suggested he will try to persuade United States president Donald Trump to join him for his ringwalk. 'I'll definitely make that offer to my old buddy, old pal, and we'll see if he's available. Probably unlikely because of the situation he's in at the moment, being the President of the United States.'

There is also a request to play live music until 3am on the same date, with a live performance expected before the ring walks.

It is proposed that the stadium roof is closed for the duration of the event, with enhanced security in place.

Other authorities and members of the public can make an objection until November 3, and a council hearing will be held to consider them. It is understood the permission will be granted if there are no objections.

There is a proposal for the ring walks for Tyson Fury (left) vs Anthony Joshua (right) to take place at 1am

There was initially doubt over whether the fight would take place in the United Kingdom or New York City.

It is understood Eddie Hearn pushed hard for the fight to be in Cardiff, with broadcaster Netflix keen to host it later so it can be shown at a reasonable time in the States.

Fury is currently favourite to take victory in the bout, with the Gypsy King claiming he has battled back from 28st – as heavy as an adult mountain gorilla – to chisel down to the shape he's in today.

Fury's physique has fluctuated heavily down the years – in January he described himself as a 'fat, binge-drinking junk-food addict' as he returned from retirement for a fifth time – but he is not messing around on this occasion.

Each fighter will pocket £75million from the face-off. As Daily Mail Sport revealed in September, the two fighters would have been taxed around 30 per cent of their purses in America, compared to 20 per cent in the UK, with Joshua particularly unhappy about the prospect of an extra £7.5million being added to his bill.

The two-time world champion instead demanded that his contract be honoured, which stipulated a British-based fight.

Hearn initially pushed for Wembley Stadium, but the combination of a roof over the Principality Stadium and the Welsh government’s willingness to bend their late-night curfew swung the fight towards Cardiff.

Sports.title: Dana White labels Eddie Hearn a NEPO BABY as war of words escalates between the promoters over Tyson Fury-Anthony Joshua showdown
Sports.content:
Dana White labels Eddie Hearn a NEPO BABY as war of words escalates between the promoters over Tyson Fury-Anthony Joshua showdown

Dana White's war of words with Eddie Hearn has taken another turn after the UFC and Zuffa Boxing chief essentially branded his rival a nepo baby.

The duo have been at each other's throats over various topics this year, from Conor Benn's future to the £150million blockbuster fight between Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua.

Things have escalated over the last month. White, who runs Zuffa Boxing alongside Saudi Arabia's boxing supremo Turki Al-Sheikh, has been billed as the main promoter for the heavyweight showdown and fought for the contest to take place in New York City.

Hearn, who successfully wrestled the fight back to Cardiff, has claimed that the contract Joshua signed stipulates that White cannot be involved in the contest and threatened crunch talks with broadcaster Netflix over White's attendance at Fury and Joshua's press conference on Wednesday in London.

And now, White has taken aim. He said on the Diary of a CEO podcast: 'Eddie's not the guy, Eddie's dad is the guy.

'And I'm not saying this to s*** on Eddie - I'm just being honest. I don't dislike Eddie. But he's not the guy; his dad's the guy.'

Dana White (left) has taken aim at Eddie Hearn (right) as their war of words continues - source: X - @danawhite

White branded Hearn a nep baby due to the sporting success of his father Barry (second left)

Barry Hearn, Eddie's father, has been a sports promoter since the 1970s and has had a huge influence on the likes of boxing, darts and snooker.

Eddie, though, now works in his own right though, according to White, is in his dad's shadow.

White continued: 'Frank Warren's the real guy. I just saw this interview with him; I was like, 'F***ing love it… all this f***ing talking and all this f***ing bulls***, let's f***ing fight.''

There had been doubt over whether the December 11 fight would in fact go ahead due to the involvement of White.

White, whose involvement has been criticised by sections of the British boxing public, was grilled by the media in a cagey press conference, where he labelled the bout a 's***show' while conceding he has 'no idea' if the contest will take place.

'I don't know. The guy who is supposed to be helping the fight has been hurting the fight the entire time,' he said. 'He hasn't done the fight any favours. I don't know anybody who is more full of s*** than Eddie Hearn.'

When asked whether he would step aside to allow the fight to go ahead, White said: 'That's not up to me. I'm involved in the f***ing fight.

'If Eddie Hearn really cared about this f***ing fight — first of all the fight would've happened a f***ing long time ago, one. Number two, he could finance the thing himself.

'Listen, this whole thing's a s***show right now. We'll all know a lot more in the next three, four days, see how this thing plays out.'

The duo have been at a battle over who will promote the fight between Tyson Fury (left) and Anthony Joshua (right)

White had initially raised eyebrows when Benn left Hearn's Matchroom to join Zuffa.

It remains to be seen whether White will have any involvement.

Hearn said this weekend: 'At this point, (White's) completely cooked. What he actually said was, "We're doing the TV production". Which, again, in the contract, is prohibited.

'After that video (of White saying he was producing the fight), I spoke to Sela (the Saudi entertainment company listed as promoters of the event). I said, "Have you seen this video?" They said, in writing, "Yes, and it's completely untrue".

'(White) cannot do that under the contract. They want me to meet them in LA next week, which I probably will.'

Sports.title: From beauty to beast! Former 'Miss Germany' targets a BOXING career and is set for her professional debut
Sports.content:
A former winner of Miss Germany has announced a surprise career switch - and will swap the catwalk for the boxing ring at the age of 33.

Tatjana Genrich was voted Germany's most beautiful woman in 2022 and has now announced she will make her professional boxing debut next month in Magdeburg, rekindling her childhood love of the sport.

Genrich was the Saxony-Anhalt state champion in the flyweight division for amateur boxers between 2007 and 2009. And she recently opened up on why she originally went into the sport, saying: 'At school I was often bullied and I wanted to find a way to defend myself. That's how it all started.'

This then led to her attending a sports school in Halle, Germany where she was picked up by boxing promoter Ulf Steinforth. Years later he reconnected with the model after her fame and stature had grown and suggested the former amateur champion try her hand in the professional ranks.

When asked about their talks, Genrich said: 'Since I sponsor the ring girls at his boxing events, he approached me one day and asked if I wouldn't like to get back in the ring. I finally agreed and am now about to make my professional debut.'

Only four years ago she was Miss Germany... now Tatjana Genrich has her sights set on a career in boxing

The supermodel turned boxer still posts regularly to her 44,500 Instagram followers and owns her own modelling agency

Genrich will be hoping to her journey will inspire a new generation of young women into different sports

Promoter SES Boxing are backing Genrich to become the country's next big superstar, saying: 'Tatjana can follow in Regina Halmich's footsteps. She has all the necessary qualities, an incredible presence, and is extremely ambitious.'

Halmich won 54 of her 56 fights during a storied career between 1994 and 2017 which saw her become one of the most successful female boxers of all time, and also modelled for German magazines.

To prepare for her first fight on November 14, Genrich - who also runs her own modelling agency with 80 models under contract - has begun a rigorous training routine that sees her spending five full days a week in the gym.

In her corner she will have coach Dirk Dzemski, who guided Robert Stieglitz to world champion status in the 2010s.

Genrich also detailed another motivation to succeed in her new career, saying:' I want to be a role model for young women and show them that you can be successful in both your career and sports.

'I train in areas like posture, running and choreography. This prepares me for competitions as well as events like fashion shows.'

Sports.title: Tyson Fury plans to invite 'old buddy' Donald Trump to be part of his ringwalk for £150m mega-fight with Anthony Joshua: 'I'll definitely make the offer!'
Sports.content:
Tyson Fury plans to invite 'old buddy' Donald Trump to be part of his ringwalk for £150m mega-fight with Anthony Joshua: 'I'll definitely make the offer!'

Tyson Fury has suggested he will try and persuade United States president Donald Trump to join him for his ringwalk when he takes on Anthony Joshua in December.

Fury met the president at the UFC Freedom 250 event at the White House in June, joining Trump, First Lady Melania Trump and a host of MAGA royalty on the South Lawn.

He raised eyebrows with a cap, which featured a particularly bold message of support for Trump. 'Donald Trump for Prime Minister', it read alongside an embroidered British flag.

The slogan was a nod to Trump's signature red 'Make America Great Again' caps, which he sported throughout his election campaigns.

It was there Fury said he was keen to take on Joshua in the near future – and that fight has come to fruition, and will take place on December 11 at the Principality Stadium in Cardiff.

And Fury is keen to have his friend there. He said: 'I'll definitely make that offer to my old buddy, old pal, and we'll see if he's available.

'Probably unlikely because of the situation he's in at the moment, being the President of the United States.'

Tyson Fury (centre) has said he will ask Donald Trump (right) to join his ringwalk when he faces Anthony Joshua

Though Fury may want Trump in his corner, Joshua will literally have a Fury in his, with Tyson's uncle, Peter, part of Joshua's group of trainers.

Tyson shrugged off suggestions that Joshua would have the inside track claiming that he hadn't spoken to him in years, but his father John was even more emphatic in discussion with Playbook Boxing, hinting at a betrayal from his brother which meant that he will 'never speak to him as long as (he) lives'.

'If he was to do that (talk to Joshua) in any way, shape or form, that would make him the lowest form of human being,' John stressed. 'Even thinking about doing it, that makes him the biggest dog, the biggest untrustworthy dog of all time.

'If he's going to start giving phone calls and advice, meeting in secret, giving him secret sessions, he's a f***ing cockroach.

'The only advice he could have wanted is on Tyson, isn't it? There is no smoke without fire.'

As if speaking directly to Peter, he finished: 'Son, give your head a wobble. Don't sell your soul to the devil for a fiver.'

Peter shared on social media that he had spoken to AJ 'two months ago' about 'advice on his skill set', calling the Londoner 'a really nice guy'.

'After his fight anything he needs from me (would) be a pleasure. He has a great team around him (including) Team Usyk.'

Sports.title: John Fury hits out at brother Peter, calling him a 'cockroach' for joining Anthony Joshua's camp ahead of Cardiff showdown
Sports.content:
John Fury hits out at brother Peter, calling him a 'cockroach' for joining Anthony Joshua's camp ahead of Cardiff showdown

John Fury called out his brother Peter for being a 'cockroach' after his estranged brother joined Anthony Joshua's camp ahead of the Briton's showdown with his son Tyson in December.

The long-awaited Battle of Britain is set to take place in Cardiff after months of back-and-forth between the Fury and Joshua camps, but neither John nor Peter will be in the corner of the Gypsy King, after Joshua announced this week that Fury's uncle had helped with his preparations.

Eyebrows were raised due to Peter's family ties, but Fury shrugged off suggestions that Joshua would have the inside track claiming that he hadn't spoken to him in years.

His father John was even more emphatic in discussion with Playbook Boxing, hinting at a betrayal from his brother which meant that he will 'never speak to him as long as (he) lives.'

'If he was to do that (talk to Joshua) in any way, shape or form, that would make him the lowest form of human being,' John stressed. 'Even thinking about doing it, that makes him the biggest dog, the biggest untrustworthy dog of all time.

'If he's going to start giving phone calls and advice, meeting in secret, giving him secret sessions, he's a f***ing cockroach.

John Fury called out his brother Peter (left) for potentially helping Tyson's rival Anthony Joshua ahead of their Cardiff showdown (pictured in 2015)

'The only advice he could have wanted is on Tyson, isn't it? There is no smoke without fire.'

As if speaking directly to Peter, he finished: 'Son, give your head a wobble. Don't sell your soul to the devil for a fiver.'

Peter shared on social media that he had spoken to AJ 'two months ago' about 'advice on his skill set', calling the Londoner 'a really nice guy'.

'After his fight anything he needs from me (would) be a pleasure. He has a great team around him (including) Team Usyk.'

John may have been staunchly defensive of Fury in the context of Peter doing anything to sabotage him in the ring, but relations between father and son remain minimal after having been, in John's words, 'completely destroyed'.

The duo are at loggerheads over Fury Junior's career, with his father adamant that he should prioritise his health and wellbeing by retiring for good after two failed attempts.

Peter previously trained Fury between 2011 and 2017, but left the camp amid a schism with father and son.

The Gypsy King had previously sought to set the record straight on Peter's involvement with his rival on social media, deeming Joshua's comments 'categorically untrue'.

'Even if Peter Fury hated me, he’s still my family,' he said. 'That would mean he would be a Fredo, scorpion, snake, rat, b****** piece of s*** if he did that.'

Sports.title: Verstappen jokes about coded messages as Red Bull phases in Lambiase’s successor
Sports.content:
There were still two races on the current Formula 1 calendar missing from Max Verstappen's list of victories: the Madring and the Marina Bay Street Circuit. Given that F1 only visited the street circuit in Madrid for the first time this year, that is understandable, but Singapore has proved to be Red Bull's Achilles' heel for years.

Until this season. In 2026, Verstappen was dominant in Singapore, claiming two pole positions and two victories over the sprint weekend. On Sunday, the main focus was on the start – a major headache for Red Bull this year – although Verstappen managed to hold his position this time.

“The start was critical, and it was just good enough. Again, something was not particularly right at the start, so I need to understand what went wrong there”, Verstappen revealed.

“Before releasing the clutch, it didn't feel good. Then we had a few laps with some deployment issues, so that's where Charles almost got me into Turn 7. Once we had cleared the deployment problems, it was fine.”

According to Verstappen, those starting problems were different from what he had experienced in recent weeks. On those occasions, things had gone wrong when he released the clutch, but this time the problem had already emerged at an earlier stage.

“I need to understand what went on with the engine before even dropping the clutch, because I think that did hurt my start. It was again not fantastic, you can say that.”

Afterwards, Verstappen braked late on the outside line and also managed to survive the deployment issues. That meant the threat from his rivals had passed, although the Dutchman still had to deal with another inconvenience for the remainder of the race: his radio was not working properly.

Charles Leclerc, Ferrari, Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing Photo by: Joe Portlock / Getty Images

The four-time world champion could still hear the team, but his responses were unintelligible.

“Maybe GP was happy that it was not working!” Verstappen laughed in the post-race press conference.

“I couldn't really say anything. He did try at one point to ask me a few things in code, and I think he understood well what I meant or what I didn’t want! But it's never nice. I've been having difficulties with my radio already the whole season, and this weekend has been particularly bad.”

It meant Lambiase had to get creative to obtain Verstappen's input. In the closing stages of the race, he asked the Dutchman to remain silent if he wanted to make another pitstop in the event of a safety car, and to press the radio button if he preferred to maintain track position.

Team principal Laurent Mekies clarified that these radio problems were entirely on Red Bull's side and were not related to any wider technical issues in Singapore.

“I don’t think it’s the circumstances, no, I think it’s on our side”, Mekies said on Sunday night.

“It was not the same issue as in FP1, but it was a little bit painful. These cars are complicated and there is a huge amount of dialogue that needs to happen between the drivers and engineers. But as you have seen, GP found his ways to communicate with Max and vice versa when it mattered.

Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing Photo by: Clive Rose / Formula 1 via Getty Images

“Of course, it's something that we take seriously like everything else. And I'm sure we will come back with a strong solution for it, because it could cost you decisive time in crucial moments.”

Hart to replace Lambiase as Verstappen's race engineer in Austin

As a reward for all his efforts, Red Bull sent Lambiase onto the podium alongside Verstappen, which also came as a surprise to the four-time world champion.

“Yeah, I didn't expect that. I remember he said to me last year in Vegas, "This might be the last time I'm on the podium." I said, "Don't be silly, we're going to win much more." But I almost jinxed myself there, I guess!” Verstappen laughed.

“It was just super nice that they sent him up. We all know that he is leaving, but I think it was very special to share the podium on a track that we had not won together. So yeah, very nice to see him up there.”

At the same time, Red Bull is planning the transition to Verstappen's future race engineer, Tom Hart. He was initially set to join Williams as Alexander Albon's race engineer, but when Verstappen made his preference for Lambiase's successor known internally, Red Bull did everything it could to reverse that move and retain Hart – successfully.

There is no official date yet for when Hart will permanently take over from Lambiase, although Red Bull is in discussions with McLaren about Lambiase's start date and his gardening leave. The timing of the transition partly depends on those arrangements, with 2027 theoretically emerging as a logical outcome.

Before that happens, Hart and Verstappen will already have several race weekends to become more familiar with working together. Red Bull has confirmed to Autosport that Hart will serve as Verstappen's race engineer in Austin, Brazil and Las Vegas, replacing Lambiase in that role.

The team added that Lambiase will still be present at the circuit during those weekends, carrying out his duties as Head of Racing.

Sports.title: Ferrari explains Hamilton’s failed Singapore GP gamble
Sports.content:
As Ferrari team principal Fred Vasseur faced the media following Formula 1’s Singapore Grand Prix, the hot topic was Lewis Hamilton.

Most of the questions revolved around the unsuccessful strategy that saw Hamilton collapse from third to sixth in the Marina Bay race, as he stayed out under the VSC to complete a mammoth 44-lap stint on soft tyres.

Across the last 22 of those, following the neutralisation, Hamilton haemorrhaged 2.5s a lap on average relative to Ferrari team-mate Charles Leclerc. That is how he ended up sixth behind Andrea Kimi Antonelli and both McLaren driver Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri.

With the unwell Briton exempted from his post-race media commitments to visit the medical centre instead, Vasseur faced scrutiny from journalists keen to establish how that decision was made to the highest level of detail. And the Frenchman wasn’t enjoying that prospect; he even interrupted the first question, suggesting it wasn’t necessarily “the big event of the weekend”.

Read Also: Formula 1 Hamilton takes blame for poor Singapore GP strategy call

Regardless, Hamilton’s post-race radio apology made it clear that he had made the call to stay out during the VSC – so how exactly did that discussion pan out?

“[It] was very clear,” Vasseur insisted. “We were P2-P3 on the track. We called two cars, ‘Guys, you pit behind the VSC’. One of my guys said, ‘No, I prefer to stay on track’. Or he didn’t say – he said, ‘I missed the pit entry’.

“Don't blame the team.”

Frederic Vasseur, Ferrari Photo by: Anni Graf - Formula 1 via Getty Images

Vasseur, who was yet to speak to his driver, said Hamilton’s decision was “clearly a mistake”, doubling down on what he previously told broadcasters.

But is it OK for a driver to override the team’s strategy, given he does not have the same exhaustive data and global view as engineers do?

“When you see the outcome, it was not a good call,” Vasseur admitted. “But on the other hand, quite often you are also telling us that we have to listen to the drivers, because they are into the car, they have the feeling with their tyres and so on.

“But I think on this one it was clear for me. But I have also to respect their feeling when they are into the car.”

Hamilton: “A painful lesson today”

Ferrari subsequently provided a statement from Hamilton – making up for his absence in the post-race media pen – in which the seven-time world champion described the setback as a “painful lesson”.

“Today wasn’t the result we were looking for and it was on me,” Hamilton was quoted as saying. “At a track that’s difficult to overtake, you need to try something different and I chose to start on a new medium tyre, to go long and try to make a one-stop work. Unfortunately, the medium didn’t perform as well as the soft.

Lewis Hamilton, Ferrari Photo by: Mark Thompson / Getty Images

“I had a good second stint and the pace was back, but I couldn’t make the progress I needed. Under the VSC, the team called me in but I missed the entry. After that, I decided to stay out and try to hold track position to the end but, in the closing laps, I was struggling massively with tyre degradation and lost three places, finishing P6, which doesn't reflect the pace we had in the car today.

“A painful lesson today, but I take full responsibility for the decisions I made. Not every call will work out, and I can accept getting it wrong but I’m sorry for the team for the points we lost today. They put so much into every weekend, and I wanted to deliver more for them.

“I’ll continue to put the work in and come back fighting at the next race.”

Sports.title: How can Antonelli become F1 world champion at US GP?
Sports.content:
It has been very clear from early on that Kimi Antonelli will become Formula 1 world champion in 2026 after an impressively dominant year for the Mercedes driver.

The 20-year-old has made a huge jump from his up-and-down rookie campaign and with five, consecutive wins from round two to six, Antonelli has been the man to beat virtually all season.

Now, the first chance for him to wrap up the title is finally in sight next time out in Austin with a 102-point gap over team-mate George Russell in second.

If he were to clinch the title at the United States Grand Prix, then Antonelli will have become champion with five rounds remaining - one shy of the record held by Michael Schumacher from 2002.

Here is how he could do it.

How many drivers can still win the F1 2026 world title?

Andrea Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes, Charles Leclerc, Ferrari, Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing Photo by: Clive Rose / Formula 1 via Getty Images

Although it is clear which way the title is going, six drivers are still in mathematical contention due to there being 150 points left available in the 2026 campaign.

That leaves Antonelli, Russell, Lewis Hamilton, Max Verstappen, Charles Leclerc and Lando Norris all with some kind of chance of winning the championship as 139 points separates the top six in the standings.

Position Driver Points Gap to top 1 Kimi Antonelli 340 N/A 2 George Russell 238 102 3 Lewis Hamilton 229 111 4 Max Verstappen 221 119 5 Charles Leclerc 215 125 6 Lando Norris 201 139

How Antonelli becomes F1 world champion at US GP

Considering it is 25 points for a grand prix win and there are five rounds after Austin, Antonelli must hold an advantage of at least 125 points to become champion. That is the maximum total available post-Texas but because the Italian is on eight victories for the season, Russell is next on three, then he could clinch the crown on countback of wins.

An example of that is the most straightforward way for Antonelli to become world champion: winning the US GP, while Russell finishes ninth or lower. Although it is quite unlikely, that would nevertheless leave a 125-point gap between the Mercedes duo with Antonelli taking it on countback.

If Russell finishes 10th at Austin, then Antonelli would still need to win the race to become champion that day. Eighth or higher for the Briton and the non-existent title fight goes to Mexico at the end of October.

If Antonelli finishes... Russell must finish... 1st 9th or lower 2nd or lower Title fight goes to Mexico

For Hamilton to remain in contention, the Ferrari driver cannot be outscored by 14 or more points in the United States. So if Antonelli wins, Hamilton must finish at least fourth and if the Mercedes driver is second, the seven-time world champion needs seventh or above.

If Antonelli finishes... Hamilton must finish... 1st 5th or below 2nd 8th or below 3rd 10th or below 4th or below Title fight goes to Mexico

For Verstappen - the man in form with two wins on the bounce in yet another late resurgence from Red Bull - to be put out of title contention, then Antonelli simply needs to outscore the Red Bull driver by at least six points.

So if the Mercedes driver takes to the top step in Texas, that is enough to end all hopes for Verstappen. Should Antonelli take second, then fourth or below would put the four-time world champion out of it.

If Antonelli finishes... Verstappen must finish... 1st 2nd or below 2nd 4th or below 3rd 6th or below 4th 7th or below 5th 8th or below 6th 9th or below 7th 11th or below 8th Title fight goes to Mexico

It is much simpler when it comes to Antonelli versus Leclerc and Norris, because not losing any points to them would put both out of contention.

The data above is in line with the current calendar, where the season would end with the Qatar and Abu Dhabi Grands Prix.

Sports.title: Hamilton takes blame for poor Singapore GP strategy call
Sports.content:
Lewis Hamilton has taken responsibility for his strategy in Formula 1’s Singapore Grand Prix, after a decision not to pit under a virtual safety car cost him dear.

The VSC was called into action by race control on lap 39 when Lance Stroll pulled aside due to a suspected clutch issue in his Aston Martin.

At that stage of the race, Hamilton had already done 21 laps on softs, while Leclerc was on a 15-lap medium stint – but it was the Monegasque only who made the most of the VSC for a cheap second pitstop.

The Ferraris, which were running second and third, could easily have been double-stacked given they were 4.4 seconds apart and going through Turns 10-11 when the VSC was enforced.

As it happens, it was Hamilton himself who decided to stay out for a mammoth 44-lap stint on softs. This was a failure, as he collapsed to sixth, even behind Oscar Piastri, who had to stop after the VSC due to a slow puncture.

The seven-time world champion was nearly 46 seconds down on team-mate Leclerc on the chequered flag, with his tactical call therefore costing him about 41.5 seconds.

Lewis Hamilton, Ferrari, Lando Norris, McLaren Photo by: Joe Portlock / Getty Images

“Sorry, boys,” Hamilton said on the radio after the race. “I let you down today with that strategy. My call, and I lost us valuable points. I’ll try and make up for it in the next one. Great job with the pitstop though.”

Racing engineer Carlo Santi replied: “Understood, thank you Lewis.”

The British driver was subsequently taken to the medical centre due to feeling unwell, Sky Sports F1 reported, and given dispensation to skip his post-race media commitments so was not available to comment.

Team principal Fred Vasseur explained to F1 TV that Ferrari split the cars at the start, with front-row Leclerc on softs instead of mediums, in order to have a shot at snatching the lead away from polesitter Max Verstappen – which the Monegasque very nearly did.

Answering for the decision under VSC, Vasseur added: “The call was to pit two and Lewis decided to stay on track.

“I think it was a mistake overall, we would have gone for P2-P3 today, but he apologised in the in-lap for the strategy that we asked him to call and he didn't.”

Hamilton’s poor result means his advantage over fourth-placed Max Verstappen in the drivers’ standings has dwindled to eight points, following the Dutchman’s maiden Singapore Grand Prix victory.

Sports.title: F1 Singapore GP: Verstappen takes comfortable victory from Leclerc and Antonelli
Sports.content:
Max Verstappen won Formula 1’s Singapore Grand Prix for the very first time on Sunday, leading Charles Leclerc and Kimi Antonelli under the chequered flag.

Verstappen’s withstood an early challenge from Leclerc and proved quicker over the remainder of the race.

Strategy cost Lewis Hamilton dear, allowing Antonelli to finish on the podium and further extend his championship lead – to the extent he will get a first chance to clinch the title in Austin. Main rival and Mercedes team-mate George Russell fought to a lowly ninth from 19th on the grid.

Verstappen holds off Leclerc at lights out

Front-row starter Leclerc had the best getaway at the Marina Bay Street Circuit, but polesitter Verstappen ever so narrowly held him off in Turn 1. Hamilton maintained third place despite using the medium compound unlike his rivals on softs, followed by Antonelli, Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri – the order of the top six on the grid was unchanged.

Leclerc remained within touching distance of Verstappen until Gabriel Bortoleto stopped on the start/finish straight with a suspected gearbox issue, causing a virtual safety car intervention, but nobody pitted with the Audi potentially blocking the pitlane exit.

By lap 11, Hamilton’s deficit to Leclerc had reached three seconds, with the Briton closely followed by Antonelli and the McLarens; however, that was when the Monegasque started consistently lapping half a second slower than Verstappen. On lap 18, he was four seconds down.

That was when, despite having started on mediums, Hamilton was the first driver to pit, switching to softs; on the previous tour, the Briton had lapped 1.8s slower than Verstappen and 1.4s slower than Leclerc.

Lewis Hamilton, Ferrari, Lando Norris, McLaren Photo by: Joe Portlock / Getty Images

Antonelli was the first frontrunner to move from softs to mediums on lap 23; Leclerc did likewise on the next tour and narrowly rejoined ahead of his Ferrari team-mate, who was not overly happy to be stuck behind – he complained several times on the radio.

“I feel something leaking between my feet,” Antonelli reported on lap 32 – but Mercedes wasn’t concerned – as Verstappen pitted, safely rejoining in the lead.

On lap 35, the Red Bull racer enjoyed a five-second advantage over Leclerc; Hamilton was seven seconds down, Antonelli 11s adrift, with the McLarens of Norris and Piastri respectively 21s and 28s away from the leader, after a 4.2s stop for the Australian.

Hamilton decides not to pit under VSC

The race was neutralised by the virtual safety car on lap 39 as Lance Stroll pulled aside with a suspected clutch issue; Leclerc and Antonelli made the most of it to switch back from mediums to softs, but Hamilton intriguingly chose to stay out on used softs.

“Mate, I have no fucking brakes! I just went straight! The pedal was so long!” shouted an aggrieved Antonelli, as Piastri pitted again on lap 41 due to a slow puncture.

Having rejoined from his second pitstop 10 seconds behind Hamilton, Leclerc caught his team-mate in just five laps and swiftly overtook him. He was 15 seconds down on Verstappen, who was experiencing radio issues, with 15 laps remaining.

Leclerc brought his deficit down to 8.3 seconds on lap 55 of 62, after which it just hovered around hat gap, and Verstappen comfortably prevailed by 7.3s.

Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing Photo by: Rudy Carezzevoli / Getty Images

Struggling on his mammoth 44-lap stint on softs, Hamilton came under pressure from Norris, but Antonelli picked up the pieces, overtaking both cars on his way to the podium. The seven-time world champion collapsed to sixth under the chequered flag, behind Piastri.

Russell struggles to ninth

Starting from 19th owing to a power unit grid drop, Russell made steady progress through the pack, albeit slow, failing to break into the top 10 before pitstops allowed him to do so.

The Mercedes racer was the last driver to change tyres, doing so during the VSC intervention, but the timing wasn’t right and the neutralisation ended shortly after he entered the pitlane.

Russell therefore rejoined behind Liam Lawson, Nico Hulkenberg and Pierre Gasly, only overtaking the Alpine to finish ninth.

It was an underwhelming day for Gasly, who had qualified an impressive seventh but lost two spots to Lawson and Hulkenberg at the start and eventually dropped out of the top 10 altogether, to Isack Hadjar’s benefit. Red Bull’s Frenchman scored one point from a pitlane start, after a nightmare Saturday when he was struck by mechanical woes.

A punchy drive from Oliver Bearman, with breathtaking wheel-to-wheel racing against Haas team-mate Esteban Ocon and a bold down-the-inside overtake on Carlos Sainz, went unrewarded in 12th place, ahead of the Frenchman and the Spaniard. Arvid Lindblad, Fernando Alonso and Sergio Perez followed.

Valtteri Bottas was nearly lapped by his Cadillac team-mate, while Alpine’s Franco Colapinto retired due to a suspected driveline issue. Alexander Albon also failed to finish the race.

Sports.title: FIA admits fairness was compromised in Singapore GP sprint qualifying “mess”
Sports.content:
The FIA has again owned up to its human error at Formula 1’s Singapore Grand Prix, with its single-seater director Nikolas Tombazis describing it as “the worst thing” for the federation.

After sprint qualifying was red-flagged following Sergio Perez’s crash, the end of SQ1 was impacted by race control first failing to reactivate overtake mode, then turning it back on for 27 seconds and deactivating it again.

Drivers were puzzled by the lack of power, and those who were eliminated in that first phase of sprint qualifying felt they unfairly came off worse.

Read Also: Formula 1 Singapore sprint qualifying chaos leaves F1 teams furious

Speaking to Sky Germany, Tombazis pointed out “there’s a lot of things happening in race control simultaneously” and explained how the mistake happened.

“Normally it is a manual process to re-enable it, because clearly when it gets re-enabled we want to make sure from a safety point of view it's okay to do so,” he detailed.

“Unfortunately, there was a pop-up window that came on somebody's computer that was not acted on quickly enough or when it should have. And then under the time pressure and the general other pressure, this was forgotten, unfortunately.

Sergio Perez, Cadillac Racing Photo by: Clive Rose / Formula 1 via Getty Images

“We then went into quite an intense analysis about, was there some other issue, because we could hear, of course, the drivers complaining and saying what's happening. We realised where the problem was.

“At that time there was an erroneous decision to briefly turn it on again, but that was sort of not exactly the correct decision in order for fairness. And then it was turned off again.”

Tombazis went on to admit the situation was “a bit of a mess, quite frankly”, given its impact on the competitive order.

“We're not happy about it, because it affected some drivers more and some drivers less,” he added.

“So as a result, just in the first session of the sprint, we felt this problem interfered with the results – which for us as FIA is probably, in some ways, the worst thing, because our top priorities are always safety and fairness.

“Of course, to have a situation where a result is not fair or incorrect is for us not good. Of course, it is a complicated job, and people do make mistakes, and we need to be conscious of that. But we also need, when we do make mistakes, to analyse them and to make sure they don't happen again – which is what we're doing.”

This blunder occurred less than a week after the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia was disrupted by a power unit glitch for a number of competitors, which required the software to be updated on all cars before the race could get under way.

Sports.title: Why McLaren considers Norris-Piastri Singapore clash so “serious”
Sports.content:
If you thought you'd never have to hear the term "Papaya Rules" again now that McLaren is no longer F1's dominant team, a new flashpoint over the 2026 Singapore Grand Prix weekend provided McLaren with a most unwanted flashback to 2025.

Exactly one year ago, Norris barged Piastri out of the way at the start of the 2025 edition, not causing either car any damage but - as the two drivers were fighting for the championship - landing Norris in hot water with the team. It was the second such incident following the Briton running into the back of Piastri at the Canadian Grand Prix, with McLaren briefly imposing undefined 'repercussions' on its driver. Those only lasted half a race weekend, until Piastri took out Norris at the start of the Austin sprint and the team wiped the slate clean.

Saturday's clumsy collision at the end of the 20-lap Singapore sprint felt like a throwback, even if it took place in vastly different conditions. McLaren has since been usurped by Mercedes as the dominant force, and Piastri and Norris diced over a mere fourth place in a sprint race, tantamount to one point.

But perhaps exactly because it was a meaningless battle, with McLaren scoring the same number of points regardless, Norris' ill-fated lunge caused team principal Andrea Stella so much grief. This one was very avoidable yet cost McLaren constructors' points in its tight battle with a resurgent Red Bull over third, as well as an even bigger workload for the mechanics on a sprint weekend and cost cap budget to repair the damage and replace Piastri's gearbox.

Straight after the incident, Stella was visibly upset, declaring the latest papaya-on-papaya contact "unacceptable". Following an initial round of private talks the Italian was more philosophical as he was quizzed by the written media, though his message didn't mellow as much as his tone did.

"It is serious because the damage for the team is material. We are in a close fight in the championship. We had the ambition to challenge Ferrari and we have an ambition to finish ahead of Red Bull, and this is a problem to finish ahead," Stella summed up the cost.

Stella will have also hoped that after the series of exhaustive - and at times exhausting - talks over the course of 2025, and some robust but respectful racing between his two aces ever since, he didn't need to have this conversation all over again.

Lando Norris, McLaren, Oscar Piastri, McLaren Photo by: Andy Hone/ LAT Images via Getty Images

"It is also serious because we come from a few seasons in which we have reflected together, team and drivers, as to how we approach racing together and how we make sure that the interest of the team is protected," he added.

So, why has it happened again, then, and did it come as a surprise? "That's an interesting question," Stella mused. "Surprised? I've worked with top drivers for so many seasons that I know that with drivers there's always a degree of unpredictability. I'm not necessarily surprised. I know that these things can happen.

"I am, if anything, disappointed. Disappointed as a team principal for a situation that is absolutely not acceptable because it caused material damage to the team and every member of the team knows that the team interest comes before any personal interest, but above all is the main beacon that guides our action and our instinct. As a team we need to reflect as to how we make sure that these situations do not happen anymore."

One source of dissonance is that while Norris apologised and was "told off" by the team, he still insisted after qualifying that both he and Piastri could have done more to avoid the clash. Norris was backed up in that view by the stewards who took no further action, not unlike the unpunished clash between Racing Bulls stablemates Arvid Lindblad and Liam Lawson in Azerbaijan. Perhaps the message has not fully landed, one reporter wondered.

"We had part of the conversations straight after the sprint, but obviously, because we are within a race weekend, what you want to do is to make sure that team and drivers are in the best and most functional condition to keep delivering during the weekend," Stella said, hinting that Norris would come to the right conclusion when there's more time to digest it.

"We will have time to go through the various conversations after the race weekend and before the race, but I trust, because I know both drivers enough, that they will keep reflecting on the episode and I trust and I'm pretty sure that they will extract the key learning without me having to say very much."

But by the same token, McLaren is also keen not to dwell on who or isn't to blame. What's more productive is to use the Singapore episode as an opportunity to learn. An unwelcome but nevertheless timely reminder of what the standard is.

"You know, the aspect of apologies, fault, one driver is predominantly [at fault]...Honestly, that's not the perspective I have and that's not the perspective I want from the drivers," Stella concluded.

"The reflection is [about] how, together, we are going to pursue, protect, promote the interests of the team. This is the assignment. I'm not looking for any apologies. I know the drivers; they are two excellent human beings.

"This is business and as a business I want to know: 'How do we work together to make sure that this does not happen anymore?'

"We approach it with a very constructive mindset because there's only one outcome. That the team will be more united and the team will be stronger in the way we pursue our quest, which is the drivers and the team's quest together."

Sports.title: What Verstappen will change after Red Bull’s poor F1 starts in Malaysia and Singapore
Sports.content:
The Singapore weekend is one of milestones for Verstappen. The Dutchman is contesting his 250th Formula 1 Grand Prix this weekend and has claimed his 50th pole position in the process.

Verstappen now belongs to an exclusive group of just five drivers – alongside Lewis Hamilton, Michael Schumacher, Ayrton Senna and Sebastian Vettel – who have secured 50 or more pole positions, but the Dutchman insists he does not pay much attention to such achievements.

"That's not why I do this. I take it one weekend at a time and always try to get the maximum out of it. Whether that's number 50, 55 or 45... The more, the better, of course, but it's not something I'm going to dwell on and pat myself on the back for, thinking, 'This is really good.' No, not at all."

Nevertheless, the first two days in Singapore have been special. Verstappen has topped every significant session so far – sprint qualifying, the sprint race and regular qualifying – despite the street circuit often proving to be Red Bull's Achilles' heel in recent years.

You might think that would be cause for satisfaction, but Verstappen is still not entirely happy when speaking to the Dutch media in the paddock.

"No, because of course it isn't perfect," Verstappen replied when asked by Autosport why he did not look 100% satisfied. "There's always more to be found and I always want to get more out of it. That's what we'll keep working on."

Extra focus on the start in Singapore

Two aspects were not optimal for Verstappen on Saturday in Singapore: the downshifts and – far more importantly – his start in the sprint race.

Immediately after the shortest race of the weekend, Verstappen described his start as “horrendous” and warned that a repeat on Sunday could cost Red Bull the race.

A closer look at the starting problems reveals two separate issues. Yes, Verstappen has generally struggled with poor and inconsistent starts on numerous occasions this year, but in the wet conditions at Sepang and Singapore, the problem was also partly related to the team's recommendation on which gear to use.

Verstappen got beaten off the line by George Russell during Saturday's sprint Photo by: Sam Bagnall / Sutton Images via Getty Images

Verstappen started in second gear on both occasions – something fairly common in F1 in wet conditions – but several rivals, including Russell, opted for first gear on both occasions, which helped them to spool the turbo and get off the line more effectively with the 2026 power units.

Read Also: Formula 1 Verstappen urges Red Bull to fix race starts problem

"In Malaysia, it was a different problem. That problem was added on top of everything else, which meant starting in second gear didn't work properly there.

"Then the team thought: if that problem doesn't happen here again, starting in second gear should work fine this time. But it still wasn't good enough. My start was actually quite okay compared to most of the others, just not compared to George and Lewis."

The start will therefore be under particular scrutiny again on Sunday, especially with two Ferraris lining up immediately behind Verstappen – on average, the best-starting cars this season.

"Yes, you just know they will have good starts. They've been like that all season. It's always an important factor in Singapore, and if you've had a few poor starts, then naturally there's even more focus on it."

When Autosport asked Verstappen whether he would approach a potentially wet start differently tomorrow, he first made it clear that he was not necessarily hoping for such conditions.

"Hopefully it'll be dry tomorrow, first of all. Otherwise, we'll just have to see whether it's good enough."

Should it be wet, however, Verstappen hinted that he would change his gear selection this time. "I think it's pretty clear that second gear isn't the right gear for us at the moment!" the four-time world champion laughed.

Verstappen knows a good start will be crucial to potentially winning the Singapore GP for the first time Photo by: Sam Bloxham / LAT Images via Getty Images

How can Racing Bulls have better starts than Red Bull?

Remarkably, sister team Racing Bulls has often enjoyed better starts than the senior team this year, even though Verstappen stressed that the hardware and software are completely identical.

"Everything is the same, but of course you have engineers who can use different settings for the clutch, the engine and different procedures for warming up the tyres and so on. So there is a difference there, between different people and how they operate."

According to Verstappen, that is precisely where Red Bull needs to improve, although he stressed that the situation is no longer as disastrous as it was at the beginning of the year.

"No, at the beginning I really had a lot of problems. A lot of random issues that kept coming up, and they also kept happening on my side of the garage."

Now it is more about the details, but Verstappen knows better than anyone that those details could make the difference between victory and defeat as he chases his first win at the Marina Bay Street Circuit.

"You know there's a good chance you'll win this race if you get a good start. But yeah, if you lose it because of that, then of course it's painful, but you also have to accept it. That's just how it is. But, of course, we'll do everything we can on Sunday."

Sports.title: Norris incorrectly believed Hamilton “would have to let me past” after turn one move | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Lando Norris revealed he mistakenly thought the stewards would rule in his favour after Lewis Hamilton went off the track as the pair battled for position.

Hamilton stayed ahead of Norris by going off the track at turn one as they pair fought for position.

Norris, who lost a position to Andrea Kimi Antonelli due to the time he lost fighting Hamilton, said afterwards he thought the Ferrari driver would have to let him overtake as a result.

“I would have passed him at some point,” Norris told Sky after the race. “I just didn’t need to try and overtake him where I did.

“I braked a bit late and could have still put a good move in and he would have had to let me past because he braked way too late.”

However the stewards cleared Hamilton of “leaving the track and gaining an advantage” after the race. They noted Norris also went off the track at the same moment, meaning Hamilton was not required to let him overtake.

“Car 44 [Hamilton] left the track in turn one while the driver was defending his position to car one [Norris],” they noted. “However, the overtaking attempt by car one was not a legitimate one as car one also left the track at the same point.

“Therefore the Stewards determine that both cars rejoined the track in the correct order. Having done so, both car 44 and car one lost their positions to car 12 [Antonelli] which was behind them when they left the track. Given all that, the stewards determine that no further action is warranted in this case.”

Norris, who tangled with his team mate Oscar Piastri while trying to overtake him during the sprint race on Saturday, said it was “not a good weekend for me in terms of making decisions like that.”

Sports.title: How Antonelli can clinch the F1 world championship at the next race in Austin | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Andrea Kimi Antonelli is poised to clinch the world championship at the next round.

The championship leader finished third in the Singapore Grand Prix, extending his lead at the top of the standings to 102 points over team mate George Russell

With six rounds remaining, none of which include sprint races, there are still 150 points up for grabs. That will fall to 125 points after the next race, the United States Grand Prix at the Circuit of the Americas.

Therefore if Antonelli leaves Austin with 125 points in hand over his rivals, he will win the world championship with five rounds to spare.

The only way he can do that is if he wins the race at the Circuit of the Americas. Antonelli will also need Russell to finish no higher than tenth and Lewis Hamilton to finish outside the top five.

Three other drivers remain mathematically in contention for the championship: Max Verstappen, Charles Leclerc and Lando Norris. However none of them can win the title if Antonelli scores another grand prix victory.

The championship situation could change if F1 is unable to hold any of the remaining races. The war in Iran has cast doubt over whether the two final rounds in the Middle East venues Qatar and Abu Dhabi will go ahead. F1 has indicated it could replace one race with another at Imola.

Sports.title: Hamilton apologises to Ferrari after failing to pit when they told him to | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Lewis Hamilton took responsibility for failing to pit when he was instructed to in Singapore, which led him to lose three places.

Ferrari told Hamilton to pit during the second Virtual Safety Car period while he was running third. He failed to, which left him at a disadvantage over the final stint.

Hamilton was running behind race leader Max Verstappen and the other Ferrari of Charles Leclerc when the VSC was deployed. Leclerc did make a second tyre stop and emerged behind his team mate, but easily re-passed him.

Three other drivers caught and passed Hamilton before the end of the race: Lando Norris, who like Hamilton only pitted once, plus two-stoppers Andrea Kimi Antonelli and Oscar Piastri. Antonelli pitted under the VSC while Piastri came in later due to a puncture.

After the race Hamilton apologised to his race engineer Carlos Santi and his crew. “Sorry boys, I let you down today with that strategy,” said Hamilton.

“My call, and I lost us valuable points. I’ll try and make up for it in the next one.”

“Great job with the pit stop though,” he added.

“Understood,” Santi replied. “Thank you, Lewis.”

Ferrari team principal Frederic Vasseur revealed the team called Hamilton in but he failed to enter the pits.

“We called them both to pit,” Vasseur told Sky. “It would have been P2, P3 because we were at P2, P3 on-track and he missed the pit entry. Honestly it’s a bit of a shame because he’s losing a podium too.”

Sports.title: Verstappen cruises to Singapore Grand Prix victory as Ferrari threat fades | 2026 Singapore Grand Prix report
Sports.content:
Max Verstappen dominated proceedings in Singapore to claim his first grand prix victory in the event.

The Red Bull driver completed a dominant weekend by winning the grand prix from pole position, as he did in the previous day’s sprint race.

Verstappen easily saw Charles Leclerc’s attempt to pass him in turn one at the start, then showed the Ferrari pair a clean pair of heels.

Ferrari split the tyre strategies between their drivers, starting Leclerc on softs like Verstappen, while fitting mediums to Lewis Hamilton’s car. However he lacked pace from the start and pitted before his team mate.

That left Hamilton in a compromised position in the second half of the race. Unlike Leclerc, he did not come in for a second pit stop during a Virtual Safety Car period in the second half of the race, and his tyres faded over the final laps.

Hamilton therefore came under attack from Lando Norris and Andrea Kimi Antonelli. He repelled the McLaren at first, which allowed Antonelli to pick off Norris, but then lost places to both his rivals. On the penultimate lap, Oscar Piastri completed his misery by picking off the Ferrari on the run to turn 16.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

Verstappen had over seven seconds in hand over Leclerc when he took the chequered flag. Antonelli was briefly troubled by overheating brakes, and sailed close to the wind with multiple track limits infringements, but came home in the final podium position. The McLaren drivers completed the top five in front of Hamilton.

George Russell made steady progress from 19th on the grid over his opening stint. The second VSC period appeared to be perfectly-timed for him, giving him the chance to cement seventh place.

However race control cancelled the VSC period as he pitted, and he lost three places to Liam Lawson, Nico Hulkenberg and Pierre Gasly as a result. Russell was able to pick Gasly off but had to settle for ninth place behind the other two.

Gasly also lost his grip on the final points place, which went to Isack Hadjar following a long slog from the pit lane. It was a tough afternoon for Alpine as Franco Colapinto was one of three drivers to retire.

Gabriel Bortoleto and Lance Stroll also failed to see the chequered flag, both triggering VSC periods as they retired. Bortoleto’s Audi briefly caught fire in the pit lane after stopping with a clutch problem.
