Sports.title: Canelo Alvarez Sticks With Original Riyadh Fight Plan
Sports.content:
Canelo Alvarez plans to proceed with his October 31 bout against Christian Mbilli in Riyadh, Turki Alalshikh confirmed, standing by the Saudi boxing chief amid ongoing uncertainty around the event.

“Canelo reached out and told me he’ll still fight in Riyadh this October, no matter what happens. He fears nothing,” Alalshikh wrote on X.

That commitment signals a fighter acting in full partnership with organizers. Instead of requesting a change of venue, Canelo gave private assurances that he will make the trip as scheduled. For someone working to hold the fight card together, receiving that backing from the main attraction carries serious weight.

Alalshikh made his appreciation unmistakable in his closing message.

“Thank you to everyone who checked in and showed support. Hard times reveal true friends.”

Canelo is displaying loyalty by keeping the original arrangement intact. Alalshikh has put substantial muscle behind major events featuring the Mexican superstar, and Canelo appears determined to return that backing when complications arise.

Turki Alalshikh is holding the deepest checkbook the sport has ever seen. For an aging superstar whose standard pay-per-view numbers in Las Vegas had begun to settle, maintaining direct favor with Riyadh Season is essential.

How prospective spectators respond to the situation remains less certain.

A promise from the headliner aids the promotion, yet it will not settle the concerns of traveling supporters. Individuals looking at plane tickets, hotel reservations, or seat prices will reach their own conclusions. Canelo’s willingness to compete does not guarantee their presence.

Sparse seating on fight night would still mean Alalshikh values the champion’s pledge. Still, empty sections would drain energy from the arena once Canelo and Mbilli step under the lights. Official ticketing numbers remain unconfirmed, making lower attendance an open risk rather than a settled fact.

The boundary is simple: the fighter controls his arrival, while paying fans decide if they make the trip.

At this point, Alalshikh holds the guarantee he needed most. Based on his statement, Canelo is staying the course in Riyadh.

Sports.title: Agit Kabayel’s Tyson Fury Pick Leans on Old Memories
Sports.content:
Agit Kabayel picks Tyson Fury to handle Anthony Joshua, but that pick relies on memories from a decade ago. Kabayel shared rounds with Fury back in 2016, sharing the ring with a fleet-footed heavyweight vastly different from the man competing today.

Kabayel credits Fury with superior ring IQ, even while respecting Joshua’s single-shot knockout power. His prediction leans on Fury having multiple paths to victory, yet those ancient gym sessions tell us very little about present-day form.

“The better boxer, the better boxing IQ [is with] Fury,” Kabayel told The Ring. “But only one guy in the heavyweight division can beat the guys with one hand. This is Anthony Joshua.” “I think Fury will win the fight. Points, KO, but we will see. My prediction is with Fury.”

The glaring flaw in Kabayel’s logic involves Fury’s faded mobility. The 2016 incarnation feinted opponents out of position, changed angles effortlessly, and slipped outside hitting range with ease. Combine that fluidity with his massive frame, and he became a nightmare to track down.

Recent outings show a far more stationary operator. Fury still knows how to manipulate range with his reach, yet recognizing open space is quite different from possessing the foot speed to claim it. Against someone carrying Joshua’s power, lingering in the pocket too long invites disaster.

Kabayel admits his sparring comparison carries an asterisk.

“For me, the hardest sparring was with Fury,” Kabayel explained, pointing out that he had logged three extra years of professional seasoning before testing Joshua in 2019.

That timeline skews the perspective. Kabayel met Fury as a raw prospect, then shared rounds with Joshua as a fully developed contender capable of holding his own.

Fury’s ring craft gives him a legitimate shot. Still, wondering whether his aging reflexes can execute his intentions remains the central issue. Kabayel’s glowing scouting report honors a long-gone fighter Joshua never has to face.

Looking at Fury across his recent outings, the double defeat to Oleksandr Usyk followed by soft recovery touches against plodding veterans like Arslanbek Makhmudov and Mariusz Wach, you are watching a fighter surviving on reputation and size rather than elite capability.

Beating Wladimir Klitschko in Düsseldorf was a psychological masterclass against an aging champion afraid to pull the trigger, and the 2020 demolition of Deontay Wilder was the absolute ceiling of Fury’s offensive bullying. Everything since has been a steady march into decline.

Sports.title: Fabio Wardley Expects Early Finish In Daniel Dubois Rematch
Sports.content:
Fabio Wardley expects his rematch with Daniel Dubois to finish early, with either heavyweight capable of ending the fight before it reaches the later rounds. Their first meeting lasted 11 rounds, so Wardley’s prediction points to a quicker, more explosive second fight.

“It’s only going one way. It’s finishing early one way or another. It’s going to be a crazy night. Everyone, tune in,” said Wardley to Queensberry.

That “one way or another” qualification leaves room for both outcomes. Wardley knows the danger Dubois brings, even after beating him the first time. He is promising action without pretending that trading heavy punches comes without a cost.

Wardley’s overhand right gives him a clear weapon to take into the rematch. He has already described how he used it to counter Dubois’ jab in their first fight, making Dubois think about what could come back whenever he extended his left hand.

Dubois needs an answer to that punch. His jab can help him control the fight, but throwing it repeatedly without adjusting his defense could give Wardley the opening he is looking for. Wardley doesn’t need to change much if the same counter remains available.

Still, their first fight showed that hurting Dubois early and finishing him early are two different things. Wardley had success well before the stoppage, yet needed 11 rounds to complete the job. Chasing a quicker ending could also make him easier to hit if he becomes too eager after landing.

Wardley expects his supporters to add to the atmosphere on Saturday.

“It’s huge for me. Hometown boy, home grown. Had the club, the supporters, everyone behind me from the beginning,” he said. “So it does mean the absolute most and they’re going to make themselves heard on Saturday night.”

The crowd will be ready for the fireworks Wardley promises. Whether the finish comes early depends on how well Dubois adjusts, and whether Wardley can turn his next opening into something decisive.

Sports.title: Ricardo Sandoval Must Settle The Score With Mendoza
Sports.content:
Ricardo Sandoval must decide on his next fight after losing his WBA and WBC flyweight titles to Sergio “Yoreme” Mendoza last Saturday night in Chicago. The immediate rematch route is his only real play if Golden Boy has a return clause baked into the contract.

Mendoza was brought in as a late replacement, so Sandoval’s team likely secured rematch language. If they did, Sandoval has to trigger it immediately. He gave up all the leverage he built by beating Kenshiro Teraji in Tokyo, and nobody at 112 or 115 is going to offer him big money without those belts.

If there is no rematch clause, Sandoval is in no-man’s-land. The flyweight division moves fast. Unification bouts, big cards in Japan, and potential moves up to junior bantamweight are off the table for him. Those paydays belong to Mendoza now.

To rebuild, Sandoval has to face reality about his defense. Getting dropped three times inside five rounds by a guy coming off a second-round knockout loss shows Sandoval’s habits caught up to him. He relies on taking shots to give shots, but without elite sharpness, his punch resistance completely disappeared last night under Mendoza’s firepower.

Apart from a rematch, he needs a tune-up to see if his chin and punch resistance can hold up before trying to climb back into the top five of the sanctioning bodies. Sandoval should aim for spring 2027, ideally March or April.

That gives him roughly five to six months. He cannot afford another extended layoff, yet he took serious physical damage on Saturday night. Absorbing three knockdowns before getting stopped in the fifth round means mandatory medical suspensions and mandatory rest. He must keep his gloves off for at least sixty to ninety days to let his body recover. Rushing into hard sparring in November or December would be reckless.

Sitting out another year would kill what is left of his career, though. Inactivity was a major reason his timing, reflexes, and punch resistance betrayed him against Mendoza. At 112 pounds, fighters burn out quickly, and the division forgets former champions fast.

Flyweight is the wrong division to play the brooding, inactive contender. It is arguably the most unforgiving weight class in the sport because success relies almost entirely on twitch reflexes, hand speed, and conditioning. Those are the exact attributes that disappear when a fighter sits on the shelf.

Sports.title: Oscar De La Hoya Hesitates Over Schofield vs. Zepeda Unification
Sports.content:
Oscar De La Hoya agreed to a Floyd Schofield–William Zepeda unification after being pressed during DAZN’s post-fight interview, but his initial response suggested little enthusiasm for matching his two lightweight champions.

Schofield had just captured the vacant WBA title by defeating Lucas Bahdi when De La Hoya announced his interest in unifying. That invitation became less straightforward once Chris Mannix brought up Zepeda, Golden Boy’s WBC champion.

“We want to unify the titles against anybody,” said De La Hoya to DAZN.

Mannix asked whether Zepeda would be next. De La Hoya’s answer sent the conversation toward Abdullah Mason instead.

“Well, maybe it’s not the fight to do next, but let’s go with Mason or any world champion in the WBC. Whoever it is, ‘Kid Austin’ is ready,” said De La Hoya.

Mannix returned to the obvious option: “Zepeda has got that WBC world title. Let’s take that fight next.”

“We’ll make that fight happen then,” De La Hoya replied.

That was an agreement, although it came after De La Hoya had already suggested taking another route. There was no date announced or indication that either fighter had accepted the matchup.

The hesitation is understandable from a business perspective. Golden Boy now has two lightweight champions it can promote separately. Each can headline title fights, build his audience, and pursue opponents from other promotional companies. Putting them together guarantees that one leaves without his belt.

Mason is with Top Rank, making him a different proposition. Schofield could lose that fight too, but a victory would bring another title into Golden Boy while preserving Zepeda’s separate championship run. An in-house unification offers no such possibility.

That does not establish De La Hoya’s motive, but it explains why “anybody” might become less appealing when the opponent is another revenue stream within his own company.

For Schofield, Zepeda would also be a tough first defense. His sustained pressure and punch volume would test the new champion’s ability to keep control while being pushed backward.

Zepeda also has an obstacle to facing Schofield next. According to EverythingBoxing’s Darshan Desai, the WBC has ordered him to defend against interim champion Jadier Herrera, with purse bids scheduled for October 20. Mason’s WBO mandatory is also due, with Joe Cordina ranked No. 1.

De La Hoya’s unification plans could therefore require approval from the sanctioning bodies or agreements involving the mandatory challengers before either fight can proceed.

Sports.title: Schofield Wins WBA Title As Sergio Mendoza Upsets Sandoval
Sports.content:
Floyd Schofield claimed the vacant WBA lightweight title, while Sergio Mendoza delivered the night’s biggest upset by stopping unified flyweight champion Ricardo Sandoval on Saturday at Wintrust Arena in Chicago.

The Golden Boy Promotions and Most Valuable Promotions card aired on DAZN. Schofield’s title victory came with disputed knockdown calls, while Mendoza overturned expectations in the co-feature.

Schofield (20-0, 13 KOs), of Austin, Texas, defeated Lucas “Prince” Bahdi (20-1, 15 KOs), of Niagara Falls, Ontario, by unanimous decision over 12 rounds. The judges scored the fight 116-110, 119-108, and 115-111.

Schofield’s speed and movement helped him win rounds, but Bahdi’s power made the contest more competitive than the widest score suggested. In the third, Schofield knocked Bahdi into the ropes, prompting referee Ben Rodriguez to rule a knockdown.

Bahdi hurt Schofield during a fierce sixth round and landed a right hand in the ninth that sent Schofield’s knee to the canvas without a knockdown being called. Rodriguez credited Bahdi with a knockdown in the eleventh, although Bahdi appeared to step on Schofield’s foot as he went down. Schofield stayed mobile in the final round to secure the belt.

In the co-feature, southpaw Sergio “Yoreme” Mendoza (28-1, 24 KOs), of Hermosillo, Mexico, stopped Ricardo “El Niño” Sandoval (27-3, 18 KOs), of Rialto, California, at 0:24 of the fifth round to capture the WBA and WBC flyweight titles.

Mendoza dropped Sandoval twice during the final half-minute of the second round, with referee Mark Nelson administering a count each time. Sandoval rallied in the fourth, outscoring the challenger, but Mendoza dropped him again early in the fifth. After Sandoval rose, Mendoza drove him into the ropes with another attack, prompting Nelson to stop the fight.

The defeat ended Sandoval’s reign in his first defense and disrupted his plans for bigger fights following a lengthy layoff.

Super featherweight Jan Paul Rivera (17-0, 7 KOs), of Salinas, Puerto Rico, defeated Abraham Perfecto (14-3, 9 KOs), of Tecate, Mexico, by unanimous decision over ten rounds.

Rivera dropped Perfecto with a left hook in the second, prompting a count from referee Tommy Gonzalez. Rivera lost a point for a low blow in the ninth but remained comfortably ahead, winning 99-89 on all three cards.

Cruiserweight Tristan “Sweet T” Kalkreuth (18-1, 13 KOs), of North Las Vegas, Nevada, stopped Ivan Rosado (12-1, 9 KOs), of San Juan, Puerto Rico, at 0:44 of the third round of their scheduled ten-round bout.

Kalkreuth dropped Rosado with a right hand to the chin in the first. A third-round flurry brought the intervention of referee Ben Rodriguez, with Rosado still on his feet.

Light middleweight Grant Flores (14-0, 10 KOs), of Coachella, California, stopped Mikey Dahlman (19-3, 17 KOs) at 1:48 of the second round.

Flores dropped Dahlman with a left to the body in round two. Dahlman beat referee Dave Smith’s count, but Flores followed with unanswered punches until Smith halted the contest.

Lightweight Jahmal Harvey (5-0, 4 KOs), a 2024 U.S. Olympian from Oxon Hill, Maryland, stopped Pedro Castaneda (9-2-1, 5 KOs), of Ciudad Juarez, Mexico, at 0:28 of the third round of their scheduled eight-round fight.

Boxing from a southpaw stance, Harvey landed a left hand to the chin that dropped Castaneda. Castaneda got up but was in no condition to continue, prompting referee Dave Smith to wave it off.

Super featherweight Cris Williams (15-0, 8 KOs), of Chicago, defeated southpaw Asa “Ace” Stevens (7-1-1, 2 KOs), of Waianae, Hawaii, by unanimous decision over eight rounds.

Williams controlled the opening four rounds and hurt Stevens in the seventh. The judges scored it 78-74 twice and 77-75, with Mark Nelson refereeing.

Minimumweight Naomy “Wonder Woman” Valle (16-1, 9 KOs), of San Jose, Costa Rica, defeated Sheyla Moreno by unanimous decision over eight two-minute rounds.

Valle’s cleaner punching helped her build a lead, and a point deduction for holding in the eighth did not prevent her from winning her professional U.S. debut. Dave Smith refereed the bout.

Heavyweight Joshua “The Rocket” Edwards (8-0, 7 KOs), a 2024 U.S. Olympian from Houston, stopped Craig Lewis (15-10-1, 8 KOs), of Detroit, one second into the third round of their scheduled eight-round contest.

Edwards controlled the first two rounds and hurt Lewis near the end of the second. Lewis could not continue because of an injury, and referee Tommy Gonzalez halted the fight at the start of the third.

Michael Vale served as ring announcer.

Sports.title: Floyd Schofield Beats Lucas Bahdi To Claim WBA Title
Sports.content:
Floyd Schofield won the vacant WBA lightweight title Saturday night, using his speed and movement to beat Lucas Bahdi by unanimous decision in a fight that tested his ability to recover under pressure.

The judges scored it 116-110, 119-108, and 115-111 at Wintrust Arena in Chicago. Schofield (20-0, 13 KOs) earned the belt, but Bahdi (20-1, 15 KOs) made him work considerably harder than the widest card suggested.

Schofield established his jab early, darting into range with combinations before moving away. Bahdi answered with heavier punches and body work, showing that he could trouble the quicker fighter when he found openings.

A left hook sent Bahdi into the ropes in round three, earning Schofield a knockdown and an early advantage. Bahdi absorbed the setback and continued looking for opportunities to land his power shots.

The sixth became a fierce round in which both fighters were hurt. Bahdi badly rocked Schofield with heavy punches, but Schofield fired back rather than allowing the Canadian to take complete control. His willingness to trade made the fight entertaining, although it also gave Bahdi the kind of contest he needed.

Schofield returned to movement and counters in the following rounds. That approach forced Bahdi to chase, and his difficulty cutting off the ring allowed Schofield to collect points without remaining in punching range.

The refereeing became a talking point in the ninth when a Bahdi right hand sent Schofield’s knee to the canvas without a knockdown being called. Bahdi received credit for a knockdown in round eleven, though their feet tangled during that incident.

Schofield stayed mobile in the twelfth and reached the final bell. He showed enough boxing ability to win, along with the toughness to recover when Bahdi hurt him. The next step is tightening his defense: his speed won rounds, but trading unnecessarily repeatedly exposed him to Bahdi’s biggest weapon.

Sports.title: Sergio Mendoza Shatters Ricardo Sandoval’s Plans With Upset
Sports.content:
Sergio Mendoza Cordova wrecked Ricardo Sandoval’s plans with a fifth-round stoppage, taking the unified WBA and WBC flyweight titles in a fight the defending champion was expected to win Saturday night in Chicago.

Mendoza (28-1, 24 KOs) dropped Sandoval (27-3, 18 KOs) three times at Wintrust Arena, recovering from a second-round knockdown of his own to deliver the biggest victory of his career. The referee intervened in the fifth as Sandoval could no longer cope with the challenger’s attack.

Sandoval had entered his first defense looking to build on the split-decision victory over Kenshiro Teraji that earned him both belts in Japan in July 2025. Instead, his return after more than a year of inactivity ended with those titles heading to Mendoza.

This was supposed to be the night Sandoval got moving again. A successful defense would have allowed him to pursue bigger fights from the position of a unified champion. Now, he faces the task of rebuilding after a damaging defeat, with those opportunities belonging to somebody else.

Sandoval briefly appeared to have the fight moving his way when a right hook put Mendoza down in round two. That success did not discourage the Mexican southpaw, who recovered and used his pressure and punching power to turn the contest.

Mendoza’s three knockdowns made this more than a champion getting caught once. Sandoval could not regain control as the challenger kept hurting him, and the fifth-round intervention ended his hopes of rescuing the defense.

The result was especially unexpected given Mendoza’s recent form. He entered after a second-round knockout loss to Thanongsak Simsri in April, making his U.S. debut as a late replacement and heavy underdog.

Sandoval’s long absence invites questions about his sharpness, but Mendoza supplied the decisive punches. An opponent expected to help launch the champion’s next run instead took both belts and forced Sandoval to start over.

Sandoval walked into Chicago treating Mendoza like a stay-busy fight to dust off fifteen months of rust, and he paid the ultimate price for it. When a unified titleholder sits out for well over a year, thinks he can just show up against a heavy puncher, and gets dragged into a firefight, this is exactly what happens.

Ghana News.title: Be careful with cross-border lending, foreign currency exposures – BoG to financial institutions
Ghana News.content:
Dr Johnson Asiama, BoG Governor

The Bank of Ghana has advised Regulated Financial Institutions (RFIs) that engage in cross-border lending, investments, trade finance, or foreign currency exposures to have adequate policies and procedures for identifying, assessing, measuring, evaluating, monitoring, reporting and controlling or mitigating country risk and transfer risk on a timely basis.

This is to avert the potential default or deterioration in credit quality of foreign counterparties arising from country-specific macroeconomic, fiscal, political or financial sector conditions.

The advice is captured in the Credit Risk Management Directive for all Banks, Savings and Loans, Finance Houses and Financial Holding Firms.

The BoG also urged RFIs not to introduce or implement such products, market entries, or delivery channels unless the required regulatory approvals have been obtained, where applicable.

Credit Risk Management Process

On Credit Risk Management Process, it said an RFI shall establish and enforce strict policies to avoid association with individuals involved in fraudulent activities or other serious financial crimes or misconduct.

Similarly, an RFI shall employ robust due diligence measures, including obtaining references from known parties, accessing credit reference bureaus, and becoming familiar with individuals responsible for managing a company, including checks on their integrity, experience, and financial condition.

Credit Appraisal and Approval

The Central Bank pointed out that an RFI shall establish sound, well-defined credit-granting criteria for approving credit in a safe and sound manner. “The criteria shall specify eligible borrowers, the types, amounts, and tenors of credit the RFI is willing to provide, and the terms and conditions under which credits may be granted”.

Again, an RFI shall undertake a comprehensive credit risk assessment that is proportionate to the nature, type and size of the exposure.

Similarly, it shall apply experienced credit judgement using a scalable and flexible approach to its credit risk assessment of a borrower, particularly where borrower information is limited, adding, FRIs shall diversify their loan portfolios across sectors, geographical locations, borrower types and credit risk mitigants within the constraints of local market structures.

Exposures to individuals

For exposures to individuals, the BoG said an RFI’s credit assessment shall, at a minimum and where relevant, consider the purpose and structure of the exposure and sources of repayment, including reasonable verification of income or cash flows using formal or alternative documentation; the borrower’s or counterparty’s current risk profile (including the nature and aggregate indebtedness) and its sensitivity to economic and market developments; among others.

From 1st July 2027, the Bank of Ghana will begin the implementation of the Credit Risk Management Directive for all Banks, Savings and Loans, Finance Houses and Financial Holding Firms.

The broad objective of the directive is to enhance the resilience of Regulated Financial Institutions (RFIs) by ensuring that they establish and fully implement adequate and effective credit risk management systems that commensurate with their risk-taking activities and capital strength.

Ghana News.title: GPL 2026/27: Medeama go three clear as Hearts of Oak recover and Bechem stage stunning comeback

Medeama strengthened their position at the top of the Premier League with a commanding 3-1 victory over Heart of Lions, while Hearts of Oak returned to winning ways and Bechem United produced an impressive comeback on an eventful Matchday Six.

Karela United completed the weekend’s round-up of winners with a 1-0 victory over Dreams FC. Malik Abubakar scored the decisive goal, giving Karela their third consecutive home win.

Ghana News.title: Ntiamoah Foundation launches “BEYOND 20” anniversary campaign
Ghana News.content:
Ntiamoah Foundation has launched BEYOND 20: From Impact to Legacy, a year-long campaign marking two decades of improving lives through education, health, and community development, while setting out its vision for the future.

Established in 2006 by the Entrepreneur, Robert Kwaku Appiah Asante (R.K.A. Asante), Ntiamoah Foundation has worked primarily with communities in the Birim North and Birim South Districts of the Eastern Region. Its interventions span early childhood literacy, Reading Clubs and libraries, ICT education, scholarships, menstrual and maternal health, support for health facilities, and community outreach.

Over the past two decades, the Ntiamoah Foundation has invested over GH¢23 million in today’s value in improving access to education, healthcare and community support. This investment has supported 34 schools and nearly 6,500 young readers, strengthened 14 Community-based health planning and services (CHPS) facilities, supported 436 life-changing surgeries and reached over 8,000 girls through menstrual health programmes, to name a few. Together, these achievements reflect a 20-year commitment to creating opportunities and improving lives in underserved communities.

Launching the anniversary campaign, Executive Director Mercy Quansah-Ansah said the milestone provides an opportunity to reflect on the Foundation’s impact and set the direction for its next chapter.

“Twenty years gives us much to celebrate, but BEYOND 20 is also about asking what we can put in place today that will still be changing lives twenty years from now. For us, that is the shift from impact to legacy: creating opportunities today that can continue to transform lives for generations to come.”

As part of the campaign launch, the Foundation has unveiled a 20th-anniversary identity and redesigned website, which will serve as a platform for impact stories, programme updates, anniversary activities and opportunities for individuals and organisations to support its work.

Building the Next Chapter

Throughout the anniversary year, Ntiamoah Foundation will continue its established education and health programmes while introducing three flagship initiatives designed to turn twenty years of impact into a legacy.

Programme B.E.A.M. will become the Foundation's flagship education model, bringing together literacy, life skills, creativity, digital learning, leadership and community support to develop confident, ethical and future-ready young people. It builds on two decades of investment in Reading Clubs, libraries, ICT and other educational interventions.

The Foundation will also launch the R.K.A. Asante Scholarship Scheme, a permanent programme established in honour of its founder. Beyond financial support, the scheme will combine scholarships with mentorship, leadership and professional development and community service. To commemorate the 20th anniversary, 20 for 20 Awards will select the first twenty scholars, creating the inaugural cohort of what the Foundation hopes will become a lifelong community of future leaders committed to giving back.

The third flagship initiative is the Legacy Project, a long-term investment in community spaces and infrastructure that will continue serving people beyond the anniversary year. The project will create spaces to preserve local history and heritage, advance learning and leadership, and build skills and opportunities for young people. It will also include recreational infrastructure, beginning with 3 multipurpose community centres to promote youth development, healthy lifestyles and community connection.

Board Chair Dr. Kojo Pumpuni Asante said the next chapter will require an even broader community of partners: “Ntiamoah's journey has always been built on partnership. As we look beyond twenty, we invite individuals, institutions and organisations who share our belief in the power of education and health to join us. The next chapter is about multiplying opportunity and building something that future generations can inherit and build upon.”

Derek Boateng, Senior Manager for Sustainability and External Relations for Zijin Golden Ridge Limited, one of the Foundation's longstanding partners, congratulated Ntiamoah Foundation on the milestone:

“Over the years, we have witnessed Ntiamoah Foundation's commitment to improving educational outcomes, strengthening healthcare delivery and creating opportunities for vulnerable communities. Its impact can be seen not only in the projects delivered, but in the lives transformed. We congratulate the Foundation on twenty years of service and look forward to continuing our partnership.”

A Year of Celebration and Legacy

BEYOND 20 will spotlight the people, partnerships and communities that have shaped Ntiamoah Foundation's journey, while mobilising support for its next chapter.

The anniversary year will culminate in a Fundraising Gala Dinner and Thanksgiving Service in December, bringing together partners, donors, community leaders, beneficiaries and other stakeholders to celebrate twenty years of service and support the Foundation's future programmes.

BEYOND 20 is both a celebration of what has been achieved and an invitation to help build what comes next.

Ghana News.title: Credit Risk Management Directive: BoG to begin implementation for banks, others from July 1, 2027
Ghana News.content:
Governor of the Bank of Ghana, Dr. Johnson Asiama

The Bank of Ghana from 1st July 2027 will begin the implementation of the Credit Risk Management Directive for all Banks, Savings and Loans, Finance Houses and Financial Holding Firms.

The broad objective of the directive is to enhance the resilience of Regulated Financial Institutions (RFIs) by ensuring that they establish and fully implement adequate and effective credit risk management systems that commensurate with their risk-taking activities and capital strength.

The specific objectives are to ensure that RFIs develop an appropriate framework for the management of their credit risk by establishing an appropriate credit risk environment, among others.

According to the Central Bank, the RFIs shall align their credit risk management practices with the requirements of this Directive. However, in assessing the quality of RFIs’ their risk management of credit risk, the BOG will take into account the principle of proportionality.

In particular, the assessment will be aimed at ensuring that RFIs’ credit risk management processes and tools are commensurate with profile, systemic importance, market and macroeconomic conditions as well as the scale and complexity of their activities, among others.

Governance and Risk Management Framework

The Bank of Ghana said the Board of RFIs shall bear the ultimate responsibility for the credit risk assumed by the RFI and for ensuring the existence and ongoing effectiveness of the credit risk management framework.

Similarly, the Board shall review and approve the RFI’s credit risk appetite, credit risk management strategy, as well as credit policies, procedures, controls and management information system (MIS) at least annually or whenever there are material changes, to ensure continued adequacy, relevance and effectiveness.

Roles and Responsibilities of the Senior Management

The Central Bank said the Senior Management of an RFI shall be responsible for implementing the Board-approved credit risk management strategy and for establishing, maintaining, and enforcing appropriate policies and processes for identifying, measuring, monitoring, reporting, and controlling or mitigating credit risk. Such policies and processes shall cover all credit related activities of the RFI and apply at both the individual exposure and portfolio levels.

The Senior Management’s responsibility for implementing the credit risk management strategy and operationalising the RFI’s credit risk policies includes ensuring that credit origination, credit assessment, approval, monitoring, and review responsibilities are clearly defined, properly assigned, and supported by appropriate segregation of duties.

According to the Bank of Ghana, the effective management of credit risk within a comprehensive risk management framework is fundamental to the safety and soundness of banks, finance houses, savings and loans companies or financial holding companies regulated under the Bank and Specialised Deposit-Taking Institutions Act, 2016 (Act 930), hereinafter referred to as RFIs.

Over the past two decades, global financial developments have underscored the critical importance of robust credit risk management frameworks in safeguarding the stability of the financial system. Events such as the 2008-2009 global financial crisis revealed how weak credit underwriting standards, excessive leverage, and inadequate risk governance can rapidly translate into widespread loan defaults and systemic distress.

The Ghanaian banking sector clean-up exercise in 2017-2019 also highlighted significant deterioration in asset quality and, consequently, pressure on capital and liquidity resulting from weaknesses in underwriting standards, risk management, governance, and related-party practices. Conversely, RFIs that established and adhered to sound credit risk management practices demonstrated stronger financial resilience.

Ghana News.title: Ghana Brands Awards 2026: Leading brands, business trailblazers to shine on November 20
Ghana News.content:
Minister for Trade, Agribusiness and Industry, Elizabeth Ofosu-Adjare

Ghana’s leading brands, outstanding businesses, visionary entrepreneurs and industry trailblazers will take centre stage on November 20, 2026, as the Ghana Brands Awards (GBA) prepares to celebrate excellence, innovation and outstanding business performance across the country.

Powered by the Chartered Institute of Project Analysts and Consultants (CIPAC), GBA is a prestigious awards programme dedicated to recognising businesses and individuals whose achievements are making a meaningful contribution to Ghana’s economic growth, industry development and national progress.

The awards will provide a platform to celebrate organisations that are setting new standards in their respective industries through strong leadership, operational excellence, quality service delivery, innovation and a commitment to sustainable growth.

Beyond celebrating established brands, GBA seeks to spotlight the entrepreneurs, business leaders and industry professionals whose vision, investment and achievements are creating opportunities, strengthening competitiveness and shaping the future of Ghana’s business environment.

A Platform to Celebrate Excellence and Build Brands

The Ghana Brands Awards aims to become a leading platform for recognising business excellence and promoting a culture of achievement across Ghana’s private and public sectors.

The initiative seeks to honour businesses that have played a defining role in advancing their industries, setting benchmarks in sustainability, operational performance, customer service and innovation. It will also recognise outstanding projects and individual achievements that distinguish businesses from their competitors and deliver measurable value to customers, investors, employees and the wider economy.

By bringing together leading players from different sectors, GBA will offer an opportunity to celebrate the local and international companies contributing to Ghana’s economic transformation while encouraging healthy competition, stronger corporate standards and continuous improvement.

For participating organisations, the awards represent an opportunity to showcase their achievements, strengthen brand visibility and position themselves among the businesses setting the pace for excellence in Ghana.

24 Awards Categories to Celebrate Industry Trailblazers

The 2026 edition will recognise outstanding performance across a broad range of industries, reflecting the diversity and growing potential of Ghana’s economy. The proposed awards categories include:

Banking, Finance and Insurance

Bank of the Year

Community Bank of the Year

Microfinance Bank of the Year

Development Bank of the Year

Debt Collection Company of the Year

Insurance Company of the Year – General

Insurance Company of the Year – Life

Health Insurance Company of the Year

Corporate Pension Trust of the Year

Securities and Investment Company of the Year

Industry, Energy and Infrastructure

Manufacturing Company of the Year

Petroleum Company of the Year – Upstream

Petroleum Company of the Year – Downstream

Real Estate Company of the Year

Postal and Courier Services Company of the Year

Shipping Company of the Year

Mining Company of the Year

Healthcare, Pharmaceuticals and Consumer Products

Diagnostics Company of the Year

Pharmaceutical Company of the Year

Herbal Medicine Manufacturing Company of the Year

Beverage/Water Company of the Year

Entrepreneurship and Social Impact

Entrepreneur Man of the Year

Entrepreneur Woman of the Year

Not-for-Profit Organisation of the Year

These categories are designed to recognise organisations and individuals that demonstrate exceptional performance, strong leadership, innovation and meaningful contributions to their respective sectors.

In an increasingly competitive business environment, recognition can help distinguish a brand, strengthen its reputation and communicate its achievements to customers, partners, investors and other stakeholders. GBA offers businesses an opportunity to bring their accomplishments into the spotlight and celebrate the people, strategies and innovations behind their success.

Participation can also create opportunities for networking, business engagement and greater visibility among industry leaders and other stakeholders.

For entrepreneurs and corporate executives, the Awards provide a platform to celebrate leadership, inspire emerging businesses and demonstrate the value of building organisations that combine strong performance with long-term sustainability.

Companies across eligible sectors are therefore encouraged to prepare their entries, showcase their achievements and take advantage of the opportunity to compete for recognition at the 2026 Awards.

GBA 2026 also presents an opportunity for organisations seeking to strengthen their corporate visibility and align their brands with business excellence, innovation and national development.

Ghana News.title: T-bills auction: Demand improves as government exceeds target by about 76%; interest rates soften
Ghana News.content:
Demand for treasury bills improved as the government exceeded its treasury bills target by about 76.4% to GH¢5.06 billion.

This is coming despite some analysts’ prediction that investor interest will remain relatively soft at the next auction.

The Treasury, however, accepted GH¢4.40 billion of the total bids as against a target of GH¢2.86 billion.

According to auction results by the Bank of Ghana, the chunk of the bids came from the 91-day instrument.

A little over GH¢3.2 billion of the bids were tendered, representing 64.9% of the total bids.

The uptake was, however, GH¢3.0 billion.

The 182-day bill received bids of about GH¢1.3 billion. A little above GH¢1.2 billion was accepted.

For the 364-day bill, about GH¢468.9 million of the bids were tendered. A little above GH¢136.5 million of the bids were accepted.

Meanwhile, interest rates continued to soften on the yield curve.

This will help reduce the government's cost of domestic debt.

The yield on the 91-day bill declined by 4.0 basis points to 4.60%.

That of the 182-day bill also went down to 6.27% from the previous week’6.31%.

Similarly, the yield on the 364-day bill dropped by 5.0 basis points to 9.75%.

Ghana News.title: Ziope undertakes initiative to build a technologically inclined community, commissions self-help ICT lab
Ghana News.content:
The Chiefs and people of Ziope in the Agotime Ziope District of the Volta Region have undertaken an initiative aimed at building a technologically inclined community.

The initiative saw the commissioning of a well-equipped self-help information and communication technology lab for the community basic school, aimed at providing all-round training for pupils.

This would enable the pupils to study the practical aspects of ICT, unlike previously, when they only had the theory with illustrations on the boards.

The Ziope Community, under the leadership of Dufia, Togbe Kpoduave Ahiagba IV, instituted the Ngoryiza, 2024, to mobilise resources towards the development of the area.

Noticing the significance of information and communication technology in today’s world, proceeds from the 2025 celebrations were directed at the construction of a lab.

Community commitment

At the commissioning ceremony, Togbe Kpoduave Ahiagba IV lauded the community’s enthusiasm towards initiatives aimed at enhancing the livelihoods of the residents.

He identified their efforts towards the construction of a 4-unit nurses’ quarters to house staff posted to the community health centre, contributing to improved healthcare delivery in the area.

He eulogised Rev Mensah Djokoto for providing forty desktop computers for the proposed ICT lab, which is furnished with an air conditioner, robotic logistics and an internet connection.

“None of the public Junior High Schools in Ghana has this kind of logistics, as seen at the Ziope Basic School. I am happy we undertook this initiative to secure the future of our children and the Ziope community", he said.

Togbe Kpoduave Ahiagba IV urged them to continue to contribute towards such development initiatives, to drive development in the Ziope community.

“In unity we will find strength and development. If you bring a cedi and I bring a cedi, doesn't it become 2 cedis? Will your Cedi alone be able to do it? So we must continue on this agenda and not be tired as we have identified another project for next year”, he said.

Coding and robotics

Rev Mensah Djokoto explained that he was touched and took the decision with a friend to make such a significant contribution to the education of pupils in the community, in an attempt to give back to society.

He said that a zeal to ensure the pupils have an all-round ICT education prompted him to add coding and robotics to the centre, hence involving the Ghana Code Club.

The Founder and Director of Ghana Code Club, Ernestina Edem Appiah, said a practical curriculum beginning with digital literacy and computational thinking, artificial intelligence, coding, robotics and electronics will be deployed, targeting how to train the pupils in creating with technology.

“The children will learn to build programs and animations using tools such as Scratch; they will explore critical computing with tools such as micro: bit. They will learn the foundations of robotics, and gradually be introduced to AI, including how AI works, how it can be used responsibly, and how they can use emerging texts to create solutions to problems within their own communities”, she said.

“We strongly believe that coding begins in their minds. So even before a child becomes confident with her computer, we tell them how to think logically and identify patterns. Break problems into smaller parts, experiment, make mistakes, and try again. That is a kind of learning we want the centre to be present”, she added.

BECE performance

The Member of Parliament for Agotime Ziope, Charles Agvbeve, lauded the initiative, underscoring the need for communities to champion self-help projects, helping the government to develop the country.

He expressed optimism about performance in the Basic Education Certificate Examination (BECE) would improve as the “Agotime Ziope District scored first in 2025”, urging pupils of the final year students of the Ziope Basic School to score 1 in ICT in the 2026 BECE.

He advised that the ICT lab should be used as a learning centre for pupils from other schools in the enclave to enhance their training as well.

The Volta Regional Chairman of the National Democratic Congress, Mawutor Agbavitor, was elated with the initiative, acknowledging their efforts to lead the way in developing their community.

He was enthused with their choice of enhancing ICT training of the pupils, as ”ICT is no longer a luxury but rather a necessity. The jobs of tomorrow, the knowledge of today, and the competition our children will face, all require digital skills.”

The community launched the 2027 edition of the Ngoryiza, hoping to raise funds to tackle other social needs of the community.

Ghana News.title: ECG announces power outage in parts of Tema, Central Region due to network fault, maintenance
Ghana News.content:
The Electricity Company of Ghana (ECG) has announced a power outage affecting parts of the Tema Region due to a fault in its network, while several communities in the Central Region will experience a temporary interruption in electricity supply on Tuesday, October 13, 2026, to allow for planned maintenance works.

In a notice to customers, ECG’s Tema Region said the network fault had affected Comm. 17, Timber Market, Resolve Hospital, Bakeshop, Marina Mall at Spintex, Baatsonaa and surrounding areas.

The company said its engineers were working to resolve the fault and restore electricity supply to the affected communities.

ECG apologised to customers for the inconvenience caused by the unplanned outage and assured them that efforts were underway to address the problem.

The company did not specify when power supply would be fully restored to the affected areas.

Meanwhile, ECG has scheduled planned maintenance works for Tuesday, October 13, from 9:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., which will result in a temporary power outage in several communities, mainly in the Central Region.

The affected areas include Komenda, Kissi, Ayensudo, Ampenyi, Elmina, Eguafo, Aburansa, Besease, Ebu Krom, Agona Town, Breman, Iture, Duakro, Amamuma, and surrounding communities, as well as several other towns and settlements listed in the company’s notice.

The company said the maintenance exercise forms part of efforts to improve service delivery and apologised in advance for the inconvenience customers may experience.

ECG has urged affected customers to take note of the scheduled outage and make the necessary preparations ahead of the exercise.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.title: Russian authorities detain suspect over St. Petersburg cafe blast
World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.

World.title: Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing
World.content:
Washington —

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

The balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person said, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical new insights to the People’s Republic of China.”

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have said.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

Video Ad Feedback Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33 • Source: CNN Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official said in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”

Gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”

The surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

Still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

World.title: Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose
World.content:
Hong Kong —

An anticipated meeting between Taiwan’s President Tsai Ing-wen and US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in California this week has sparked concerns of a repeat of the pressure campaign China launched last year when then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei.

At that time, Beijing encircled the island democracy with unprecedented military drills – firing multiple missiles into its surrounding waters and sending dozens of warplanes speeding across a sensitive median line dividing the Taiwan Strait.

It also cut off contact with the United States over a number of issues from military matters to combating climate change, in retaliation for what it viewed as a violation of its sovereignty.

This time, Beijing has already threatened to “resolutely fight back” if a Tsai-McCarthy meeting goes ahead.

Video Ad Feedback See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32 • Source: CNN See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32

It also slammed Washington for allowing Tsai to stopover in the US while en route to and from official visits in Central America, warning it could lead to “serious” confrontation between the two powers.

A defiant Tsai staked out her own ground, pledging as she took off on her 10-day trip not to let “external pressure” stop Taiwan from connecting with the world and like-minded democracies.

But the optics of the meeting, taking place in California and not Taiwan, and its timing – at a particularly thorny moment in China’s foreign relations and ahead of a presidential election in Taiwan that could reset the tone of its relationship with Beijing – may see Beijing tread more carefully this time, or at least not escalate further, analysts say.

“This puts the burden on China not to overreact, because any overreaction is only going to push China further away from the world,” said Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington.

That doesn’t mean, however, that Beijing won’t be closely watching Tsai’s movements as it calibrates its response – and decides how much military might to flex over her meeting with an American lawmaker on American soil.

The opacity of China’s system – and the potential for competing interests within its vast bureaucracy – also make it difficult to accurately predict its response.

“Every time Taiwan does anything that China doesn’t like, the Chinese react with their own military coercion,” Sun said. But in the current situation, “they have to consider the consequences of overreaction,” she added.

House Speaker Kevin McCarthy talks to reporters at the Capitol in Washington on March 24, 2023. J. Scott Applewhite/AP

Rising pressure

The expected meeting, which McCarthy’s office announced earlier this week would take place on Wednesday, also comes at a precarious moment in US-China relations.

Washington and Beijing are struggling to stabilize their communication amid flaring tensions over issues from a downed suspected Chinese surveillance balloon to semiconductor supply chains – raising the stakes of potential damage to that relationship if Beijing lashes out as it did when Tsai met Pelosi.

Taiwan is still feeling the fallout of that response last August, with Chinese military forces now regularly making incursions over what had previously been an informal but largely respected border of control between Beijing and Taipei in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan’s official Central News Agency also reported Monday that Tsai would meet with McCarthy, citing Tsai’s presidential office.

Video Ad Feedback See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05 • Source: CNN See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05

But a meeting between Tsai and the leader of the Republican majority in the US House of Representatives, who ranks second in line to the Presidency, would mark another symbolic moment for Taiwan and the US, which only maintain unofficial ties.

For Tsai, who is entering the final year of her two-term presidency, “it’s clearly a capstone event,” according to Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at the Australian National University’s Taiwan Studies Program. “She has this image as the Taiwanese president who has taken US-Taiwan relations to new heights, and who … has been able to give Taiwan almost unprecedented international visibility,” he said.

That increased visibility – and enhanced cooperation with the US – has followed China’s mounting pressure on the island, which sits fewer than 110 miles (177 kilometers) from the mainland coast.

China’s Communist Party claims the self-governing island democracy as its own despite never having controlled it, and has vowed to take the island, by force if necessary.

The party has undertaken a sweeping expansion of its military capabilities over the past decade under leader Xi Jinping – and ramped up its pervasive economic, diplomatic and military pressure on Taiwan.

That’s driven concerns, among some in Washington, that Beijing is preparing for an invasion, though China’s official language still suggests that scenario is not its preferred option for achieving the claimed goal of “reunification.”

It is those pressures – and how to support Taiwan against unilateral actions by Beijing – that are likely to be on the table when Tsai, McCarthy and a bipartisan group of US lawmakers sit down on Wednesday.

Congress has been a pillar of increasing American support for Taiwan in recent years. Lawmakers regularly visit the island and drive bipartisan legislation enhancing support and cooperation.

While the US switched its diplomatic relations to Beijing decades ago, it maintains unofficial ties with Taiwan and is bound by law to provide the democratic island with the means to defend itself.

Under Washington’s longstanding “One China” policy, the US acknowledges China’s position that Taiwan is part of China, but has never officially recognized Beijing’s claim to the island of 23 million.

Though McCarthy does not have Pelosi’s decades-long record of advocacy regarding China, the California Republican is now a leading voice pushing for closer scrutiny of Beijing, and meeting Tsai could help him to burnish that image.

Last month, McCarthy told reporters that meeting Tsai in the US would not impact whether he travels to Taiwan in the future – something he had earlier said he wanted to do.

Fighter jets of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Eastern Theater Command conduct joint combat training exercises around Taiwan on August 7, 2022 in this photo released by Xinhua News Agency. Gong Yulong/Xinhua/AP

Beijing watching

A meeting in California, on US soil, is widely seen as less likely to provoke Beijing than a McCarthy visit to Taiwan.

Pelosi’s trip – the first from a lawmaker of that rank to the island in 25 years – generated a fever pitch of nationalist and anti-US rhetoric in mainland China.

This time, so far, domestic conversation in China’s heavily controlled media sphere has been significantly muted.

But the stakes remain high – including for Beijing itself – over how it responds, analysts say.

As Taiwan prepares for a presidential election in January, a fierce response could push voters away from Taiwan’s main opposition party Kuomintang (KMT), widely seen as more friendly toward Beijing.

It could also jar with another high profile trip happening now: a tour of mainland China from former Taiwan president and senior KMT member Ma Ying-jeou, the first visit from a current or former Taiwan leader since the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.

Ma’s tour is a “once in a half a century opportunity to send a conciliatory message between the two sides, Beijing shouldn’t want to tank that,” said Sung, the political scientist.

China is also acutely aware that its actions toward Taiwan are under a significantly brighter global spotlight following the invasion of Ukraine by Russian President Vladimir Putin, a close diplomatic partner of Xi. Putin’s rhetoric over Ukraine has echoes of how Xi speaks of Taiwan.

Beijing has recently sought to position itself as an agent of peace in that conflict – especially as it aims to repair frayed ties with Europe.

This week, as Tsai is expected to meet with McCarthy, French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will head to China – an important opportunity that Xi may not want to overshadow with military posturing.

An aggressive response also risks stoking confrontation with the US, not yet six months after Xi and US President Joe Biden called to enhance communication during a face-to-face meeting in Bali.

“(A less overtly aggressive response) would imply that Beijing does not wish to escalate tension with the US to a level that can risk getting out of hand,” said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London.

“A reset in US-China ties is not on the agenda, but an easing of tension is not beyond the realm of possibility.”

World.title: UK Greens leader seeks rule change after party declares Zionism is racism
World.content:
Zack Polanski calls for internal rule reforms to give party leaders greater control over policy after Zionism vote.

Zack Polanski, the leader of the United Kingdom’s Green Party, has proposed a potential overhaul of his party’s democratic mechanisms, calling for the leader to have larger control over strategic direction.

The appeal came in an article published in The Guardian on Sunday after party members passed a motion declaring that Zionism is racism at their annual conference on October 4 in a divisive vote.

Polanski also failed to grab a parliamentary seat in the wake of the row with Israel in a by-election.

The Labour Party won the election for the parliamentary seat vacated by former leader Keir Starmer in Holborn and St Pancras on Friday, fending off a strong challenge from the left-wing Green Party in a boost for British Prime Minister Andy Burnham.

“Our party democracy must now evolve to meet that – creating wider engagement for members, giving leaders more responsibility to set the party’s strategic direction, and making our processes as robust and accessible as possible,” he wrote.

“Above all, that unity must be deployed in the service of changing this country for the better,” the Green Party leader added.

Criticism over vote on motion

Polanski also replied to the criticisms of him for not participating in the vote on the motion on Zionism.

“I have been asked why I was not present for the vote. The answer is that my priority was fighting a hugely consequential by-election for our party,” he said, adding that he put all his “energy into the race in Holborn and St Pancras”.

He admitted that some members feel “let down” by his decision not to make an appearance there.



The Green Party’s motion, which called for “Palestinian liberation, the right of return, Boycott, Divestment and Sanctions (BDS), and a full arms embargo against Israel” was criticised by Jewish groups, other parties and most Green Party MPs.

After conceding defeat in the fiercely contested by-election, Polanski answered his critics, saying he would stay on as leader.

He was barred from entering Israel after his party backed a motion to define Zionism as racism.

World.title: Two killed near Israeli-occupied area in south Lebanon
World.content:
Despite a ceasefire agreement reached between Israel and Lebanon in June, Israeli attacks continue.

Share Two killed near Israeli-occupied area in south Lebanon on social media

Two men have been killed in southern Lebanon’s Bint Jbeil district while taking part in an annual olive harvest, according to Lebanese state media and local authorities, as attacks by Israel continue.

One of the men died Sunday in the village of Froun from a munition left behind by recent fighting and the other in Yater as a result of Israeli shelling that “targeted the outskirts of the town while he was inspecting his land and olive harvest”, according to the official National News Agency (NNA).

The Lebanese army blamed Israeli tank fire and called the ongoing attacks “a flagrant breach of existing agreements”.

Afterwards, the Yater municipality urged residents “to avoid the outskirts of the town and refrain from crossing the earthen barrier separating some unsafe neighbourhoods” for fear of Israeli attacks.

In Froun, the NNA reported that “a foreign object” left over from previous Israeli operations exploded and killed the man, who was an engineer, as he and others tended their trees.

The engineer had come down from Beirut, where he lives, for the harvest, Froun mayor Hassan Bazzi told AFP.

The incident prompted local residents to call off the harvest and wait for “the Lebanese army to complete the decontamination of the village”, Bazzi said.

Displaced people

Since an agreement between Lebanon and Israel was struck in June, violence in the south has lessened, but not stopped.

Lebanon was pulled into conflict on March 2, when Hezbollah struck Israel in support of Tehran during the US-Israel war on Iran. Subsequently, Israel launched a bombing campaign and a ground invasion that authorities say have killed more than 4,300.



In August, Lebanon’s Prime Minister Nawaf Salam accused Israel of intentionally targeting homes and civilian infrastructure across the country. The International Organization for Migration (IOM) recorded nearly 350,000 internally displaced people in late August, a sign of the worsening displacement crisis.

Volunteers from the nearby town of Jebchit and locals came to help their southern neighbours with the harvest in an act of solidarity.

“From north to south, one people and one land,” said organiser Ahmad Chahhal.
