World.title: Houthi strike on Riyadh Airport kills 12, injures 309 as Saudi Arabia vows retaliation
World.content:
A missile strike on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, killed 12 people and injured 309 others, prompting the Saudi-led coalition to threaten a decisive response against Yemen’s Ansar Allah rebels (popularly called the Houthis) amid escalating regional tensions.

Al Jazeera reports that the Sunday attack was the deadliest on Saudi soil in more than a decade. Some of the injured were reported to be in critical condition.

The Saudi-led coalition blamed the Iran-backed Houthis for the attack, describing it as a “full-fledged war crime” because of the deaths and injuries among civilian passengers and airport personnel.

The strike comes amid renewed fighting between the Houthis and forces loyal to Yemen’s internationally recognised government, which is backed by Saudi Arabia. The escalation has heightened concerns about a wider regional conflict, particularly after US President Donald Trump indicated that Washington could consider joining military action against the group.

Passengers flee as airport is hit

Witnesses described scenes of panic at the airport following the strike, with passengers running for safety as people were injured.

One passenger told AFP that they were at Gate 403 when the adjacent Gate 401 area was hit.

“I saw 401 hit, I saw injured in front of my eyes. Everyone was running,” the witness said.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Saudi Arabia’s General Authority of Civil Aviation said the fatalities included four Saudi nationals, two Bangladeshis and one citizen each from the United States, Egypt, Jordan, Syria, Palestine and Sudan.

Airport operations were suspended following the incident, while authorities began assessing the damage.

The scale of the casualties also prompted health officials to mobilise additional medical personnel to respond to what a medical source described as a serious emergency.

Two doctors told AFP that some of the injured were pilgrims travelling to Mecca.

Houthis warn airlines against using Saudi airports

Following the attack, the Houthis renewed their warning to airlines, airport workers and travellers against using Saudi airports.

The group urged those concerned to take its warning seriously and said Saudi Arabia bore responsibility for what it described as failed interception efforts.

The warning signals the possibility of further attacks on Saudi aviation infrastructure as hostilities intensify between the group and Saudi-backed Yemeni forces.

The renewed violence follows the breakdown of a United Nations-brokered truce that had helped keep large-scale fighting largely contained since 2022.

The latest developments threaten to undermine diplomatic efforts to end Yemen’s prolonged conflict, which has caused widespread displacement and a severe humanitarian crisis.

Saudi Arabia faces pressure to retaliate

The Saudi-led coalition has vowed a decisive response to the airport attack, raising the prospect of further military operations against Houthi positions in Yemen.

Dania Thafer, executive director of the Gulf International Forum, said Saudi Arabia would likely respond forcefully but suggested that Riyadh would prefer to avoid a prolonged escalation.

She said the Houthis’ actions posed challenges not only to Saudi national security but also to international maritime security.

The conflict, she argued, had expanded beyond a series of retaliatory attacks, with implications for regional stability and international shipping.

Saudi Arabia has previously led a military coalition against the Houthis, intervening in Yemen’s civil war in March 2015 in support of the internationally recognised government.

Trump considers possible US military involvement

The attack has also raised questions about the extent of possible US involvement in the conflict.

US President Donald Trump said on Saturday that Washington was considering whether to join military action against the Houthis.

“We may. We’re going to look at it,” he told reporters.

The US president also said he intended to speak with Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, describing the airport attack as “not acceptable”.

According to media reports cited in the coverage, the United States has provided intelligence-sharing, target-identification and planning assistance for the latest Saudi-backed offensive.

Washington previously supported the Saudi-led campaign in Yemen with intelligence, logistical assistance and weapons, although it did not directly participate in the coalition’s air strikes during the initial intervention.

In 2021, however, the administration of former US President Joe Biden ended support for the Saudi-led offensive, citing the devastating humanitarian consequences of the war.

Yemen conflict threatens wider regional stability

The airport strike underscores the risk that renewed fighting in Yemen could develop into a broader confrontation involving regional and international powers.

The Houthis have maintained their opposition to the Saudi-backed Yemeni government and have repeatedly threatened targets they consider linked to their adversaries.

Saudi Arabia, meanwhile, faces pressure to protect its territory and critical infrastructure while avoiding a return to a prolonged military campaign.

With Washington considering its next steps and the Saudi-led coalition threatening retaliation, the latest attack could further complicate efforts to restore a lasting ceasefire and secure a political settlement to Yemen’s conflict.

The escalation also raises concerns about the security of civilian aviation and international maritime routes, both of which could be affected if the hostilities spread beyond Yemen’s borders.

World.title: CDS orders extension of aerial intelligence to troubled North-west, North-central theatres
World.content:
The Chief of Defence Staff (CDS), Olufemi Oluyede, has directed the Defence Space Administration (DSA) to extend its “space-based” intelligence and surveillance support to ongoing military operations in the North-west and North-central theatres.

The spokesperson for the DSA, Funmilayo Bamisaye, disclosed this in a statement on Sunday, noting that the directive, given on Friday during the DSA’s 12th anniversary in Abuja, was aimed at enhancing operational effectiveness and troops’ situational awareness.

Mr Oluyede said the aerial support is already aiding troops of Operation Hadin Kai, a joint task force in the North-east. Its extension is expected to bolster joint forces of Operation Fansan Yamma in the North-west and Operation Savannah Shield in the North-central.

“As we speak now, they are supporting Operation Hadin Kai, and I have given instructions that they should extend that to Operation Fansan Yamma in the North-West and Operation Savannah Shield in the North-Central,” Mr Oluyede, a Nigerian Army general, was quoted as saying.

The defence chief commended the military agency for its “contributions to military operations through space-based intelligence, surveillance and communications capabilities.”

Mr Oluyede also urged the DSA to prioritise indigenous research, technological innovation and human capital development. He also called for stronger collaboration with academic institutions, industries and relevant national agencies to develop resilient space capabilities.

According to the defence chief, systems must be developed, field-tested and refined to meet operational requirements while remaining compatible with existing military structures and equipment.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Mr Oluyede lauded the DSA’s strides, including the launch of DELSAT-1, Nigeria’s military satellite launched in 2022, the Special Intelligence Infrastructure, an enabling framework for DELSAT-1, and the Modular Earth Observation Outpost station at the headquarters of Operation Hadin Kai.

He said these initiatives had strengthened Nigeria’s defence space architecture and brought specialised intelligence support closer to operational commanders.

Mr Oluyede also welcomed the commencement of academic activities at the Defence Space School in Delta State, describing indigenous expertise and technological development as essential to strengthening Nigeria’s capacity to harness space for national security and development.

The DSA boss, Philip Ilodibia, corroborated the defence chief, saying modern warfare increasingly depends on timely intelligence, situational awareness, secure communications and effective coordination across multiple operational domains.

Mr Ilodibia, a major general, noted that DSA has progressively developed capabilities to support the operational requirements of the Armed Forces and other security agencies since its establishment in 2014.

He said the DSA’s success should be measured by the operational challenges it resolved, the decisions it enabled and the strategic advantages it delivered.

The DSA boss called for stronger synergy among the Nigerian Army, Nigerian Navy and Nigerian Air Force, stressing that space-enabled intelligence, surveillance, communications and geospatial capabilities could improve joint situational awareness, interoperability and operational effectiveness.

He also advocated sustained collaboration between the National Space Research and Development Agency (NASRDA) and the Nigerian Communications Satellite Limited (NigComSat) to strengthen indigenous space capabilities.

Gabriel Olonisakin, a former CDS under late President Muhammadu Buhari, welcomed Nigeria’s plan to strengthen space-based intelligence. However, he noted that it requires sustained investment.

Mr Olonisakin, a retired general, referenced the Russia-Ukraine war, highlighting the growing role of space technology in modern conflicts, particularly cyberattacks on satellite communications infrastructure and the use of satellite imagery to monitor troop movements.

He urged the DSA to leverage strategic partnerships to develop sovereign space capabilities and strengthen national security.

World.title: Enugu govt condemns attack on NDC members
World.content:
The Enugu State Government has condemned Saturday’s attack on members of the Nigeria Democratic Party (NDC) at two locations in Enugu, stating that no one died during the attacks.

The government also dismissed reports that a party member, Ifeanyi Nworie, died during the incident at the party’s state secretariat, describing the claim as false.

Chidiebere Onyia, the secretary to the Enugu State Government (SSG), disclosed this while briefing reporters at the Government House, Enugu, on Sunday.

Mr Onyia said the incidents occurred at the Akanu Ibiam International Airport and the NDC State Secretariat in the Government Reserved Area, Enugu, on Saturday.

He explained that the airport incident was a matter between the party and federal authorities, adding that the state government had taken steps to establish what transpired.

According to him, the NDC had published a notice inviting its supporters and members of the public to its proposed “Grand Statewide Campaign Flag-off 2026” at the airport.

He said the police had advised the party to obtain approval from the Federal Airports Authority of Nigeria (FAAN) before security personnel could be deployed for the event.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“Our findings revealed that the NDC did not secure FAAN’s approval to host a grand statewide rally at the airport.

“Security agencies, therefore, advised the organisers to reconsider the event, but the party went ahead to mobilise its members to the facility.

“The attempt to forcibly gain entry into the airport resulted in a face-off between party members and airport authorities, prompting security agencies to intervene and restore order,” he said.

On the incident at the party’s state secretariat, Mr Onyia said security reports confirmed a violent clash, which the police are investigating.

He disclosed that a 43-year-old man, identified as Ifeanyi Nworie, sustained a gunshot wound during the incident.

“Our findings showed that Nworie was rushed to the Enugu State University Teaching Hospital, Park Lane, where he was stabilised before being transferred to the National Orthopaedic Hospital, Enugu, for further examination.

“We can, therefore, authoritatively report that there were no deaths as falsely claimed by some reports and NDC leaders,” he said.

Enugu govt reacts to allegations

The SSG reiterated the state government’s commitment to protecting lives and property, irrespective of political affiliation.

He said Governor Peter Mbah’s administration had invested heavily in security to sustain peace and create an enabling environment for investment and economic development.

“The Enugu State Government strongly condemns any form of violence, including politically motivated violence.

“We welcome healthy debate, freedom of association and peaceful assembly, but these rights must be exercised responsibly.

“Political parties should be models of good conduct, while politicians should embrace decorum and issue-based campaigns ahead of the 2027 general elections,” Mr Onyia said.

He also dismissed allegations that the Chief Security Officer (CSO) to the governor supervised the shooting at the NDC secretariat.

According to him, the governor’s CSO was with Mr Mbah at the Teachers’ Grassroots Movement mega rally held at Okpara Square, Enugu, at the time of the incident.

Mr Onyia accused some opposition figures of attempting to portray Enugu as unsafe and the government as intolerant of political opposition.

He alleged that internal leadership disputes among opposition parties sometimes led to violent clashes, which the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) was later blamed for.

The SSG cited the 12 September incident at Obuofia in Nkanu West Local Government Area, saying investigations had identified suspects who were being prosecuted by the police.

He further alleged that the government had uncovered plans by some opposition elements to recruit armed thugs and bandits to create insecurity in the state ahead of the 2027 general elections.

Mr Onyia maintained that the Mbah administration had no reason to undermine opposition activities, expressing confidence that the governor’s performance would earn him re-election in 2027.

(NAN)

World.title: International Day of the Girl Child, By Obiageli “Oby” Ezekwesili
World.content:
A girl who learns is a girl who is not a bride. Today the world is asked to end child marriage and invest in girls’ rights. I join that call wearing three hats: as a member of the advisory council behind Columbia University’s report Accelerating Efforts to End Child Marriage; as Civil Society Representative on the Steering Committee of the African Union’s Decade of Accelerated Action for the Transformation of Education and Skills Development in Africa (2025–2034); and as the leader of Human Capital Africa, an organisation that has spent years arguing that Africa’s human capital crisis begins in the early-grade classroom.

The numbers are clear. UNICEF’s 2026 estimates show that about one in five girls worldwide is married before 18. That adds up to roughly 650 million women and girls alive today who were married as children. More than 12 million girls are still married each year, about one every three seconds, and sub-Saharan Africa has the highest prevalence at 31 per cent.

In Nigeria, 23.6 million women and girls were married before 18, the largest number in West and Central Africa. In parts of the North the situation is a national emergency: in Jigawa, 78 per cent of women aged 20–49 were first married before 18, and 63 per cent of women left school to marry.

The cost of inaction is high. Our Columbia report includes new analysis by the Center for Global Development. It estimates losses of up to $175 billion a year, or almost $2.5 trillion by 2040, from lost productivity and higher health risks caused by child marriage. The report also warns that aid cuts, weakening global commitment to women’s rights, and rising conflict could slow or reverse progress.

Child marriage is not a side issue in development. It drains a nation’s human capital directly.

Progress is possible. An estimated 68 million child marriages have been averted over the past 25 years, through girls’ education, legal reform and social protection. The evidence on what works is strong:

Each year of secondary education lowers a girl’s chance of marrying before 18 by five percentage points or more.

In Niger, when the government removed the direct costs of middle school for rural girls, each additional year in secondary school was associated with a 19 percentage point lower probability of marriage.

If every African girl completed secondary education, child marriage could be almost eliminated.

Where HCA’s mission and this campaign meet. A girl cannot stay in secondary school if she never learned to read. Today, 89 per cent of children in sub-Saharan Africa are in learning poverty, unable to read and understand a simple text by age ten. A girl who cannot read by ten falls behind, then drops out.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Once she is out of school, she is at the greatest risk of marriage. That is why we say schooling is not learning. Foundational literacy and numeracy are the first and cheapest protection a girl has.

At the Columbia launch I said that community programmes and advocacy are not enough on their own. Governments must lead. On this Day of the Girl, Human Capital Africa calls on African governments to:

Make foundational learning a girl-protection policy. Every girl should be reading with comprehension by age ten, using proven methods such as structured pedagogy and Teaching at the Right Level.

Every girl should be reading with comprehension by age ten, using proven methods such as structured pedagogy and Teaching at the Right Level. Guarantee the move into secondary school. Remove fees, uniform and transport costs for girls, especially in rural communities with high rates of child marriage.

Remove fees, uniform and transport costs for girls, especially in rural communities with high rates of child marriage. Enforce 18 as the minimum age of marriage in law and in practice , in every state and every community, with traditional and religious leaders as partners.

, in every state and every community, with traditional and religious leaders as partners. Fund this domestically. As foreign aid shrinks, African budgets and African philanthropy must take over.

As foreign aid shrinks, African budgets and African philanthropy must take over. Measure and publish. Track girls’ learning, their transition to secondary school, and child marriage rates in national accountability systems. The AU Decade of Education gives Africa ten years and a continental mandate. As a member of its Steering Committee, I will press for girls’ learning and retention to be at the centre of how the Decade’s success is measured. A Decade that does not end child marriage will not have transformed African education.

The Columbia report sets a realistic target: cutting child marriage prevalence from one in five to one in seven within five years. Africa can lead the way to that target, but only if we treat every girl’s classroom as the place where her childhood is protected.

Any girl-child should be a student, not a bride. She should learn, then lead.

Obiageli “Oby” Ezekwesili

Founder, Human Capital Africa

Former Nigeria’s Minister of Education and Vice President for Africa Region, World Bank.

World.title: Messi’s retirement: FCTA ex-spokesman proposes FIFA Over-40 World Cup
World.content:
A former spokesman for the Federal Capital Territory Administration (FCTA), Nosike Ogbuenyi, has asked the Fédération Internationale de Football Association (FIFA) to introduce an Over-40 World Cup so that retired international footballers can keep showcasing their skills.

Mr Ogbuenyi said he submitted a proposal to FIFA through the Nigeria Football Federation (NFF) secretariat in Abuja on Thursday.

He said the competition, proposed for players aged 40 to 65, would give fans more opportunities to watch some of football’s most celebrated players long after they retire from conventional professional football.

“The introduction of the FIFA Over-40 World Cup will enable the football-loving world to continue to watch the best of all times on the field of play for a longer period,” he said.

Mr Ogbuenyi, who served twice as special assistant on media to the FCT minister, said the proposal was inspired partly by the retirement of some of the game’s biggest names and the difficulty fans face in keeping up with former stars after their playing careers.

“Here in Nigeria, we have seen our most talented and best of all times retire and become less visible publicly. We, the football fans, find it difficult to keep track of our legends and stars like Jay Jay Okocha, Kanu Nwankwo, Victor Ikpeba, Emmanuel Amunike, Obafemi Martins, Vincent Enyeama and John Obi Mikel,” he said.

Beyond Nigeria, he listed several former and current players whom he believes fans would like to see return to the pitch in a veterans’ competition. They include Lionel Messi, Cristiano Ronaldo, Angel Di Maria, Gabriel Batistuta, Michael Owen, David Beckham, Andres Iniesta, Sergio Ramos, Xavi, Zlatan Ibrahimovic, Ronaldinho, Ronaldo de Lima, Roberto Carlos, Didier Drogba, Samuel Eto’o, Zinedine Zidane and Thierry Henry.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Others on his list include Oliver Kahn, Miroslav Klose, Manuel Neuer, Lothar Matthäus and Keisuke Honda.

Proposed rules, benefits

Mr Ogbuenyi said the proposed tournament could promote fitness among former players, provide an additional income source, and keep them in the public eye after retirement.

He also argued it could help former internationals stay connected to their countries and contribute to developing younger players and the wider game.

According to him, the competition would give professional footballers a clearer pathway after leaving the physically demanding environment of youth and senior football, while allowing supporters to follow their idols for longer.

He further suggested that the tournament could discourage age cheating in youth and senior football categories by giving players another age-based competition to aspire to.

On eligibility, Mr Ogbuenyi proposed that players be between 40 and 65 years old and have represented their countries at the senior international level. He also said players should retire from senior international football before representing their countries in the veterans’ competition.

He argued the tournament could be commercially viable for FIFA, citing potential revenue from television rights and corporate partnerships, given the prospect of bringing together some of the game’s most recognisable names.

Why now?

Mr Ogbuenyi said Messi’s retirement, the Argentine forward and eight-time Ballon d’Or winner, created an opportunity to draw attention to his proposal.

“I have found this period of the retirement of the eight-time Ballon d’Or winner, Lionel Messi, the most auspicious time to submit this proposal. As the iconic Argentine footballer bowed out after a 21-year international soccer career on Tuesday, 6 October 2026, I kept wondering what the football world would look like if FIFA created a new tournament that would allow talismanic players such as Messi, Cristiano Ronaldo, Jay Jay Okocha, Kanu Nwankwo and others to continue to exhibit their skills on the global stage.

“In fact, I first started nursing this idea when Jay Jay Okocha, Nigeria’s most adored football prodigy, retired about 15 years ago. But I had to wait for this moment of Messi’s retirement to submit the proposal because of the anticipated global momentum.”

He said he had no personal interest in the proposal and was motivated by his passion for the game.

“I am not making any claims for bringing up this idea and putting it across through this proposal to FIFA. I am just writing as a football fan who wants the world to be happier through more football games entertainment.”

Mr Ogbuenyi expressed confidence that FIFA would evaluate and approve the proposal, which he believes could offer another way to celebrate former players and promote the game.

He currently works as an assistant editor at PREMIUM TIMES. He has previously worked with Daily Champion, The Comet, The Sun, and ThisDay newspapers.

World.title: La Liga: Isco’s Betis rise back above Real Madrid to third
World.content:
Real Betis’ Spanish midfielder #22 Isco (R) celebrates with Real Betis’ Colombian forward #09 Juan Hernandez scoring his team’s fourth goal during the Spanish league football match between Real Betis and CA Osasuna at Benito Villamarin Stadium in Seville on October 11, 2026. (Photo by JORGE GUERRERO / AFP)

Veteran playmaker Isco struck twice to help Real Betis climb back into third place in La Liga with a 5-2 win over Osasuna on Sunday.

The Andalucian side moved a point above Real Madrid, fourth, and level with second place Atletico Madrid, trailing leaders Barca by five points.

Manuel Pellegrini’s side claimed a sixth league win from eight matches with an exciting display of attacking football at La Cartuja stadium, where they are playing until their Benito Villamarin home is renovated, likely 2028.

Former Real Madrid midfielder Isco, 34, netted from the penalty spot after a foul on Rodrigo Riquelme, and Ez Abde doubled the hosts lead after half-an-hour with a cool finish.

Ante Budimir’s own goal gave Betis their third after half-time, before the Croatian striker netted at the correct and Raul Garcia added another to give Osasuna a fighting chance.

Isco capitalised on a loose ball in the box to grab his second and Jose Morante bagged a fifth in stoppage time to close out Betis’s big win.

“Football is never truly under control,” said Pellegrini after his side almost let their three-goal lead slip.

“As soon as the pace drops, the other team can pull level.”

The former Manchester City coach also praised Isco after his brace.

“He has spectacular quality and a maturity as a player that allows him to perform at whatever level he wants to,” added Pellegrini.

Elsewhere Valencia, 19th, earned a point in a 2-2 draw at Racing Santander under new coach Javier Aguirre.

Real Sociedad defeated Deportivo La Coruna 3-2 in another entertaining battle.

The Basque side, sixth, eased into a three-goal lead Mario Soriano pulled one back for the visitors in San Sebastian to spark a Depor fight back.

They were given further encouragement when Real Sociedad’s Pablo Marin was sent off in the 66th minute for a foul on Nsongo Bil in the box and Yeremay Hernandez netted from the penalty spot.

Both teams finished with 10 men after Lorenzo Amatucci brought down Mikel Oyarzabal as the last man, and Depor could not find an equaliser.

On Saturday Liga leaders Barcelona beat Getafe 3-0 to prolong their perfect start to the season, with eight wins from eight league games.

Hansi Flick’s side are followed by second place Atletico Madrid, who snatched a late 2-1 win at Alaves, while Jose Mourinho’s Real Madrid scraped a 1-0 victory over Villarreal despite Vinicius Junior’s red card for hair-pulling.

World.title: Tinubu to flag off 376km Niger highway Tuesday
World.content:
By Luminous Jannamike

ABUJA – President Bola Tinubu will on Tuesday flag off the reconstruction and dualisation of the 376km Lambata–Bida–Mokwa–Makera–Kontagora Federal Highway in Niger State, a project expected to improve transport links and boost agricultural and commercial activities across North-Central Nigeria.

For farmers struggling to move produce to markets, traders transporting goods and commuters travelling between communities, the highway could ease movement and open up economic opportunities, provided the project is delivered to the required standard.

In a statement by Dr Abiodun Essiet, Senior Special Assistant to the President on Community Engagement for the North-Central region, the project was described as a major infrastructure initiative under Tinubu’s Renewed Hope Agenda.

The flag-off, scheduled for noon in Bida, is expected to attract the Minister of Works, Senator David Umahi; Niger State Governor, Mohammed Umaru Bago; and other federal and state government officials.

The statement said the highway would strengthen the movement of people, agricultural produce and commercial goods across the region.

“Beyond road construction, the project represents an investment in the economic connections that link farmers to markets, businesses to customers and communities to wider commercial opportunities,” it said.

Niger State’s agricultural economy stands to benefit from improved access to markets, while transport operators and businesses could gain from better road conditions, reduced journey delays and safer travel.

The project aligns with the Renewed Hope Agenda’s infrastructure priorities, which identify road development as a driver of economic growth and national development.

However, the statement did not disclose the contract sum, contractor, construction timetable or expected completion date.

It said the project’s success would ultimately depend on what is delivered to road users and host communities.

“The ultimate measure of the project’s success will be the delivery of a durable highway that improves transportation, strengthens economic connections and serves the needs of communities along the corridor,” the statement said.

World.title: Tinubu to Aspirants: Don’t make promises you cannot fund
World.content:
Tinubu

By Nwafor Sunday Polycarp, Online News Editor

President Bola Tinubu has challenged those seeking to lead Nigeria to explain the cost of their campaign promises, how they intend to implement them and whether they can sustain them.

Tinubu said every government commitment must be backed by a credible plan and be financially sustainable to avoid passing the burden to Nigerians and future generations.

The President stated this in a post on his X platform on Sunday, stressing that leaders must balance the need to provide immediate relief with the responsibility to protect the future of the country’s children.

“As President, I have a duty to provide relief today without compromising our children’s future.

“Every commitment must be sustainable and backed by a credible plan. That responsibility guides our decisions, including the difficult ones,” he said.

Tinubu added that political promises were easy to make when their costs could be deferred, leaving citizens and future generations to bear the consequences.

“Anyone seeking to lead Nigeria should be prepared to explain what their promises will cost, how they will deliver them, and whether they can sustain them.

“Promises are easy to make when the costs can be postponed, leaving Nigerians and future generations to pay the bill,” he said.

The President also referred to the stories of some Nigerians, including Blessing, Ada, Abigail and Kabir, saying their experiences demonstrated the impact of government investments on people’s daily lives.

He also acknowledged a request from Emmanuel, saying it reminded him of the work still required to expand access to essential services.

“Emmanuel, your request reminds me of the work still ahead. I know many more Nigerians like you are waiting for these services,” Tinubu said.

He stressed the need to continue expanding access to affordable transportation across the country, noting that the Federal Government would work with state governments to achieve the objective.

“Our responsibility is to keep expanding access until affordable transportation becomes a reality for more communities across our country.

“That is the work we will continue in collaboration with the States,” he added.

World.title: Adelabu denies calling on Nigerians to reject APC
World.content:
Adelabu

Says viral video is an old 2022 interview taken out of context

The media office of former Minister of Power, Chief Adebayo Adelabu, has dismissed a viral report claiming that he called on Nigerians to reject the All Progressives Congress (APC), describing the allegation as false and misleading.

In a statement issued in October 2026, Adelabu’s media office said the video circulating on social media was an excerpt from an interview he granted in 2022, when he was the governorship candidate of the Accord Party in Oyo State.

It said Adelabu did not call on Nigerians to reject the APC, urging the public to disregard what it described as a deliberate attempt to misrepresent his position and create friction between him, President Bola Tinubu and the party’s leadership.

According to the statement, Adelabu had consistently maintained his loyalty to the APC and the President despite controversies surrounding the party’s governorship nomination process in Oyo State.

The former minister, who served under the APC-led Federal Government, reportedly left public office to pursue his governorship ambition in the state.

The statement alleged that the APC nomination process was marred by controversies, including the alleged imposition of a preferred aspirant and the failure to transparently release the primary election results.

It said Adelabu had nevertheless maintained that he had no intention of leaving the party and that his political ambition was not a do-or-die affair.

“His position has been consistent: loyalty does not preclude the demand for fairness, transparency and adherence to democratic principles,” the statement said.

It argued that Adelabu’s criticism of the party’s internal electoral process should not be interpreted as a call for Nigerians to reject the APC.

The media office explained that the 2022 interview reflected Adelabu’s view that political parties had disappointed Nigerians and that voters should focus on the credibility and character of individual candidates.

It added that the comments were made in the context of the political environment at the time and did not amount to opposition to the APC or Tinubu’s presidential ambition.

The statement also described Adelabu’s relationship with Tinubu as longstanding, saying it was based on mutual respect and trust.

It challenged those circulating the video to publish the full, unedited interview rather than selectively extracting portions of it.

The media office further claimed that Adelabu had not granted any media interview since the conclusion of the controversial APC governorship nomination process in Oyo State in which he made the alleged statement.

It urged APC members, the media and the public to verify information before sharing it, warning against the spread of unsubstantiated claims.

“Chief Adelabu remains committed to the APC, loyal to Mr President and supportive of the party’s broader political objectives,” the statement said.

The media office advised the public to rely on authentic statements from Adelabu or his authorised representatives.

World.title: Top 10 highest-paid content creators in 2026 – Forbes ranking
World.content:
MrBeast has emerged as the world’s highest-paid content creator, earning an estimated $300 million as social media influencers expand their businesses into entertainment, technology, consumer products and streaming.

According to Forbes’ 2026 Top Creators ranking, the 50 creators featured on the list collectively generated $1.02 billion, representing a 20 per cent increase from $853 million recorded in the previous year’s ranking.

The publication, edited by Steven Bertoni, with reporting by Zoya Hasan and Alexandra York, alongside Sofia Chierchio and Martina Di Licosa, highlighted how digital creators are transforming their online popularity into lucrative business empires.

From YouTube personalities and TikTok stars to podcasters and entrepreneurs, the creators are increasingly competing with traditional entertainment companies through original productions, brand partnerships, merchandise and investments.

Forbes noted that creators are also making significant inroads into Hollywood and streaming. Examples include films developed from online content that have generated hundreds of millions of dollars at the box office, as well as digital personalities securing deals with major streaming platforms.

Here are the 10 highest-paid creators featured in the Forbes 2026 ranking, based on their reported earnings.

1. MrBeast — $300 million

Total followers: 873 million | Average engagement: 3.00%

Jimmy Donaldson, popularly known as MrBeast, tops the ranking with estimated earnings of $300 million.

He built his popularity through elaborate YouTube challenges, stunts and competitions before expanding into a business empire spanning entertainment, food, merchandise and technology.

His company, Beast Industries, oversees ventures including Feastables, Lunchly, analytics platform Viewstats, and toy and clothing licensing.

According to Forbes, his YouTube channels have more than 640 million subscribers and attract over five billion views annually.

MrBeast has also expanded into streaming with Beast Games on Amazon Prime Video, with its third season already in production at the time of the report.

In February 2026, Beast Industries acquired Step, a financial app designed to teach teenagers about investing and money management. Forbes also reported that the company had attracted venture investment at a valuation of $5 billion.

2. Dhar Mann — $65 million

Total followers: 171 million | Average engagement: 0.09%

Dhar Mann ranks second with estimated earnings of $65 million, driven by scripted videos that focus on life lessons, relationships and personal transformation.

His production team of approximately 200 people creates digital shows that, according to Forbes, generate nearly 300 million views in a typical week.

Mann’s content reaches audiences in 13 languages, helping him build a global following across social media platforms.

He has also expanded beyond short-form digital entertainment. His partnership with the NFL saw him serve as the league’s “Chief Kindness Officer” for Super Bowl LX, while a deal with Fox Entertainment will see him produce 40 vertical dramas over 18 months.

His business model demonstrates how creators can build production companies capable of supplying content to traditional broadcasters and emerging digital platforms.

3. Steven Bartlett — $52 million

Total followers: 38.7 million | Average engagement: 0.22%

British entrepreneur and podcast host Steven Bartlett ranks third, with estimated earnings of $52 million.

Bartlett is best known for The Diary of a CEO, an interview podcast that grew from a project he started at his kitchen table into a major media brand.

According to Forbes, his holding company, Steven.com, is valued at $425 million and has interests spanning media, publishing, live events and investments.

His commercial partnerships include Spotify, LinkedIn and Adobe. He has also invested in technology companies Replit and Lovable.

Bartlett continues to expand his television profile through Dragons’ Den, the investment programme in which entrepreneurs pitch business ideas to potential investors.

His success illustrates how podcasting can develop into a wider business involving advertising, investments and entertainment.

4. Markiplier — $38 million

Total followers: 76.8 million | Average engagement: 0.21%

Mark Edward Fischbach, known professionally as Markiplier, occupies fourth place with estimated earnings of $38 million.

Initially known for gaming videos and online entertainment, Markiplier has moved into filmmaking, demonstrating how established creators can use their digital audiences to support projects outside social media.

His self-funded and self-produced feature film, Iron Lung, screened in approximately 3,000 theatres across North America and generated $50 million at the box office, according to Forbes.

The creator also negotiated a 50-50 revenue split with theatres, an arrangement that gave him a direct stake in the film’s theatrical performance.

Beyond filmmaking, Markiplier continues to host the podcasts Distractible and Go! My Favorite Sports Team.

5. Rhett & Link — $37 million

Total followers: 45.6 million | Average engagement: 0.12%

Comedy duo Rhett McLaughlin and Link Neal rank fifth, with combined estimated earnings of $37 million.

The childhood friends are best known for Good Mythical Morning, their long-running YouTube talk show featuring food challenges, product reviews, trivia and discussions about popular culture.

Forbes reports that the programme produces approximately 240 episodes annually and attracts nearly 20 million viewers.

The duo also operates the Mythical Kitchen channel, which features the Last Meal series hosted by Josh Scherer. Guests have included Tom Hanks, Gordon Ramsay and Ed Sheeran.

Their expansion into Tubi and publishing, including their fourth food book, Spaghetti Head & Chicken Fingers, further demonstrates their ability to turn a digital entertainment brand into multiple revenue streams.

6. Charli D’Amelio — $18 million

Total followers: 209.8 million | Average engagement: 11.59%

TikTok star Charli D’Amelio ranks sixth with estimated earnings of $18 million.

She rose to global prominence through dance videos on TikTok and has since expanded her career into theatre, fashion and other forms of entertainment.

Following her Broadway run in & Juliet, D’Amelio returned to posting dance content and YouTube vlogs while maintaining major fashion partnerships.

She serves as a Prada ambassador and has appeared in campaigns for Kate Spade.

Her position on the list highlights the commercial value of a highly engaged social media audience, particularly for creators whose influence translates into brand partnerships and opportunities beyond digital platforms.

7. Druski — $20 million

Total followers: 38.5 million | Average engagement: 13.77%

Comedian and internet personality Druski, whose real name is Drew Desbordes, ranks seventh with estimated earnings of $20 million.

He gained recognition through comedy sketches shared on YouTube, TikTok and Instagram before expanding into mainstream advertising and television.

His commercial appearances include campaigns for T-Mobile and Dunkin’, while his collaborations have brought him alongside entertainment figures such as Kevin Hart, Timothée Chalamet, Jeff Bridges and Zoe Saldaña.

Forbes also highlighted his role as host of the BET Awards in June.

Druski’s career illustrates how internet comedy can serve as a launchpad for opportunities in advertising, live entertainment and mainstream media.

8. IShowSpeed — $30 million

Total followers: 184 million | Average engagement: 0.39%

Popular streamer IShowSpeed ranks eighth with estimated earnings of $30 million.

The creator, whose real name is Darren Watkins Jr., initially gained attention through gaming videos featuring titles such as NBA 2K and Fortnite.

His popularity grew significantly after clips of his energetic reactions and gaming outbursts went viral on TikTok.

He later diversified into football-related content, collaborating with global stars including Cristiano Ronaldo, before expanding into travel livestreams and videos.

His projects include Speed Does America and Speed Does Africa. His commercial partnerships include Dick’s Sporting Goods, Beats by Dre and Doritos.

Forbes also highlighted his World Cup 2026 Tour with FIFA as part of his expansion into football-related entertainment and global travel content.

9. Mark Rober — $30 million

Total followers: 90.7 million | Average engagement: 0.23%

Former NASA engineer and science communicator Mark Rober ranks ninth, with estimated earnings of $30 million.

Rober is known for highly produced YouTube videos that explain scientific concepts through experiments, engineering projects and elaborate stunts.

His content includes projects designed to teach physics through roller coasters, explore scientific approaches to escaping Alcatraz and demonstrate robotics in collaboration with football superstar Cristiano Ronaldo.

According to Forbes, his team of approximately 100 people produces episodes that can cost seven figures to make.

Rober also operates CrunchLabs, a business that sells science and engineering kits through a subscription model.

His work combines education and entertainment while attracting commercial partnerships with companies including Rivian, Google and Disney.

10. Codie Sanchez — $31 million

Total followers: 10 million | Average engagement: 0.37%

Entrepreneur and former journalist Codie Sanchez rounds out the top 10, with estimated earnings of $31 million.

Sanchez creates content focused on entrepreneurship, business ownership and investment opportunities, particularly in businesses that are often overlooked by technology-focused investors.

Her educational videos discuss ventures such as laundromats, vending machines and landscaping businesses, encouraging audiences to consider established industries that can generate recurring revenue.

She shares business advice across YouTube, Instagram and TikTok, with Forbes reporting that her content reaches more than seven million followers across these platforms.

Rather than focusing on get-rich-quick promises, Sanchez advocates acquiring and operating businesses as a route to building wealth.

Her position on the list highlights how financial education and practical business advice can become profitable creator-led enterprises.

Source: Forbes’ 2026 Top Creators ranking. Earnings and audience figures are Forbes-reported estimates and may reflect different measurement periods.

Vanguard News

World.title: Otti urges Abia residents to reject election-season promises by politicians
World.content:
Abia State Governor, Alex Otti

Gov. Alex Otti of Abia has urged voters to resist financial and material inducements from politicians, warning that such offers could undermine the state’s future in the 2027 general elections.

Otti gave the warning on Sunday at the 2nd Session of the 7th Synod of the Anglican Communion, Diocese of Aba Ngwa North, held at All Saints Anglican Cathedral, Abayi-Umuocham, Aba.

The governor, represented by his Chief of Staff, Dr Caleb Ajagba, charged citizens to prioritise long-term development over immediate material benefits offered by politicians.

He alleged that politicians responsible for the state’s challenges over 24 years were returning to seek voters’ support.

Otti warned against allowing such politicians to derail the progress his administration was pursuing.

“The people that created a problem that God now had to answer your prayer by sending someone after His own heart, are all over again.

“But the Bible says surely they shall proceed no further. Please, let us be careful.When God opens a door, may we not close it.

“Don’t use the ₦5,000, the ₦10,000, the wrapper or the rice they will give you and close the destiny of Abians for the next four years, because even prayer and fasting will not open it.

“May we not lose what God has given to us on the platter,” he said.

The governor also urged Christians to remain vigilant, warning that some politicians who previously neglected the Church were seeking its attention.

“Like we have been told the season is here again and politicians are everywhere and as the Bible says we are not ignorant of the devices of the enemy.

“These are devices, because many of them who have not been coming to church have started coming to church.

“Many of them who have not been accepting or taking your calls have suddenly started calling you. If you call them and you miss their call, they call you back. Those are devices,” he said.

Otti said the first three years of his administration had focused largely on laying a foundation for development, adding that the next four years, beginning in 2027, would prioritise consolidation.

“Those who build houses will understand that foundation-laying is the most crucial, and the foundation has been laid after 24 years of ruins.

“What will now be happening is consolidation and beauty will emerge.

“This present house (Abia State) you are seeing today, in the next four years, you will know that God has really come to tabernacle in the midst of man.

“Today Abia State has become a point of reference,” he said.

On the church’s development projects, Otti assured the congregation of his administration’s support towards their completion.

He, however, reiterated that public funds should be deployed to develop the state rather than finance religious projects.

The governor commended the guest speaker for delivering what he described as an appropriate and unadulterated message, urging Christians to verify information and examine issues critically before reaching conclusions.

He said the synod’s theme, “Don’t Just Absorb It; Think It Through,” drawn from Acts Chapter 17 verse 11 to 12, was relevant as the country approached another political season.

“As Christians, we have the capacity to change the negative narrative of this nation; especially our state,” he said.

Earlier, the Bishop of Aba Ngwa North Diocese, Anglican Communion, Dr Nathan Kanu, said the theme challenged Christians to move beyond hearing messages to examining issues prayerfully and responding wisely.

Kanu commended Otti for identifying with the church and supporting its activities, presented gifts to the governor’s representative and prayed for God’s blessings on his administration.

In his sermon, the Guest Speaker and Bishop of Ohaji/Egbema Diocese, Rt. Rev. Chidi Oparajiaku, urged Christians to think critically before taking action.

Speaking on: “The Bereans Wisdom,” with his text from Acts chapter 17 verse 12 and 15, Oparajiaku said the synod’s theme was timely and encouraged believers to examine messages rather than accept or reject them without reflection.

“The theme of the synod is very important and apt in this our time, it didn’t say throw it away, it says think through it,” he said.

Oparajiaku regretted that Christians, who were expected to demonstrate sound judgement, sometimes fell victim to deception.

“When members of the church know the Bible they would not be deceived.

“This is because the church refused to behave like the Bereans. The Bereans Christian never took everything for granted they always thought through whatever they heard,” he said.

The Bishop thanked God for giving Abia the opportunity to be governed by Otti, whom he credited with changing the state’s narrative.

The synod attracted dignitaries, including the Labour Party’s National Vice-Chairman, South-East, Hon. Ishmael Onuoha; state chairman, Sir Peter Azubuike; and Osisioma Local Government Area Mayor, Hon. Chidi Agu.

Others were the Special Assistant to the Governor on Special Duties, Dr George Chiedozie; Special Adviser to the Governor on Labour Matters, Godson Anucha; and Aba industrialist, Mr Bob Udeagha.

World.title: Peter Obi faults Tinubu’s 30-day petrol discount, calls policy reactive
World.content:
Obi

Presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress ((NDC), Peter Obi, has criticised the 30-day petrol discount announced by the President Bola Tinubu-led federal government, describing the initiative as a reactive policy that fails to address the economic hardship facing Nigerians.

Obi, in a post on X, said the temporary discount was an attempt to substitute “political optics for sound policy”, arguing that the government had failed to properly assess the effects of its economic reforms.

He said he delayed commenting on the announcement to allow time to assess its outcomes before concluding that the policy reflected what he described as a confused approach to governance.

Obi recalled that Tinubu removed the petrol subsidy on May 29, 2023, without adequate consultation or assessment of its potential impact on the economy and the livelihoods of ordinary Nigerians.

He also faulted the subsequent floating of the naira and tax reforms, saying the policies were poorly sequenced and implemented.

According to him, the combined effects of the policies included rising inflation, higher prices of goods and services, increasing poverty, unemployment and insecurity, as well as widening inequality and the migration of young Nigerians.

“Collectively, these policies stoked inflation in all sectors, pushing in most cases unbearable price hikes across board which placed severe shocks and other adverse consequences on Nigerians,” Obi said.

The former Anambra State governor accused the federal government of failing to conduct and publish detailed regulatory impact assessments of its policies.

He argued that such assessments would enable the government to consult stakeholders and citizens and develop more inclusive and sustainable economic strategies.

Obi also questioned the potential impact of the petrol discount, which he described as less than five per cent of fuel costs.

“What really does the President Bola Tinubu-led government want to achieve with a one-month discount of less than 5% on fuel cost. Will it reduce poverty, unemployment, insecurity, and inequality? Will it increase productivity and exports?” he asked.

He further questioned whether the initiative was intended to test public reaction to a possible restoration of subsidy or was politically motivated ahead of the 2027 elections.

Obi concluded his criticism by saying the government had raised too many questions about the policy without providing answers.

World.title: Mbah, Nnaji, Ohaa, 13 others make INEC list for Enugu governorship
World.content:
Gov. Peter Mbah, former Minister, Chief Uchenna Nnaji, and former Federal Permanent Secretary, Chief Chinyeaka Ohaa, are among 16 candidates listed for the 2027 Enugu governorship election.

The candidates, representing various political parties, are seeking to control the state’s Government House.

The News Agency of Nigeria reports that the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) displayed the final list at its Enugu headquarters on Sunday.

The document contains the personal credentials of all 16 candidates contesting the state’s top political office.

Mbah, the incumbent governor contesting on the platform of the All Progressives Congress (APC), will face Nnaji of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP).

Other contenders include Ohaa of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) and Chief Obodoeze Ocho of the African Democratic Congress (ADC).

The list also names Mr Edwin Alor of Accord, Prof. Jehu Nnaji of the New Nigeria Peoples Party (NNPP), and Mr Okwudilichukwu Ugwu of the Labour Party (LP).

Other candidates are Mr Nnamdi Ugwu of the Democratic Leadership Alliance (DLA), Mr Anthony Udeani of the Young Progressives Party (YPP), and Mr Afamefuna Ani of the Action Peoples Party (APP).

Mr Elvis Ugwoke of the Zenith Labour Party (ZLP), Mr Friday Iloka of the Social Democratic Party (SDP), and Mr Nnamdi Omeje of the Action Democratic Party (ADP) are also contesting.

The remaining candidates are Mr Ken Ikeh of the Allied Peoples Movement (APM), Chief Obioma Nnamani of the Because Of Our Tomorrow (BOOT) Party, and Mr Ndubuisi Okonkwo of the National Rescue Movement (NRM).

The candidates have intensified statewide electioneering activities, engaging stakeholders and elder statesmen ahead of the 2027 governorship election.

Mbah is expected to campaign on his administration’s projects, programmes and social interventions as he seeks re-election.

Government sources described the administration’s “verifiable projects and social interventions impacting the people” as key strengths ahead of the poll.

The election is shaping up to be a crowded contest, with Mbah facing 15 challengers seeking to wrest control of Enugu State from the APC.

World.title: Stormers perform Impi song after victory against Sharks [video]
World.content:
The Stormers posted an emotional rendition of their famous Impi YamaStormer anthem, this time celebrating Siya Kolisi’s homecoming and Leolin Zas’s 100th test cap.

The praise song also marked their 39-22 victory over the Sharks at their home, at the DHL Stadium.

STORMERS SING IMPI SONG AFTER VICTORY OVER SHARKS

In a clip posted on their social media platforms, the Stormers team gathered to sing their famous Xhosa praising song, Impi yamaStormer, in their changerooms



This followed the final whistle, marking their 39-22 victory over the Sharks at the DHL Stadium.

Player Sazi Sandi led the team in song, with the players singing in beautiful harmony.

The emotional rendition saw the return of Siya Kolisi and Cheslin Kolbe, who is still recovering from a broken jaw. It also marked Leolin Zas’s 100th test cap.

Watch the emotional performance below…

SAZI SANDI: ‘IT UNIFIES US’

The Stormers performing Impi yamaStormer first made headlines in 2023



At the time, the club posted a video of players singing the Xhosa song, accompanied by the Ubumbo Legends, ahead of their first match of the season at DHL Stadium against La Rochelle.

The song is inspired by Impi, the iconic 1981 song by Johnny Clegg and his band Juluka, which tells the story of the Zulu people’s victory over British forces at the Battle of Isandlwana in 1879.

Impi yamaStormer feat. @UbumboLegends 🎶



We can't wait to have you doing your thing in the stands on Saturday for our first game at DHL Stadium this season.#iamastormer #dhldelivers #gwijo pic.twitter.com/sH4EzyVtU0 — DHL Stormers (@THESTORMERS) December 13, 2023

The Stormers adapted their fighting spirit into a team anthem, with Sazi Sandi becoming a familiar leader of the chant.

He said of the modern rugby warcry: “It’s great to cap off a game and a win. It unifies us and just gives us that grounding, that feeling that we all are together.

“We are saying, well done to the Impi of the Stormers, well done to the Stormers soldiers. It’s quite lekker to sing it after a win, because you went to war and came out on top.”

World.title: Viking and his Valkyrie: RG Snyman elated after daughter’s birth
World.content:
RG Snyman on being a first time father. Images via IG

RG Snyman is on cloud nine after becoming a father for the first time. The Springbok and Leinster player welcomed daughter, Rooks Rose, with his wife, Saskia last month.

The towering rugby player -known as the “Viking” – is currently in rehabilitation over an ACL injury sustained earlier this year.

RG SNYMAN ELATED AFTER BECOMING A FATHER

On his Instagram account, RG SNyman has shared new pictures of himself and his newborn daughter, Rooks Rose.



In the pics, the “Viking” lovingly cradled his baby girl, born a month ago.

He captioned the post: “This is the best thing I’ve ever experienced. How amazing that I get to be her dad”.

He added: “She is incredible!”

Earlier this week, RG and Saskia – who live in Ireland, where he plays rugby for Leinster – celebrated a month of being parents.

BACK ON THE PITCH?

RG Snyman suffered a ruptured ACL in his right knee while playing for Leinster against Glasgow Warriors back in March.



With a lengthy rehabilitation, Leinster confirmed that RG had been ruled out for the remainder of the 2025/26 season.

Speaking to Ireland AM TV show in June, RG shared his disappointment in his third ACL injury

He said: “It’s difficult because it’s a long road and it’s hard to know what’s coming

World.title: Louis Vuitton to Era: MaMkhize claps back at ‘downgrade’ label
World.content:
MaMkhize has clapped back at claims she 'downgraded'. Images via IG

Shauwn Mkhize, also known as MaMkhize, has clapped back that she downgraded from her luxury lifestyle after her much of her personal items were auctioned off to pay her R40 million SARS debt.

The businesswoman and soccer club boss has kept a low profile in recent months amid allegations of financial woes.

MAMKHIZE CLAPS BACK AT ‘DOWNGRADE’

Following a hiatus, MaMkhize announced her return to Instagram with a video that responded to her critics.



In the clip, the 51-year-old smashed a bottle of champagne before rolling her designer luggage into the boot of her BMW.

She captioned the clip: “Crushing all bad energies and making room for new beginnings. ✈️✨ Sometimes you just need to take a short left, switch off and get moving.

MaMkhize stated that she was “supporting sisterhood” by publicly endorsing DJ Zinhle’s ERA travelling luggage and South African clothing label AM Collection.



She added: “Stopping Pull Down syndrome, embarrassing our own always”.

MaMkhize’s decision to support local rather than international fashion houses, like Gucci, Versace and Dolce & Gabbana, was not lost on her followers.

When one follower commented, “From Louis Vuitton to Era”, MaMkhize clapped back: “Era is from my sister. Why is there a problem when I support her? I don’t know Louis Vuitton, but I know Zinhle, hence I go loud with her brand”.



SARS SCANDAL

Over the years, MaMkhize has courted controversy for all the wrong reasons, with allegations of tax evasion, tender fraud, corruption, and forgery.

In 2024, the businesswoman’s properties were raided during a search-and-seizure operation authorised by SARS and granted by the High Court.



Through her family’s Shandi Trust, MaMkhize was reported to owe around R40 million in unpaid taxes.

Her luxury assets, like cars, handbags, furniture, specialised equipment, and even alcohol, were auctioned off to help settle the debt.

MaMkhize’s soccer club, Royal AM FC, was placed under curatorship, and, after failed bids, was expelled by the PSL.

World.title: Monday beach plans? Here’s when the tides will turn
World.content:
If you’re heading to the coast on Monday, check the tide times before planning your activities, as spring tides bring changes to water levels along South Africa’s coastline.

However, tides are only part of the picture. Wind, waves and swell and the shape of the seabed can also affect conditions along the shore and at sea.

When to expect the next spring tide

Spring tides are important to watch out for because they bring higher high tides and lower low tides than usual, changing conditions along the coast.



The most recent spring tide coincided with the new moon on Saturday, 10 October. The next spring tide is expected around the full moon on Monday, 26 October 2026.

These changes can affect swimming, surfing, fishing and other coastal activities. Higher tides can cover rocks and reefs, while lower tides expose more of the shoreline.

Check the tide times and the latest weather and marine warnings before you head to the coast.

World.title: Rachel shows support at Siya Kolisi’s Stormers homecoming
World.content:
Rachel Kolisi supported her ex Siya Kolisi at his Stormers homecoming. Images via IG

Rachel Kolisi accompanied her two children to support her ex, Siya Kolisi at his Stormers homecoming match at the DHL Stadium in Cape Town.

The 35-year-old – who is dating influencer Rachel John – returned to his franchise club to be closer to his children and siblings.

Two years ago, Springboks’s first couple announced their marriage split.



RACHEL SHOWS SUPPORT TO SIYA KOLISI’S STORMERS HOMECOMING

On her Instagram Stories, Rachel Kolisi donned a Stormers shirt as she accompanied her children to watch their dad, Siya Kolisi make his Stormers return to DHL Stadium.

The occasion marks the first time in five years that Siya has played for the Cape Town club at its home stadium.

“We did it all today, would be an understatement”, Rachel shared.

It’s not the first time Rachel put her differences aside to support her ex.

Last year, the blonde author and philanthropist travelled to Paris with her children to watch Siya earn his 100th Springboks test cap.

CLOSER TO FAMILY

Siya Kolisi has shared that his transfer from the Sharks to the Stormers was not just a career move, but a bid to be closer to his two children, Nick and Keziah and siblings, Phelo and Liyema.

Following their marriage split, Rachel, and the children returned to their Cape Town family home.

Siya shared in a statement: “My family is in Cape Town, and it is important to me to be close to them. This move gives me the chance to do that while also giving back to the team and fans who made such a big contribution to the player and person I am today.

He added: “I am looking forward to contributing in any way I can to the future success and happiness of this special club and its incredible supporters”.

Stormers boss John Dobson told the press that Siya Kolisi had taken a “massive pay cut” in his sacrifice to return home. He said: “Siya was desperate to come back and made a massive financial sacrifice to be here. That gesture is appreciated.

“He said all I want to do is play for the Stormers and come back to Cape Town.

“When you have a Springbok captain who has made a great contribution to the country, make that gesture; it would be unfair to him to reveal the numbers, but that showed where his heart is.

“There is not one element of financial gain.”

World.title: Inside Vasti and Dricus du Plessis’s wedding of the year [photos]

Inside Vasti and Dricus du Plessis's wedding. Images via IG

Dricus du Plessis and his bride, Vasti, threw the wedding of the year over the weekend at the celebration attended by friends and family.

The five-star affair took place in Franschhoek on Saturday, 10 October.

The MMA fighter and his boxer trainer partner met in 2023 and got engaged last year.



VASTI AND DRICUS DU PLESSIS TIE THE KNOT!

Here’s what we know about Vasti and Dricus du Plessis’s wedding day…

When and where did it take place?

The wedding took place on Saturday, 10 October at the La Paris Estate in Franschhoek.



The couple hosted a wedding weekend, with a pub dinner the night before featuring lots of karaoke and dancing.

What did they wear?

Vasti wore a custom Anel Botha creation during the ceremony, while Dricus du Plessis wore a crisp black tuxedo.



The blonde bride changed into an Amara Bespoke gown adorned with sequins and pearls, and wore a white feather boa for the reception, while her husband donned a cream suit to match her.

Vasti and Dricus du Plessis’s wedding ceremony look.

World.title: 'Everything is falling apart,' EFF calls for accountability in eThekwini.
World.content:
DURBAN - The Economic Freedom Fighters' (EFF) eThekwini mayoral candidate Hlengiwe Mkhaliphi says her party will prioritise the people.

Mkhaliphi spoke at the We The Nation Elections 2026 debate at Mangosuthu University of Technology in Umlazi on Sunday.

She lamented failures in municipal service delivery.

‘Everything is falling apart in eThekwini,’ she explained.

Mkhaliphi also accused the current leadership of failing to communicate with residents.

‘We need a mayor that loves people, loves accountability and will interact with people to solve the problem.’

Mkhaliphi wants a Metro that is transparent about the reasons for water problems.

‘They are not explaining to the community why there has been no water for eight years,’ she says.

Mkhaliphi says that in her party's first 100 days, they will address the water billing system, debt in the City, and the water crisis.

World.title: ANC a no-show at election debate
World.content:
DURBAN - ANC eThekwini mayoral candidate Cyril Xaba was a no-show at the We The Nation Elections 2026 debate at the Mangosuthu University of Technology in Umlazi on Sunday.

Mayoral candidates from the Economic Freedom Fighters (EFF), Democratic Alliance (DA), Inkatha Freedom Party (IFP), and uMkhonto weSizwe Party (MK Party) attended the special broadcast. Independent candidates were also present.

It is unclear why Xaba and other party members failed to arrive.

Mayor Xaba is the incumbent. He runs a Metro where residents continue to voice displeasure at the state of service delivery.

The Auditor-General noted R4.4-billion in irregular expenditure in 2024/2025.

World.title: DA promises R10bn in eThekwini water restoration
World.content:
DURBAN - The Democratic Alliance's eThekwini mayoral candidate Haniff Hoosen says the party will work towards putting R10-billion towards the City's water infrastructure should they take control of the Metro.

'We have a serious problem in the ANC over the last 20 years,' Hoosen said.

'They have not invested in the water infrastructure, and that is why we have 13,000 active water leaks throughout the City,' he explained.

The DA has promised to address water losses that run at 65%. An additional R6-billion is needed to fix ageing wastewater treatment plants.

The Auditor-General noted R4.4-billion in irregular expenditure in 2024/25.

Hoosen says they will start replacing the municipality's pipes and repairing every leak. He wants to do away with water trucks.

'We cannot continue like this,' he said.

World.title: 'If it's broken, fix it', IFP promise better services for eThekwini
World.content:
DURBAN - We need to fix what is broken, says Inkatha Freedom Party eThekwini mayoral candidate, Mkhuleko Hlengwa.

'Our approach is the broken window approach,' he says.

'If it is broken, fix it now," he adds. Hlengwa was speaking at the We The Nation Election Debate at the Mangosuthu University of Technology.

Over 65% of the metro’s treated water is lost to leaks before it reaches a tap. It’s believed an additional R6-billion is needed to fix its ageing wastewater treatment plants.

The Auditor-General noted R4.4-billion in irregular expenditure in the last financial year. In addition, over 2,300 murders were recorded in a single year. Inanda, Umlazi and KwaMashu are among the country's deadliest policing precincts.

Hlengwa says the City's water crisis needs government as a collective and society as a whole.

'We are going to constitute a Mayoral Water Crisis Committee to join civil society, academia and others to provide us with the necessary skills,' he says.

Hlengwa says water provision remains a priority for the IFP.

World.title: 109 migrants dead, 116 missing in boat wreck off Djibouti: UN
World.content:
DJIBOUTI - At least 109 migrants died, including 15 children, and 116 went missing when a boat sank off the shores of Djibouti on the night of October 8-9, a UN agency said Sunday.

Survivors said the vessel, which was carrying 305 people from Djibouti to Yemen, capsized north of the Djibouti town of Obock, according to a statement from the International Organization for Migration (IOM).

"Survivors told me that the boat started to sink backwards as soon as they got in it," Alexandre Coissac, IOM chief of mission in Djibouti, told AFP.

"This is a devastating loss of life," he said earlier in the statement.

"Our thoughts are with the survivors and the families who have lost loved ones or remain without news of their relatives."

Coissac said IOM teams were on the ground alongside Djiboutian authorities to provide emergency aid.

"This tragedy is a stark reminder of the dangers faced by migrants along this migration corridor as they seek economic opportunities" by trying to cross the Bab al-Mandeb Strait to Yemen and then reach Gulf countries.

Among the 109 bodies recovered were 52 men, 42 women and 15 children, nine girls and six boys, the statement said.

More than 80 people survived the shipwreck, all Ethiopian nationals.

"Poverty, insecurity and the growing impacts of climate change drive many to undertake this journey, despite mounting instability across the Middle East," the IOM said.

- Perilous Yemen route -

The IOM said it was assisting 64 survivors at a migrant centre in Obock.

"Djiboutian authorities are continuing search and rescue operations as fears grow for those still missing."

It said that 178,000 people had arrived in Djibouti from Ethiopia from January to October this year.

Since September 10, the IOM detected more than 20,000 crossings to Djibouti from Ethiopia, despite a surge in conflict in Yemen.

The country is stricken by fighting between the Saudi-backed government and Tehran-backed Houthi rebels, who have joined in the regional conflict involving the US and its allies against Iran.

Coissac said 150 of the people on the boat that sank off Djibouti had previously been turned back from Yemen but had attempted the crossing again.

He said he had also spoken to one survivor of the wreck who came from the Tigray region of northern Ethiopia, where rebels are battling the federal government in a recent flare-up of violence.

In 2025, more than 900 migrants died or went missing along the sea route to Yemen and the number attempting the journey increased by 18 percent, the IOM said.

A shipwreck in March 2026 left nine people dead and 45 missing.

IOM spokesman Kennedy Omondi Okoth told AFP this week that most of the people attempting the journey were from Ethiopia or Somalia.

He said many of them were ending up stuck in Djibouti.

The IOM urged "donors and partners to strengthen support for Djibouti's response, including search and rescue operations and life-saving assistance".

World.title: Government eyes supervisory order on asylum ruling
World.content:
PRETORIA - Home Affairs needs more time to prepare for the implementation of the Constitutional Court’s asylum ruling.

Government has said the department needs to strengthen its systems, staff and processing capacity before the judgment can be fully implemented.

Justice Minister Mmamoloko Kubayi said government may ask the court for a supervisory order to oversee the process.

"Following a detailed legal consultation, we have been duly advised that government can approach the courts to seek a supervisory order in this regard. A supervisory order in practical terms would enable the court to retain oversight of the implementation process and provide guidance on how the order should be operationalized.

“Such an order may also include a suspension period to allow the Department of Foreign Affairs the necessary time to develop and strengthen administrative, human resource, infrastructure, and processing capacity required to implement the judgment effectively and sustainably.

“We believe that this approach represents a responsible and lawful mechanism to ensure that constitutional obligations are fulfilled in a manner that is orderly, practical and in the public interest. It will allow government to avoid administrative disruption while ensuring that the rights recognized by the court are progressively and meaningfully realized.”

World.title: All systems go for matric exams
World.content:
PRETORIA - The Basic Education Department has put plans in place to ensure this year’s matric exams run without disruption.

Minister Siviwe Gwarube said strict quality control measures and a zero-tolerance for examination irregularities will be enforced.

“This year we will have a network of around 7,100 examination centers and to ensure a secure environment, have audited an entire network and implemented risk-based monitoring approach, directing our supervision and resources exactly to where they are needed most.

“I want to assure the public that the setting, the moderation, the quality assurance, and all the examination materials are complete. All question papers and examination instruments have been rigorously reviewed by the DBE and have been approved by UMALUSI.

“Crucially, learning from the past challenges, have significantly strengthened our security controls of the entire production and distribution chain. Through the district vetting and examination officials and close collaboration with national and provincial law enforcement structures, we are safeguarding examination materials very closely.

“We have established 189 marking centers, successfully recruiting 51,104 qualified and experienced education markers to mark our scripts. We will apply a standardized national approach to marking, underpinned by strict quality control processes strengthened and the moderation of school-based assessment.

“Let me be clear; the DBE is taking a proactive, zero-tolerance approach to examination irregularities. The candidate and parent pledge agreements to instill a culture of integrity to our young ones and 24-hour examination hotline which is active for the public to report any and all suspicious activity. Furthermore, we have robust contingency plans in place to manage operational challenges including severe weather conditions, community disruptions, because we want no learner to be disadvantaged.”
