World.title: From the archive: The songs that all Mexicans magically know
World.content:
I’ve been living in Mexico for a very long time. When I first came, I was barely an adult, and I’ve “grown up” here in the sense that I grew into an adult here. In lots of ways, I feel like Mexico has raised me from the age of 21 on, which I think most of us can agree is the age of just a baby.

I also love karaoke. A lot. I have a pretty average voice but can mostly hit the notes, and that’s enough for me. Really, there are few things more fun than pretending to be a rockstar, and Mexico is where I first honed my rockstar-pretending skills.

It’s at these parties, though, that I remember: actually, I’m not Mexican.

What makes this obvious? Song choices, mostly. And also this sad fact: Everyone seems to know every single word to lots of songs I’ve never heard in my life. They belt them out with the passion and pain of recently jilted lovers while I stand awkwardly by.

How and when did they learn them? Is there a secret Mexican kids club where they learn all the mariachi classics in elementary school?

Basically, the answer is yes, there is. Really, though, it’s mostly just from them listening to the music their parents listened to growing up. Remember too that children are included at parties here just as much as adults. They might be running around and playing, but Juan Gabriel’s music is subliminally making its way to their memory centers while they do.

I did not grow up with Mexican parents, so I’m still playing catch-up. It’s hard not to feel second-rate at these moments. I mean, what are the songs that Americans universally know? “She’ll Be Comin’ Round the Mountain?” Give me a break.

I know plenty of songs in Spanish, but I really just want to sing “I Want to Break Free” and other favorites at karaoke that fall within my limited voice range. If only I could comfortably hit Shakira’s high notes!

At least I can do fellow Tejana Selena’s Como la Flor, right? Alas, I am still far behind. Luckily, I am surrounded by Mexicans who can help me learn them, or at the very least what they are.

Some are ballads, and some are pop hits. But they all seem to have a magical effect on all Mexicans’ party time. They’re keys that unlock something inside the Mexican psyche, making them close their eyes, tilt their heads back, and position their hands in a way that can only be described as a gesture of anguish born from a deep well of heartbreak and passion.

So I have gone on a deep well expedition for you all, my friends, and have returned! Here are some of the songs that Mexicans know — completely, by heart — and love.

‘El Rey’ by Vicente Fernández

Vicente Fernández - El Rey (En Vivo)

Watch this video on YouTube

You might actually recognize this song, or at least some parts.

“Con dinero y sin dinero, hago siempre lo que quiero…” and “Llorar, y llorar…” are two of its most recognizable lines.



Vicente Fernández, like many of the great Mexican acts of the 20th century, had a real rags to riches story. Born in Jalisco, he spent his teenage years doing odd jobs, including working as a cashier at an uncle’s restaurant. Eventually, he started singing at restaurants and weddings, and the rest is history.

‘ Rata de Dos Patas’ by Paquita la del Barrio

Paquita la del Barrio - Rata De Dos Patas (En Vivo)

Watch this video on YouTube





Now, this song has some seriously sick burns. Here’s the chorus: “Rata de dos patas / Te estoy hablando a ti / Porque un bicho rastrero / Aún siendo el más maldito / Comparado contigo / Se queda muy chiquito.”

“Two-legged rat / I’m talking to you / Because a creeping bug / Even the worst kind, Compared to you / Is nothing.”

As you might guess, Paquita is known for her fearless teasing of, and anger at, Mexican misogyny. “¿Me estás oyendo, inútil?” — “Do you hear me, you good-for-nothing? — often makes its way into her live performances, and honestly, who can get enough of it? Someone’s got to stand up to all those cheating machistas!

‘Bésame Mucho’ by Consuelo Velázquez

Consuelo Velazquez — Besame Mucho

Watch this video on YouTube

You’ve probably heard this song before — it seems every artist has a version of it.

This is a recording of the original composer, who, if Wikipedia is to be believed, had never been kissed when she wrote this song at the age of 16. Check out this video to see her chops on the piano. Wow!

‘Amor Eterno’ by Juan Gabriel

Juan Gabriel - Amor Eterno (En Vivo [Desde el Instituto Nacional de Bellas Artes])

Watch this video on YouTube

Juan Gabriel, like many of the artists mentioned, is a Mexican institution. He sang passionately and often, accompanied by a full orchestra and mariachi singers.

I’m almost certain that most Mexicans know every single word to every one of his songs, but have not proved this scientifically.

‘El Triste’ by José José

José José - El Triste en vivo

Watch this video on YouTube

This is another one of those singers whose every song has essentially been memorized by a sizable portion of the population. Rumor has it that his singing voice completely left him after years of drinking.

Thankfully, he recorded quite a bit before that point.

‘Mis Ojos Lloran por Ti’ by Big Boy

Mis Ojos Lloran Por Ti

Watch this video on YouTube

This is a more contemporary song than the ones above, and it is a fun one! Whoever can sing this one at karaoke, in fact, pretty much wins the night.

Why? There’s a lot of really fast rapping woven throughout the song, and it is a major challenge.

‘Que Bello’ by Sonora Dinamita

La Sonora Dinamita - Que Bello (letra)

Watch this video on YouTube

This song cracks me up, and it’s one that I actually know! Sometimes I try to sing it at karaoke, but usually start laughing when I hear a line like “Pero me arrepiento, en el piso o donde sea y tómame” — “But I change my mind, on the floor or wherever, take me.”

Um, I’m sorry, a cold, hard floor? When there’s a nice, comfy bed available? Who are these people? In any case, it’s a fun little cumbia and a major classic.

‘Si No Te Hubieras Ido’ by Marco Antonio Solís

Marco Antonio Solís - Si No Te Hubieras Ido | Lyric Video

Watch this video on YouTube

This is the newest song on the list, having come out in 1999, the year I graduated high school. It’s a beautiful and heartbreaking ballad, with one of my favorite lines of any song: “El frío de mi cuerpo pregunta por ti.” “The cold of my body asks for you.”

See? Super romantic.

Sarah DeVries is a writer and translator based in Xalapa, Veracruz. She can be reached through her website.

World.title: Mexico’s week in review: An unauthorized police academy stirs a security row with US as triple storm threat keeps coasts on alert
World.content:
Listen to this article

Storms swirled around and within Mexico this week as a political misstep by Governor Mauricio Kuri in Querétaro became a national controversy.

Simon, currently located off the Pacific coast of Jalisco and Colima, is now a Category 4 hurricane and will make landfall this weekend. Hurricane Isaias swept past the Yucatán Peninsula and landed near Destin, Florida, on Friday evening. Far out in the Pacific, Tropical Storm Rachel, which briefly reached hurricane strength, stayed clear of the Mexican coastline on Saturday but was expected to weaken and send its remnants toward Baja California and the U.S. Southwest.

On land, President Claudia Sheinbaum reacted swiftly to the surprise inauguration in Querétaro of a binational security institution that received direct support from the United States. According to the federal government, the project was never disclosed to or authorized by the corresponding Mexican authorities.

In Nayarit, searching mothers helped authorities uncover an alleged “extermination center” near Tepic, where investigators found a makeshift burner and a pit containing the remains of recently cremated bodies. Officials haven’t said how many people died or tied the site to a criminal group. The discovery underscored Mexico’s disappearance crisis, with more than 130,000 people registered as missing.

Didn’t have time to catch this week’s top stories? Here’s what you missed.

Police academy controversy

Sheinbaum opened the week by questioning an “International Police Training Academy” in central Mexico, whose cornerstone Gov. Mauricio Kuri and U.S. Ambassador Ronald Johnson laid Oct. 2. She said such a project can’t exist without federal authorization and asked why the military, the Security Cabinet and the Foreign Ministry weren’t invited.

A leaked letter then showed Kuri had told Foreign Affairs Minister Roberto Velasco only that Johnson would visit Querétaro, calling the interactions ceremonial and never mentioning the academy. The Foreign Affairs Ministry replied that any security training project with a foreign government needs prior approval from the High-Level Security Group (GANSEG), which hadn’t been granted. It also offered to help Querétaro seek it.

On Tuesday, Sheinbaum said federal officials had approved nine Querétaro–U.S. cooperation projects since December 2021, but not this one. She cited the state’s security minister, who said the facility would bring specialized training from U.S. agencies. Johnson had called it a “State Interdiction Academy” and noted more than US $10 million in U.S. support for Querétaro police over the past decade. The episode drew parallels to April’s alleged CIA involvement in a Chihuahua drug lab raid. Both states are governed by the opposition National Action Party (PAN).

On Thursday, Sheinbaum met with U.S. business leaders at the National Palace, with Johnson in attendance, but said security would be handled separately. She said Johnson had agreed to meet Velasco soon, and Security Minister Omar García Harfuch told legislators that bilateral cooperation is subject to Mexican law.

Hurricane Simon threatens Jalisco and Colima

Simon strengthened into a Category 4 hurricane on Saturday morning, with sustained winds of 230 km/h (145 mph). The U.S. National Hurricane Center (NHC) said the eye could pass near or over Mexico’s west-central coast late Saturday or Sunday, though its track remained uncertain. Civil Protection chief Laura Velázquez said the impact zone could be Cihuatlán, La Huerta, Tomatlán, Cabo Corrientes or Puerto Vallarta in Jalisco, or Manzanillo, Colima.

A hurricane warning covers Punta San Telmo, Michoacán, to Punta Mita, Nayarit. Rainfall could reach 20 to 38 centimeters, with isolated totals of 64 centimeters. Authorities set up command centers in Puerto Vallarta, Cihuatlán and Manzanillo, began evacuations in the flood-prone Jalisco community of El Rebalse and suspended classes in 22 Jalisco municipalities Friday and Monday. Simon could be the second hurricane to make landfall in Mexico this Pacific season, after Polo.

On the Atlantic side, Isaias became the season’s first hurricane Wednesday night, the latest first hurricane in the 60-year modern era. It was forecast to make U.S. landfall Friday evening, with no Mexico landfall expected, though it dumped heavy rain on the Gulf coast and Yucatán Peninsula states. It followed Mexico’s first hurricane-free Atlantic September since 1994, a contrast with a Pacific that had produced nine hurricanes by Wednesday. Experts point to a “super” El Niño, which warms Pacific waters and raises wind shear in the Atlantic.

Sheinbaum presents presidential decrees regarding nationality and social media

On Wednesday, Sheinbaum signed a decree formalizing a constitutional reform that requires exclusive Mexican nationality for presidential, gubernatorial and Mexico City mayoral candidates. The ban takes effect from 2028, after gubernatorial elections in 17 states next June. Citizens Movement (MC) Sen. Luis Donaldo Colosio Riojas criticized the reform for creating “two categories of Mexicans.”

On Friday, after a fatal machete attack at a Torreón school, the government presented a decree on “safe digital environments” for minors. It bars platforms from showing or recommending content that promotes hate speech, violent extremism, sexual exploitation, suicide, self-harm, eating disorders, cyberbullying and illegal conduct. Sheinbaum said it would be published in the official gazette next Tuesday or Wednesday after legal review to ensure it doesn’t exceed the executive branch’s authority.

Border deployment and gunfire incident

Mexico sent 500 Army and National Guard troops to the Tamaulipas border after U.S. Coast Guard personnel were fired upon from the Mexican side Sept. 26 and returned fire. The U.S. ordered 500 soldiers to the Texas side.

The Foreign Affairs and Defense ministries described the twin deployments as part of a “Concurrent Operation,” backed by two UH-60 helicopters, drones and anti-drone equipment in five Tamaulipas municipalities. The Navy is also participating through “Operation Saber.” No injuries or damage were reported in the shooting.

Mazatlán gets elite reinforcements as violence persists

The federal government formed a Special Operations Group of 29 Defense Ministry soldiers to work within Mazatlán’s municipal police after repeated troop deployments failed to stem the violence. The unit follows a wave of homicides, armed attacks and explosive assaults that led officials to urge caution between 3 and 10 p.m. The city also bought 50 bicycles for soldiers and National Guard members.

Then came Thursday’s shooting at El Castillo prison, which killed nine inmates and a 2-year-old boy and injured 16 prisoners. Alleged Sinaloa Cartel figure “El Owen” was reportedly among the dead. Sheinbaum said the Security Cabinet is working with interim Sinaloa Governor Graciela Domínguez to strengthen the state’s prisons.

Inflation edges up

Annual headline inflation rose to 3.45% in September from 3.26%, the highest since May but well below March’s 4.59% peak. Core inflation eased to 3.75% from 3.88%. Fruit and vegetable prices jumped 8.78% annually, while meat prices fell 4.46%. The Bank of Mexico held its benchmark rate at 6.50% two weeks ago and meets again Nov. 5.

Investment news

Fixed capital investment grew 6% annually in July, the fastest pace in two years, driven by construction. Private sector investment growth hit a 30-month high, though the total remains 2.35% below its July 2024 record. Spending on Mexican-made machinery and equipment fell 8% from January to July, while imported equipment rose 3.5%.

In Nuevo León, Gov. Samuel García announced US $600 million for industrial infrastructure, mainly data centers in Apodaca and Pesquería. That brings 2026 foreign investment in the state to $136.6 billion by his count.

Bárcena says ‘not yet’ to fracking in Mexico

On Tuesday, Environment Minister Alicia Bárcena told lawmakers the conditions for fracking “do not exist” and that Sheinbaum hasn’t authorized pilot tests. Only testing for deep saline water has been approved. Government scientists identified the Sabinas-Burro-Picachos basin as the only viable site, but nonprofit CartoCrítica says all the fresh water needed there would come from basins lacking available supply.

4 economy headlines to know

Mexico’s trade surplus with the U.S. rose 21.2% to US $155.87 billion from January to August, as exports hit a record $419.34 billion. Only Vietnam posted a larger surplus. The government faces a tough negotiating backdrop, with the U.S. having declined to renew the USMCA trade agreement in its current form, in part due to its deficit with Mexico, which the Trump administration views as an unacceptable imbalance.

The International Monetary Fund raised its growth forecasts to 1.5% for 2026 and 1.8% for 2027, citing a strong second quarter, but urged fiscal consolidation.

Auto parts output hit a record US $10.85 billion in July, up 7.15%. Vehicle production, however, fell 15.1% in September, its steepest drop since 2021, and car exports declined 11.85%.

Finally, a Citi survey of Mexico-based analysts sees the peso at 18 per dollar at the end of 2026 and 18.50 at the end of 2027, after the currency fell 6% in September.

World.title: Things to Do in Zanzibar 12 to 31 October 2026
World.content:
ZANZIBAR · Culture

Nyerere Day on Wednesday 14 October is the one confirmed dated event for Zanzibar from 12 to 31 October, with the short rains arriving. Everyday outings fill the rest.

The Stone Town seafront on a cloudy day. (File photo, Wikimedia Commons, resized)

ZANZIBAR — This is the monthly guide for people who live on the island or are staying for weeks, not a one-weekend tourist list. Here are the things to do in Zanzibar in October 2026 from Monday 12 to Saturday 31 October: one dated public holiday, a set of established island outings, and what the weather is likely to do. Earlier dates are left out. Eight cards follow, fewer than usual because we found no other confirmed dated event. For wider context, see our explainer on Tanzania.

The short rains are known in Swahili as vuli. The Tanzania Meteorological Authority forecasts above-normal to normal rainfall in several parts of Tanzania during the October to December vuli season, with increased rain expected particularly in November (The Citizen). The forecast is national, not specific to the islands. Pack a light rain layer, and keep outdoor plans flexible.

Only one dated item could be confirmed on the island in this window: the Nyerere Day holiday. The Yas Zanzibar International Marathon was run on Sunday 20 September at Maisara Grounds, with 5 km, 10 km and 21 km races (The Citizen), so it is not an October event. Everyday attractions fill the gaps. We quote no prices, because no operator or official tariff was available to check.

12 and 13 October: Before the Public Holiday

Daily, October Stone Town Walking Tours Stone Town, Zanzibar City · Price from the operator · All ages Stone Town is a UNESCO World Heritage Site, and licensed guides run walks through the old town. Typical routes pass the former slave market site, the House of Wonders, the Old Fort and the carved wooden doors of merchant houses. The walks show how Swahili, Omani, Indian and British influences layered over each other. Book through your hotel or a Stone Town tour office a day ahead.

Daily, October Spice Farm Tours Central Zanzibar · Price from the operator · All ages Morning spice tours are the usual way to see clove, nutmeg, cinnamon and vanilla growing, and most finish with a tasting or a Swahili lunch. Go early, before the heat, and wear closed shoes in case of wet paths. Arrange transport through a local operator or your accommodation.

Every evening, October Forodhani Gardens Night Market Forodhani Gardens, Stone Town · Free entry, food priced per stall · All ages The seafront park fills with food stalls after sunset, selling Zanzibar pizza, grilled seafood and sugar cane juice. Residents use it as much as visitors do. Carry small shilling notes and agree the price before ordering. Stalls may close early if rain arrives.

14 October: Nyerere Day

Wednesday 14 October, all day Nyerere Day Nationwide, including Zanzibar · Public holiday, no ticket · All ages Tanzania marks the death of Julius Nyerere, the country’s first president, on 14 October 1999. Nyerere Day is a public holiday on Wednesday 14 October. Government offices and banks are normally closed on public holidays, and tourist businesses may keep different hours, so check ahead. Plan paperwork and banking for another day.

15 to 24 October: Mid-Month Outings

Daily, October Jozani Chwaka Bay National Park Jozani, central Zanzibar · Entry fee at the gate · All ages The island’s only national park protects mangrove boardwalks, forest trails and the endemic Zanzibar red colobus monkey. We could not find an official tariff, so confirm the fee at the gate. Go early, when the monkeys are most active, and expect muddy trails after rain.

Daily, October Nungwi and Kendwa Beach Days Nungwi and Kendwa, northern Zanzibar · Free beach access · All ages The north coast is the usual choice for swimming at most tides, and it is warm in October. Kendwa is known for its sunsets. Dhow trips and snorkelling can be arranged on the beach, but agree the price and the boat condition before paying. Sea conditions can turn as the rains approach.

25 to 31 October: Late Month

Daily, October Prison Island (Changuu) Boat Trips Boats leave from the Stone Town waterfront · Price from the operator · All ages A short boat ride from Stone Town takes you to Changuu Island, known for its giant tortoises and a small beach. Negotiate the boat price as a return trip and confirm the waiting time on the island. Trips can be cancelled in rough weather.

Daily, October Darajani Market Darajani, Stone Town · Free entry · All ages The main market of Stone Town is where residents buy fish, meat, spices and fruit. It is loud and crowded, and a direct view of daily island life. Go in the morning, keep your bag in front of you, and ask before photographing people.

What it means for you

If you are visiting from the United States, October is a sensible month for a first trip: the island is quieter than in the peak season, but the rain risk is rising. A flexible itinerary and travel insurance that covers weather disruption matter more than usual this year, given the national rainfall outlook.

Africa Intelligence One email, every weekday morning. African markets, politics and business — filed from our newsroom in Rio. Yesterday’s subject line: “Sudan drone strike follows failed US embargo push” Get the brief Free. We send a confirmation link first — nothing arrives until you click it. Unsubscribe with one click in any edition. If you stop opening us for 30 days we stop sending by ourselves, as we assume the interest is no longer there. See our privacy policy. We never share your email.

If you live on the island, the practical point is the 14 October holiday, when banks and government offices close. Do banking and official errands before Wednesday 14 October or after it.

What is not known

The marathon was run on 20 September, so there is no race date to plan around this month. We found no confirmed festival, concert or market for 12 to 31 October. We could not verify any other listing for these dates. Check back as organisers confirm dates.

Planning your Zanzibar in October

Mornings and late afternoons are the most comfortable times for walking. Rain tends to arrive in short, heavy bursts, so build a gap into any plan that depends on a boat.

Getting around at night is easiest by taxi or a pre-arranged driver, especially outside Stone Town. Agree the fare before the journey. Shared dala-dala minibuses are cheap, but slow and crowded.

Carry small shilling notes for markets and street food. For other Tanzanian events this month, see our Dar es Salaam guide, and for the island’s economy, our report on the Zanzibar revenue authority.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the main public holiday in Zanzibar in October 2026?

Nyerere Day falls on Wednesday 14 October 2026. It is a public holiday across Tanzania, including Zanzibar, and banks and government offices close.

When is the Zanzibar Marathon in 2026?

The sixth Yas Zanzibar International Marathon was run on Sunday 20 September 2026 at Maisara Grounds, with 5 km, 10 km and 21 km races, so there is no marathon in October.

What is the weather like in Zanzibar in October 2026?

The short rains (vuli) run from October to December. Tanzania’s weather authority forecasts above-normal to normal rainfall in several areas of the country this season, with increased rain expected particularly in November.

Are there festivals in Zanzibar from 12 to 31 October 2026?

We found no confirmed festival, concert or market in that window. The one dated item is the Nyerere Day holiday on 14 October.

Is Stone Town worth visiting in the rainy season?

Yes, in general. Walking tours and the markets are outdoors, so a sudden downpour can pause them, and we could not check each operator’s wet-weather policy. Allow flexible time.

World.title: Florianópolis Events 12 to 31 October 2026
World.content:
FLORIANÓPOLIS · Culture

Free Vivo Música on 18 October, a feijoada party in Jurerê on 17 October, pagode on 24 October and live music on 30 October. Twelve checked events from 12 to 31 October 2026.

FLORIANÓPOLIS — This guide is for people who live here or stay for weeks, not for a weekend tourist. It lists 12 events from 12 to 31 October 2026 that we checked against organiser, venue or ticket pages, with practical details on things to do in Florianópolis October 2026. Events before 12 October are no longer listed.

Fenaostra, the oyster festival, ends on Monday 12 October, which is also a national public holiday. After that the city shifts to free culture in the middle of the month, then to big arena nights in São José and Jurerê. Dates and times come from the organisers and can change, so check the ticket page on the day. All prices below convert at R$4.98 per US$1 (RT, close of 9 October 2026).

File photo: Florianópolis, Santa Catarina.

12 to 14 October: Holiday Monday and midweek music

Monday 12 October, 11:00 to 22:00 Fenaostra Kids, final day of Fenaostra CentroSul, Av. Governador Gustavo Richard 850, Centro · From R$15 (about US$3) plus a R$2.50 (about US$0.50) fee · Children under 12 free On the festival’s last day the programme is built around families. Felipe Bluezera opens at noon, a storytelling session starts at 13:30, there is Boi de Mamão folk theatre, Maria Clara & JP perform and the Papa Ostra eating contest has its final. Expect crowds because it is a holiday.

Monday 12 October, 20:00 Festival Choro Mulheril, opening round Bugio Trindade, Trindade · Free, voluntary donations accepted The opening of a festival that celebrates women in choro, a Brazilian instrumental style. It runs until Sunday 18 October, with recitals at Teatro Álvaro de Carvalho later in the week. We could not confirm the full programme.

Tuesday 13 October, 20:00 Violoncelo em Cena, Camerata Florianópolis Teatro Ademir Rosa, Centro Integrado de Cultura, Agronômica · R$10 (about US$2) and R$5 (about US$1) · Blueticket or the Camerata office, Rua Joe Collaço 708 Cellist Érico Miranda Schmitt plays Vieuxtemps’ Cello Concerto No. 1, followed by Bizet’s Symphony in C. Maestro Jeferson Della Rocca conducts. It is a rare classical concert at pocket-money prices.

15 to 18 October: Free culture and the big stages

Thursday 15 and Saturday 17 October, both from 13:00 Praça Inclusiva Thursday: Praça da Cidadania, UFSC, Trindade · Saturday: outside Pista de Skate, Beira-Mar Continental, Balneário · Free An afternoon of music, adapted sport and dance for people with and without disabilities. A Corda em Si previews its show “As paredes têm ouvidos”, with percussionist Rodrigo Gudin Paiva and MC/DJ Beal. The organisers say both sites are fully accessible for wheelchair users and people with strollers.

Saturday 17 October, from 12:00 Feijoada do Cacau, 28th edition P12, Servidão José Cardoso de Oliveira, Jurerê Internacional · Second batch R$230 (about US$46) plus fees · Ingresse · 18+ A beach-club party with open food and an open bar (drinks until 20:00). Wanessa Camargo headlines, with Banda TBT and DJ Mari Florêncio. Entry is banned for anyone under 18, even with a parent. Check Ingresse for current batches.

Saturday 17 October, opening at 14:00 Ernesto Neto, Ananta Ananda Centro Cultural Veras, Rua Vera Linhares de Andrade 2064, Córrego Grande · Free The first solo show in the region by one of Brazil’s best-known contemporary artists, with three sculptures that have not been shown in Florianópolis before. It runs until 10 April 2027, Tuesday to Friday 14:00 to 21:00 and Saturday 13:00 to 19:00. The organisers have not published an opening programme.

Saturday 17 October, 17:00 Mostra de Cinema Infantil, closing session with Palavra Cantada Teatro Ademir Rosa, Centro Integrado de Cultura, Agronômica · Free The 25th children’s film festival (9 to 17 October, 137 films) ends with a concert by the children’s music group Palavra Cantada. Free tickets are handed out 40 minutes before each session, first come, first served.

Sunday 18 October, doors 18:00, show 19:00 A Culpa é dos Amigos Arena Opus, Rodovia SC-281, São José · Bronze R$90 (about US$18), half price R$45 (about US$9); top Diamante R$300 (about US$60); plus 15% online fee · Uhuu · 16+ A stand-up night with seven Brazilian comedians, including Thiago Ventura, Afonso Padilha and Dihh Lopes, lasting about two hours. The show is in Portuguese, so it suits you only if your listening is strong.

Sunday 18 October, from 16:00 Vivo Música Parque Beira-Mar Continental, Av. Cláudio A. Barbosa 24, Balneário · Free, subject to capacity · All ages A free open-air concert backed by Brazil’s federal cultural incentive law. Dandara Manoela opens, Camerata Florianópolis and Dazaranha follow, and Vanessa da Mata is the headliner. It is the standout free event of the month. Arrive early, because the waterfront fills up.

24 to 31 October: Pagode, comedy and rock

Saturday 24 October, from 15:00 Vibra Pagode Arena Floripa, Parque Metropolitano Francisco Dias Velho, Centro · Ingresse · 18+ Thiaguinho, Belo and Turma do Pagode share one bill of pagode, a Brazilian samba-based style. We could not confirm ticket prices in the sources we checked, so see the Ingresse page.

Saturday 24 October, doors 19:30, show 21:00 Renato Albani, Salve-se Quem Puder Arena Opus, São José · Minha Entrada The comedian presents a new stand-up show built on everyday situations. Prices were not visible in the listing we checked, so confirm them on Minha Entrada.

Friday 30 October, doors 20:00, show 21:30 Abruna Delfino 146, Rua Luís Delfino 146, Centro · First-batch price from R$50 (about US$10) plus a fee · Pensa no Evento · 18+ The singer revisits Amy Winehouse, Billie Eilish, Jorja Smith, Rita Lee and Cássia Eller in a pop, rock and R&B set with a five-piece band. Online sales close at 21:00 on the night.

Planning your Florianópolis in October

October is spring: mild to warm, humid and changeable, with frequent rain. Coastal wind can make evenings cooler on the Beira-Mar waterfront. Check a forecast shortly before each outdoor event.

12 October 2026 is Nossa Senhora Aparecida, a Brazilian national public holiday. It is also Children’s Day, but Children’s Day is not itself a public holiday. Expect reduced opening hours at some shops and heavier traffic on the bridges and beaches.

Getting around at night is easiest by car or ride-hailing app. Buses run less often after midnight, and Arena Opus in São José and the mainland waterfront need a bridge crossing, so plan your return in advance.

Tickets are sold on several platforms: Uhuu, Ingresse, Minha Entrada, Blueticket and Pensa no Evento. Foreign cards usually work online, but some small venues prefer Pix, Brazil’s instant bank transfer, so ask in advance if you have no Brazilian bank account.

What it means for you: a visitor with only one free evening gets the most for the least on Sunday 18 October, when Vivo Música costs nothing and sits next to the mainland waterfront. For indoor options in wet weather, the Camerata concert and the Ernesto Neto show are the cheapest choices.

We could not verify every event announced for the period. Smaller bar shows and private parties are left out on purpose, and we listed no event without a date, venue and organiser or ticket page.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the biggest free event in Florianópolis in late October 2026?

Vivo Música on Sunday 18 October from 16:00 at Parque Beira-Mar Continental, with Dandara Manoela, Camerata Florianópolis, Dazaranha and Vanessa da Mata. Entry is free, subject to capacity.

Is 12 October 2026 a public holiday in Brazil?

Yes. 12 October is Nossa Senhora Aparecida, a national public holiday. It is also Children’s Day, which is not itself a public holiday.

How much do arena shows in Florianópolis cost in October 2026?

A Culpa é dos Amigos on 18 October starts at R$90 (about US$18) for Bronze, plus a 15% online fee. Prices convert at R$4.98 per US$1.

Which free exhibitions and shows can I see after 12 October 2026?

Ernesto Neto’s Ananta Ananda opens free at Centro Cultural Veras on Saturday 17 October and runs to 10 April 2027. Praça Inclusiva is free on 15 and 17 October, and the Mostra de Cinema Infantil closes free at 17:00 on 17 October.

Where can I buy tickets for events in Florianópolis?

The events in this guide sell through Uhuu, Ingresse, Minha Entrada, Blueticket and Pensa no Evento. The Camerata concert on 13 October is also sold at the orchestra’s office, and the free events need no ticket or hand them out at the door.

World.title: Oaxaca Events 12 to 31 October 2026 Guide
World.content:
OAXACA · Culture

Oaxaca’s next three weeks open with the Tule tree’s birthday on 12 October, add a regional Mexican concert and an Afro-Mexican festival, and end with the Day of the Dead parade on 31 October.

A brass band leads a calenda procession through Oaxaca’s centre, a sight that returns with the Day of the Dead season. File photo. Photo: ProtoplasmaKid, CC BY-SA 4.0 via Wikimedia Commons

OAXACA — Oaxaca de Juárez has nine events with a published date between Monday 12 and Saturday 31 October 2026, and most list no admission price. The first is the 12 October birthday of El Tule, the ancient cypress outside the city. The biggest is the Day of the Dead parade on Saturday 31 October.

This guide is for people who live in the city or are staying for weeks. Dates, times and venues come from the state tourism programme as reported by Oaxaca’s regional press and from event listings, checked on 11 October 2026. We found fewer than ten confirmed events, so we list only those. Where no price is published, we say so, and we give no peso amounts because none were published.

For US readers: Oaxaca is on UTC−6 all year. Until US clocks change on 1 November, it is one hour behind Chicago and two hours behind New York.

12 to 19 October: a tree, a concert and a coastal festival

Monday 12 October, 06:00 to midnight Birthday of the Árbol del Tule Santa María del Tule · Admission price not published The town celebrates its ancient Montezuma cypress. The programme lists “Mañanitas con Chirimía” (a dawn serenade with a traditional pipe and drum) at 06:00, a pre-Hispanic ritual from 06:10 to 07:00, Mass from 10:00 to 12:00 and a traditional dance from 19:30 to midnight. The tree is a short taxi or colectivo ride east of the city, so go early for the quietest hour.

Saturday 17 October, 21:00 El Trono de México and Lenin Ramírez Auditorio Guelaguetza, Fortín · Ticket price not confirmed A double bill of regional Mexican acts at the open-air hillside venue used for the Guelaguetza dance festival in July. Oaxaca’s regional press lists both acts; a tour-date listing confirms the El Trono de México date and time. We could not confirm ticket prices, so check the organiser before you go. Taxis and ride-hailing apps are the practical way home, as the hill is far from the centre.

Monday 19 October, procession 16:00, programme 17:00 Guelaguetza Afro, “La Rejunjuneada” Chacahua Isla, Villa de Tututepec, Costa de Oaxaca · Free admission The state government lists this Afro-Mexican celebration on the Pacific coast, with a street procession followed by the main programme. It is a long trip from the city, so plan an overnight stay and check road and boat access with local hosts.

26 to 31 October: the Day of the Dead run-up

From Monday 26 October to Tuesday 3 November Day of the Dead programme, state capital Parque Juárez “El Llano”, Templo de Jalatlaco and the Zócalo · Prices not published The state government announced more than 100 activities for this period. They include a marigold-field circuit called “Flores que guían el alma” that starts at Parque Juárez, a 250 square metre sand tapestry in the Jalatlaco neighbourhood, a facade competition in the historic centre and “Casa Hecho en Oaxaca” at the Real Alhóndiga from 10:00 to 20:00. Exact daily schedules were not yet published.

Friday 30 October, 19:00 Verbena Xandú Zócalo · Free tamales, bread, chocolate and coffee A popular evening fair in the main square, with free traditional food, as part of the state programme. Arrive early, since free food draws crowds.

Friday 30 October, 22:00 Recorrido al Mictlán race Ex Convento de Santo Domingo · Price not published A night run themed on the Aztec underworld, starting from the former convent beside the Santo Domingo church. Entry rules and fees were not published.

Saturday 31 October, 18:00 Gran Comparsa of Day of the Dead Calzada Porfirio Díaz to García Vigil · Public parade A costumed street parade from Calzada Porfirio Díaz to García Vigil street. A comparsa is a travelling band of costumed dancers and musicians. Stand along García Vigil early if you want a clear view.

Saturday 31 October, evening Catrinas contest and concert Alameda de León, Centro · Price not published The programme lists a contest for the best Catrina costume (the elegant skeleton figure of Day of the Dead) and a concert in the park beside the cathedral. Reports give the concert start as 20:00. The artists were not named.

Running through the month

Until Saturday 31 October Mole de caderas in Oaxaca restaurants Participating restaurants, Oaxaca de Juárez · Dish prices vary After the 10 and 11 October festival, participating restaurants in the city keep mole de caderas, a goat-hip stew from the Mixteca region, on the menu until 31 October. The state tourism ministry did not publish the restaurant list in the sources we checked, so ask your hotel.

Planning your Oaxaca in October

October is the end of the rainy season in the Valles Centrales, so showers are possible in the afternoon and evenings turn cooler. Carry a light layer for outdoor concerts at the Auditorio Guelaguetza, which sits on a hill above the city.

Día de Muertos (Day of the Dead) runs from 31 October to 2 November, with the main observances on 1 and 2 November. Our Day of the Dead 2026 date guide explains the calendar.

Many events do not publish prices online. Ask at the venue, and carry cash, since smaller venues do not always take foreign cards. For daily costs, see our Oaxaca cost-of-living guide, and for food context our explainer on tlayudas. More coverage is in the Mexico section.

What it means for you: a US visitor staying a month can reach most of this without a car. The Day of the Dead events are in the centre, while the Tule, Chacahua and Fortín trips need a taxi or a local driver. Hotel prices for the Day of the Dead week usually rise, so book early if you want 31 October to 2 November.

What we could not confirm: ticket prices for the Trono de México concert, the artists at the 31 October concert, daily schedules of the Day of the Dead programme from 26 October, and fees for the Mictlán race. We did not list events whose date, venue or organiser we could not verify, including several exhibitions and arts-centre programmes that earlier listings mentioned.

Frequently Asked Questions

What events are on in Oaxaca between 12 and 31 October 2026?

The Tule tree celebrates its birthday on Monday 12 October, El Trono de México and Lenin Ramírez play the Auditorio Guelaguetza on Saturday 17 October at 21:00, and Guelaguetza Afro takes place in Chacahua on Monday 19 October. The Day of the Dead programme begins on 26 October.

When is the Gran Comparsa of Day of the Dead in Oaxaca in 2026?

The Gran Comparsa leaves at 18:00 on Saturday 31 October and runs from Calzada Porfirio Díaz to García Vigil street. A Catrinas contest and a concert follow at the Alameda de León.

Is Día de Muertos in October or November in Oaxaca?

Día de Muertos is celebrated from 31 October to 2 November, with the main observances on 1 and 2 November. The state programme of more than 100 activities in the capital runs from 26 October to 3 November.

What is the Verbena Xandú in Oaxaca?

It is a popular evening fair in the Zócalo on Friday 30 October at 19:00, with free tamales, bread, chocolate and coffee, listed in the state Day of the Dead programme.

Is the Guelaguetza Afro on 19 October free?

Yes. The state government lists free admission for the celebration at Chacahua Isla, Villa de Tututepec, with a procession at 16:00 and the main programme at 17:00.

World.title: Mombasa Events 12 to 31 October 2026
World.content:
MOMBASA · Culture

Four dated events are confirmed for Mombasa and its coast from 12 to 31 October: Mashujaa Day, a coast golf open, Pwani Innovation Week and a tourism summit.

MOMBASA, Kenya. The coast’s big arts festival, Wimbi La Sanaa, ended on Saturday 10 October. What follows is quieter and more business-minded: a national holiday on Tuesday 20 October, then a golf day, a youth innovation week and a tourism summit in the last week of the month.

We list only events that an organiser, venue or official source confirms. That left four. Several concerts and parties appear on ticket sites, but we could not confirm them with the venue or organiser, so we left them out. For readers in the United States, Mombasa is Kenya’s main port city, and the coast is where many visitors and remote workers base themselves.

Key Facts — Who Residents, remote workers and visitors on the Kenyan coast, including Americans planning a trip.

— Holiday Mashujaa Day (Heroes’ Day) falls on Tuesday 20 October.

— Golf Uganda-Kenya Coast Open at Vipingo Ridge, Kilifi County, on Saturday 24 October.

— Late October Pwani Innovation Week runs Monday 26 to Friday 30 October; the Uganda-Kenya Coast Tourism & Innovation Summit runs 26 and 27 October.

— Not yet confirmed Ticket prices and the venue for Pwani Innovation Week. The organisers have not published them in the sources we checked.

Palms and a thatched beach building on the Kenyan coast near Mombasa. File photo. Photo: Melissa Guadalupe Huertas, CC BY-SA 4.0 via Wikimedia Commons

Tuesday 20 October: Mashujaa Day

Tuesday 20 October Mashujaa Day National public holiday · Kenya Mashujaa Day honours national heroes. The state celebration is in Eldoret, in the Rift Valley, not on the coast. Government statements reported by Citizen Digital put the main event at Kipchoge Keino Stadium on 20 October, with related events from 13 to 18 October under the theme “Security, Sports and the Finance Sector (The Economy)”. In Mombasa, expect public offices to close and some shops and tour operators to change their hours. Confirm with restaurants, tour operators and ferry services in advance.

Saturday 24 October: golf north of Mombasa

Saturday 24 October Uganda-Kenya Coast Open Vipingo Ridge PGA Baobab Course, Kilifi County · Organisers: Kilifi County, coast counties and the Ugandan consulate in Mombasa · Entry prices: ask the venue This is the fourth event in the Uganda-Kenya Coast Open series. Players join either the Kenya Coast team or Team Uganda in an 18-hole Stableford competition. Entry is through an online form, and stay-and-play packages with accommodation are priced by the venue. Vipingo Ridge is in Kilifi County, north of Mombasa island, so allow travel time. Contact details are on the Vipingo Ridge event page.

Late October: innovation and tourism

From Monday 26 October Pwani Innovation Week 2026 Mombasa · Organiser: Swahilipot Hub · Registration: through the organiser This is the seventh edition and coincides with ten years of Swahilipot Hub, a youth-led creative and technology hub on the coast. Citizen Digital reports the dates as 26 to 30 October (Monday to Friday); check the final programme for the closing day. If you work in technology, the creative industries or social enterprise, it is the main technology and creative-industries gathering on the Mombasa calendar this month. We could not find a published venue or ticket price.

Monday 26 and Tuesday 27 October Uganda-Kenya Coast Tourism & Innovation Summit Sarova Whitesands Beach Resort & Spa, Mombasa · Registration: ask the organisers The fifth edition has the theme “Unlocking Tourism Opportunities: Resolving Policy Bottlenecks through Technology, Youth and Seamless Mobility across East Africa”. The Ugandan consulate in Mombasa organises it with tourism stakeholders from both countries. Its focus areas include youth-led innovation, digital visitor services, tourism investment and the movement of people and services across East Africa. It is a trade event, not a public festival, so treat it as a networking date for anyone in hospitality, travel or cross-border business.

Further ahead

If you plan to stay on the coast into December, our guide to the Beneath the Baobabs festival in Kilifi covers a date north of Mombasa. For cultural context, read Kenya culture and the key figures to know.

What it means for you

If you are in Mombasa this month, plan around Tuesday 20 October: a holiday week can thin out services even though the national celebration is far inland. Business visitors should look at the last week of October, when the golf day, the summit and Pwani Innovation Week fall within three days of each other.

What is not known

We could not confirm the venue or ticket prices for Pwani Innovation Week, the entry fees for the golf day, or whether Mombasa itself plans any local Mashujaa Day event. We will add more dates once an organiser or venue confirms them.

Getting around is easiest by taxi or ride-hailing app after dark. If you cross between the island and the mainland, leave early, because queues at crossings can add time on event days.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is on in Mombasa from 12 to 31 October 2026?

Four dated events are confirmed: Mashujaa Day on Tuesday 20 October, the Uganda-Kenya Coast Open golf day at Vipingo Ridge on Saturday 24 October, Pwani Innovation Week from Monday 26 to Friday 30 October, and the Uganda-Kenya Coast Tourism & Innovation Summit on 26 and 27 October.

When is Mashujaa Day 2026?

Tuesday 20 October 2026. The national celebration is in Eldoret at Kipchoge Keino Stadium, with related events across three Rift Valley counties from 13 to 18 October, according to Kenyan government statements reported by Citizen Digital.

Where is the Uganda-Kenya tourism summit held?

At Sarova Whitesands Beach Resort & Spa in Mombasa on 26 and 27 October 2026, according to the Ugandan consulate in Mombasa.

Who organises Pwani Innovation Week?

Swahilipot Hub, which says the 2026 edition is the seventh and marks ten years of the hub.

Where is the Uganda-Kenya Coast Open golf day?

At the Vipingo Ridge PGA Baobab Course in Kilifi County, north of Mombasa, on Saturday 24 October 2026. It is a Stableford competition, and stay-and-play packages are available through the venue.

World.content:
LUSAKA · Culture

Six Lusaka events from 16 to 31 October 2026 are confirmed with an organiser or ticket page, from a jobs expo on Friday 16 October to a Halloween party on Friday 30 October. Prices are in kwacha and US$.

File photo: Kenneth Kaunda International Airport, Lusaka.

LUSAKA — This is the culture and events guide for 12 to 31 October 2026, for people who live in Zambia’s capital or are staying for a few weeks. Every event below has a date and venue and, where one exists, a price on the organiser, venue or ticket-platform page, checked on 11 October 2026.

Prices are in Zambian kwacha (K), each with its US$ value. We converted at the RT market rate of about K19.83 per US$ (11 October 2026), so US$1 buys roughly K20. Ticket platforms add booking fees, and card providers add their own exchange spreads.

The weekend festivals of 10 and 11 October, including R&G Oktoberfest, have already taken place and are not listed. Six events remain that we could confirm: business and study dates in the middle of the month, one premium evening, and a Halloween party. Listings that appear only on aggregator calendars are left out, so this guide is shorter than those calendars.

16 and 17 October: jobs, study and a premium evening

Friday 16 October, from 08:00 JOBEXPO Zambia Showgrounds, Lusaka · Ticket price not published A career and recruitment expo hosted by HRLeverage Zambia Limited, connecting job-seekers with employers. The Tickethost page gives an 08:00 start and lists registration as guest, delegate, exhibitor, student or speaker, but no price. Confirm the time and entry terms with the host on +260 765 676 314.

Saturday 17 October, 11:30 to 17:00 Zambia International College Fair 2026 Radisson Blu Hotel, 19029 Great East Road, Lusaka · Free, registration required A study-abroad fair with more than 20 universities from Canada, the UK, the USA, Malta, Egypt, China, Japan and other countries. The organiser, Nigeria International Education Fair, promises one-to-one talks with admission officers and scholarships of up to 30%. Register on Eventbrite.

Saturday 17 October, 10:00 Waxes & Oldies Rustic Flower Pots, 11104 Mboya Road, near Kabwata Cultural Village · K550 (about US$28) plus K5 booking fee A hands-on candle-making day run by Bourdine Body and Scents, with drinks, snacks and music included in the ticket. It suits small groups and newcomers who want to meet people. Tickets are on Tickethost.

Saturday 17 October, 17:00 to 21:00 L’Orangerie at Twilight Amber Grove, Ibex Hill, Lusaka · K2,500 per guest (about US$126) An upmarket evening with garden cocktails at sunset, canapés, a dessert service and a live performance by Tio Nason. The dress code is “elevated cocktail”. Tickets are limited and sold through Ticket Tailor.

26 to 31 October: technology and Halloween

Monday 26 and Tuesday 27 October, from 08:30 Africa Tech-Xpo 2026 Mulungushi International Conference Centre, Lusaka · Student pass K100 (about US$5) · Exhibition and Conference pass K500 (about US$25) The first pan-African edition of an exhibition that grew out of Zambia Tech-Xpo. The organiser says it connects innovation, capital, policy and infrastructure across Africa’s digital economy, with startups, investors, policymakers and technology leaders. Tickets are on Tickethost.

Friday 30 and Saturday 31 October, from 18:00 The Haunted Affairs Lusaka, venue not published · K100 (about US$5), plus K5 booking fee A Halloween party billed as a night of darkness, mystery, costumes and music, organised by Hidden Agenda.zm. The listing gives no venue beyond Lusaka, so confirm the location before you buy. The K5 booking fee is added at checkout. Tickets are on Tickethost.

What it means for you

Ticket prices are low in dollar terms. The paid events here start at about US$5 (K100) for the Tech-Xpo student pass and the Halloween party, and reach about US$28 (K550) for the candle-making day. Only the Amber Grove evening costs more than US$100 per guest. Check card fees with your bank before you travel.

For US readers with business in Zambia, the most useful dates are JOBEXPO on Friday 16 October and Africa Tech-Xpo on 26 and 27 October. Families weighing study abroad can meet US, UK and Canadian universities on Saturday 17 October at no cost, with registration.

Planning your Lusaka in October

Saturday 24 October is Zambia’s Independence Day, a public holiday marking independence from the United Kingdom in 1964. This year’s theme is “Zambia@62: Our Journey, Our Growth, Our Future”. We found no organiser-confirmed public event for that day, so we list none. Check the Zambian government’s announcements for official ceremonies, and expect some shops and offices to close.

For late nights, use a trusted driver or a ride-hailing service, and agree the fare or check the app price before you set off.

Each is missing an organiser-confirmed date, price or city, and most appear only on aggregator sites.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is on in Lusaka in the second half of October 2026?

Six events are confirmed: JOBEXPO Zambia on Friday 16 October, the Zambia International College Fair, Waxes & Oldies and L’Orangerie at Twilight on Saturday 17 October, Africa Tech-Xpo on Monday 26 and Tuesday 27 October, and The Haunted Affairs on 30 and 31 October.

How much do Lusaka events cost in October 2026?

Confirmed prices run from K100 (about US$5) for The Haunted Affairs and the Tech-Xpo student pass to K2,500 (about US$126) for L’Orangerie at Twilight. Waxes & Oldies costs K550 (about US$28). The Zambia International College Fair is free with registration, and JOBEXPO has no published price.

When is Zambia’s Independence Day in 2026?

Saturday 24 October 2026. It is a public holiday marking independence from the United Kingdom in 1964.

Which business events can visitors attend in Lusaka in October 2026?

JOBEXPO Zambia on Friday 16 October at the Showgrounds, starting at 08:00 according to Tickethost, and Africa Tech-Xpo 2026 on Monday 26 and Tuesday 27 October at the Mulungushi International Conference Centre. Tech-Xpo passes cost K100 (about US$5) for students and K500 (about US$25) for the exhibition and conference.

Is there a study-abroad fair in Lusaka in October 2026?

Yes. The Zambia International College Fair is on Saturday 17 October from 11:30 to 17:00 at the Radisson Blu Hotel, 19029 Great East Road. It is free with registration and lists more than 20 universities from countries including Canada, the UK and the USA.

World.title: Lula Rejects Court ‘Interference’ 14 Days Before Vote
World.content:
BRAZIL · POLITICS

Key Facts — What happened Lula joined a “March for Democracy” on Avenida Paulista on Sunday.

— The charge He told reporters the court made “many biased decisions,” per Poder360.

— The trigger A Sunday order suspended a pro-Lula WhatsApp channel.

— Crowd size “Thousands,” per Agência Brasil; no official estimate was published.

— The runoff Lula faces Flávio Bolsonaro on Sunday, 25 October.

— Prediction markets Polymarket gives Lula a 12.5% chance (11 October, 4:29 p.m. ET). Polymarket puts Flávio Bolsonaro’s chance of winning at 87% and Kalshi at 88% (Lula: 13% and 13% ), as of 11 October, 5:40 pm ET ; prices are bets, not polls.

Trailing in the polls, the president criticised the judges running the election before joining a São Paulo street march.

President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva accused Brazil’s electoral court of “biased decisions” on Sunday, 11 October. He then spoke at a rally on São Paulo’s Avenida Paulista, two weeks before the 25 October runoff.

His remarks followed a court order that told WhatsApp, owned by the US company Meta, to suspend a pro-Lula channel. For US investors in Latin America’s largest economy, it marks a sharper clash between the incumbent and the election’s referees.

Latin America Power Index · October 2026 edition Brazil ranks 1st of 14 with 75.0 points. Strongest pillar: military means (100); weakest: state capacity & security (56). Alignment group: Hedging. WatchRating below investment grade (BB); public debt at 93% of GDP. See the full index, the business lens and the data →

What Lula Said About the Court

Lula spoke to journalists in São Paulo before the march, the news site Poder360 reported. “We will not accept undue interference by the Electoral Justice,” he said.

He said he had seen “many biased decisions” for several days. He said the head of the electoral court should behave in a “civilised, republican” way and let the election run without interference.

Lula said his lawyers would ask the court’s president for an explanation. He added that his Workers’ Party (PT) would go to court that day to “balance the game” on social-media reach.

Poder360 published the remarks with a 94-second video of Lula speaking. Whether the party’s petition was actually filed on Sunday was not confirmed by Sunday evening.

This also signs you up to our weekday newsletter, The LatAm Brief. Nothing arrives until you click the confirmation link, and you can stop either with one click. Privacy policy

The WhatsApp Order Behind the Remarks

The court is the Superior Electoral Court (TSE), which runs and polices Brazilian elections. Its president, Kassio Nunes Marques, is a Supreme Court justice appointed in 2020 by former president Jair Bolsonaro.

On Sunday he suspended “Exército do Lula” (Lula’s Army), a WhatsApp channel created by Lula ally and federal deputy André Janones. Poder360 put its following at about 3.3 million.

The Rio Times reported that order in Brazil Gives WhatsApp 3 Hours to Shut Pro-Lula Channel. Later on Sunday afternoon, Agência Brasil reported that the court’s inspector-general, Ricardo Villas Bôas Cueva, overturned the suspension.

The March on Avenida Paulista

The “Marcha pela Democracia” filled most of the avenue, São Paulo’s best-known protest route, according to the state news agency Agência Brasil. It gave no crowd figure, and no police or official estimate was published.

Social movements and pop-music fan communities organised the march. Organised supporter groups of the football clubs Palmeiras and Corinthians, the São Paulo Pride organisers and student groups backed it.

Lula spoke from a sound truck outside MASP, the São Paulo Museum of Art. His official YouTube channel streamed the event live as “Lula em São Paulo: O Brasil Pronto Pra Mais.”

What Else Lula Said on Sunday

Speaking to reporters before the march, Lula called the coming week decisive. He pointed to Wednesday’s Senate vote on ending the “6×1” schedule, six working days for one day off.

He challenged the Liberal Party (PL), Flávio Bolsonaro’s conservative party, to show whether it backs two rest days a week. He called an opposition push to delay the vote until after the runoff an attempt to deceive voters.

He attacked the spending cuts announced by Flávio, which he called a “tesouraço” (big scissors). He compared them with the cuts made by Argentina’s President Javier Milei.

Lula said a constitutional amendment creating a Ministry of Public Security could advance this week. He also urged voters over 70 to turn out, citing first-round abstention of 21.08%.

Who Is in the Race

Lula, 80, leads the left-wing PT and has been president since January 2023. He is seeking a fourth term.

Flávio Bolsonaro is a PL senator for Rio de Janeiro and the eldest son of Jair Bolsonaro. He finished first in the 4 October first round and leads the runoff polls.

What It Means for You

US funds hold Brazilian shares and NYSE-listed firms such as Petrobras, Vale and Itaú. A sitting president questioning the electoral court adds uncertainty before the result.

Meta, which owns WhatsApp, is now at the centre of a Brazilian campaign fight. US tech firms face fast takedown orders from the court until 25 October.

What Prediction Markets Say

Prediction markets · who wins the runoff Implied chance of winning Brazil’s presidency on 25 October, from traders’ prices. Polymarket Flávio Bolsonaro 86.9% · Lula 12.5% (US$180 million traded) Kalshi (regulated in the US by the CFTC) Flávio Bolsonaro 88% · Lula 13% As of 11 October, 5:40 pm ET (22:40 Lisbon), updated every 20 minutes. Prices are bets, not polls, and can move fast. Why we show this: prediction markets turn real-money bets into a live probability that moves within minutes of the news, which is why investors, campaigns and newsrooms in the United States now follow them closely. We show them next to polls and official results, never instead of them.

On Polymarket, with about US$180 million traded on the election, bets gave Lula 12.5% at 4:29 p.m. ET on Sunday. Its margin market put a Flávio win by 4 to 8 points at 49%.

On Kalshi, which US regulators at the CFTC oversee, bets gave Flávio 87% and Lula 13% at 11:07 a.m. ET on Sunday.

Why we show this: prediction markets turn real-money bets into a live probability that moves within minutes of the news, which is why investors, campaigns and newsrooms in the United States now follow them closely. We show them next to polls and official results, never instead of them.

What Is Not Known

There is no official crowd figure for the march. No public reply from the TSE to Lula’s criticism was found by Sunday evening.

It is also unclear whether the PT filed its promised petition, and on what grounds.

What Comes Next

Monday, 12 October, is a national holiday in Brazil. The Senate votes on the 6×1 work week on Wednesday, 14 October.

Brazilians choose between Lula and Flávio on Sunday, 25 October.

Frequently Asked Questions

What did Lula say about the electoral court?

He said he would not accept undue interference and saw many biased decisions. He said his party would go to court over social-media reach.

Why is Lula criticising the court?

On Sunday the court’s president suspended a pro-Lula WhatsApp channel. Another judge later overturned that order, Agência Brasil reported.

How many people joined the march?

Agência Brasil reported thousands on Avenida Paulista. No police or official crowd estimate was published.

When is Brazil’s presidential runoff?

The runoff between Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro is on Sunday, 25 October. Polls close at 5 p.m. Brasília time.

World.title: Brazil Judge Restores 3.4M-Member Lula WhatsApp Channel
World.content:
BRAZIL · COURTS

Key Facts — What happened Brazil’s electoral inspector-general overturned the suspension of a pro-Lula WhatsApp channel.

— When Sunday afternoon, 11 October, hours after the court’s president ordered it.

— The channel Janones’s “Exército do Lula” has more than 3.4 million members.

— US platform The channel may run again on Meta’s WhatsApp pending a full-court ruling.

— Prediction markets Polymarket gives Lula 12.5% to win the 25 October runoff (11 October, 4:27 p.m. ET). Polymarket puts Flávio Bolsonaro’s chance of winning at 87% and Kalshi at 88% (Lula: 13% and 13% ), as of 11 October, 5:40 pm ET ; prices are bets, not polls.

A second judge at Brazil’s electoral court has lifted a ban on a pro-Lula channel hosted by a US-owned messaging app.

A pro-Lula channel on WhatsApp, owned by US company Meta Platforms, may operate again after a Brazilian judge overturned its suspension. Ricardo Villas Bôas Cueva, the electoral court’s inspector-general, reversed the order on Sunday afternoon, 11 October, state news agency Agência Brasil reported.

Earlier on Sunday, Kassio Nunes Marques, president of the Superior Electoral Court (TSE), had ordered WhatsApp to suspend it. The reversal leaves a US platform between two judges of the same court, two weeks before the 25 October runoff.

Latin America Power Index · October 2026 edition Brazil ranks 1st of 14 with 75.0 points. Strongest pillar: military means (100); weakest: state capacity & security (56). Alignment group: Hedging. WatchRating below investment grade (BB); public debt at 93% of GDP. See the full index, the business lens and the data →

What the Judge Decided

Cueva, the rapporteur of the case, restored the channel provisionally until the court’s full bench rules, the Bahia Econômica news site reported. He left room to reconsider if new facts justify a stricter measure.

Suspending a whole channel “exige demonstração da extensão e da reiteração das condutas,” he wrote. That means proof of how widespread and repeated the conduct is.

Milder steps against individual posts must first be shown to fall short, he added. In his view, the suspension came before evidence-gathering in the case was finished.

Federal deputy André Janones created the channel, “Exército do Lula” (Lula’s Army), to back President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva. Janones represents Minas Gerais for Rede Sustentabilidade, a small environmentalist party that supports Lula.

This also signs you up to our weekday newsletter, The LatAm Brief. Nothing arrives until you click the confirmation link, and you can stop either with one click. Privacy policy

Why the Channel Was Suspended

Flávio Bolsonaro’s campaign asked for the suspension. It argued the channel spread disinformation about cuts to Bolsa Família cash transfers and to pensions.

Flávio is a senator for the conservative Liberal Party (PL) and son of former president Jair Bolsonaro. He faces Lula, of the left-wing Workers’ Party (PT), in the runoff.

Nunes Marques said the channel repeated content the court had already judged untrue, Agência Brasil reported. One example was a claim that Flávio favoured dropping Our Lady of Aparecida as Brazil’s patron saint.

Nunes Marques is a Supreme Court justice appointed by Jair Bolsonaro in 2020. Cueva sits on the Superior Court of Justice (STJ), Brazil’s top court for non-constitutional cases.

The Case Behind the Dispute

On Saturday, 10 October, the TSE said Cueva had admitted Flávio’s abuse case against Lula, running mate Geraldo Alckmin and Janones. The filing seeks to strip Lula and Alckmin of their registration and to suspend the channel.

Cueva ordered no suspension then. He gave Flávio 72 hours to supply more information, and the defendants five days to file their defence.

The court stressed that admitting the case does not mean the allegations are true.

Before the reversal, Janones said “A censura já começou” (censorship has already begun), Agência Brasil reported. Lula told journalists in São Paulo he would not accept “intromissão indevida da Justiça Eleitoral” (undue interference by the electoral court).

Lula’s campaign had called the suspension a cause of “estranheza e revolta” (surprise and outrage), Poder360 reported.

What It Means for You

For US investors in Meta, two opposite orders in one day show how fast Brazilian judges can direct a US platform. Earlier on Sunday, WhatsApp had been given three hours to switch the channel off.

For holders of Brazilian assets, the runoff sets economic policy from January 2027. Court fights over online campaigning add noise to a race that bets favour Flávio to win.

We show them next to polls and official results, never instead of them.

On Polymarket, with about US$180 million traded on the election, bets gave Lula a 12.5% chance at 4:27 p.m. ET on Sunday. On Kalshi, which the US CFTC regulates, Flávio stood at 87% and Lula at 13% at 11:07 a.m. ET.

Why we show this: prediction markets turn real-money bets into a live probability that moves within minutes of the news, which is why investors, campaigns and newsrooms in the United States now follow them closely. We show them next to polls and official results, never instead of them.

What Is Not Known

It is not known whether WhatsApp had reactivated the channel by Sunday evening. No TSE note on Cueva’s decision had been published.

It is unclear when the full court will rule, or whether Flávio’s campaign will challenge the reversal.

What Comes Next

The abuse case continues, with Flávio’s 72-hour and the defendants’ five-day deadlines running this week. Monday, 12 October, is a national holiday in Brazil.

The full TSE bench must still decide whether the channel stays open until the runoff on Sunday, 25 October.

Background: Brazil Tax Reform 2026 Replaces Five Taxes With Two VATs.

Frequently Asked Questions

Who restored the “Exército do Lula” channel?

Ricardo Villas Bôas Cueva, the electoral court’s inspector-general and rapporteur of the case, restored it. He overturned the suspension on Sunday afternoon, 11 October.

Why did he lift the suspension?

He said suspending a whole channel requires proof of how widespread and repeated the conduct is. Milder steps against individual posts must first be shown to fail.

Who ordered the original suspension?

TSE president Kassio Nunes Marques ordered it earlier on Sunday at the request of Flávio Bolsonaro’s campaign. He said the channel repeated content the court had judged untrue.

When is Brazil’s presidential runoff?

Brazilians choose between Flávio Bolsonaro and Lula on Sunday, 25 October. The full electoral court has yet to rule on the channel.

World.title: Brazil Women Beat Argentina 3-1, Lose Two NWSL Players
World.content:
BRAZIL · SPORT

Key Facts — The country Brazil, host of the 2027 Women’s World Cup.

— What happened Brazil beat Argentina 3-1 in a friendly on Saturday, 10 October.

— The decision Brazil’s football federation released two NWSL players on Sunday, 11 October.

— The injuries Bruninha (Gotham FC) tore a ligament; Angelina (Orlando Pride) broke her nose.

— The crowd More than 20,000 fans at Beira-Rio, a 2027 World Cup venue.

— Next Brazil face Argentina again near Recife on Tuesday, 13 October.

Brazil’s World Cup rehearsal drew a big home crowd, but it cost Brazil two players from American clubs.

Brazil’s women’s national team beat Argentina 3-1 in a friendly at Estádio Beira-Rio in Porto Alegre on Saturday, 10 October. The win cost two clubs in the US National Women’s Soccer League (NWSL) a player each.

On Sunday, 11 October, Brazil’s football federation, the CBF, released defender Bruninha of Gotham FC and midfielder Angelina of Orlando Pride. The CBF said scans confirmed a complete rupture of Bruninha’s anterior cruciate ligament, a major knee injury.

Latin America Power Index · October 2026 edition Brazil ranks 1st of 14 with 75.0 points. Strongest pillar: military means (100); weakest: state capacity & security (56). Alignment group: Hedging. WatchRating below investment grade (BB); public debt at 93% of GDP. See the full index, the business lens and the data →

Angelina was diagnosed with a broken nose, according to the federation’s statement, published in full by the sports daily Lance. Saturday’s game was the women’s team’s first match at Beira-Rio, a venue for the 2027 Women’s World Cup.

How Brazil Beat Argentina

Luany opened the scoring in the 26th minute, reported Agência Brasil, the public news agency. Geyse doubled the lead with a bicycle kick in the 38th minute.

Captain Angelina made it 3-0 shortly before half-time, a goal Lance also credited to her. Maricel Pereyra, who plays for São Paulo FC, pulled one back for Argentina about six minutes after the restart.

Head coach Arthur Elias missed the game through suspension, so his assistant Rodrigo Iglesias led the team. Brazil made several changes in the second half, and the home side lost some rhythm, the agency said.

Follow this story Get an email when there’s news on Brazil Email address Follow Free. One email a day at most, and only when there is news. This also signs you up to our weekday newsletter, The LatAm Brief. Nothing arrives until you click the confirmation link, and you can stop either with one click. Privacy policy

Two NWSL Players Ruled Out

The CBF said Bruninha sprained her knee during the match, and tests then confirmed the ligament rupture. She will stay with the squad for treatment until the October international window ends, then have surgery.

Angelina suffered a direct blow to the face, the federation said. She will continue her treatment with her club, Orlando Pride, in Florida.

Bruninha, a full-back, plays for Gotham FC, the club based in the New York and New Jersey area. Angelina wore the captain’s armband for Brazil on Saturday, according to Agência Brasil.

A World Cup Rehearsal in Porto Alegre

The crowd topped 20,000, according to Lance, while Agência Brasil put the attendance above 28,000. Both describe a big turnout for a women’s friendly in southern Brazil.

Aline Pellegrino, FIFA’s director of legacy and institutional relations for the 2027 tournament, spoke to Lance after the match. “Today was a day when the whole stadium saw the women’s national team for the first time,” she said.

Porto Alegre’s city government ran a drive to hand out tickets for the friendly. Its World Cup office says Beira-Rio will host seven matches in 2027, six group games and one round-of-16 tie.

The city says the tournament runs from 24 June to 25 July 2027. Arena Pernambuco, the venue for Tuesday’s rematch, is also a host stadium.

What It Means for You

For NWSL fans, Gotham FC loses a Brazil international defender to a serious knee injury. A cruciate ligament rupture that needs surgery usually means months out, though the CBF gave no timeline.

Orlando Pride supporters should watch for updates on Angelina, whose treatment now moves to the club. No return date was given for either player.

For US travelers, Saturday’s crowd was an early test of a 2027 host stadium. US citizens need a visa to visit Brazil, so fans planning World Cup trips should apply early.

What Is Not Known

The CBF has not said how long Bruninha or Angelina will be out, or whether it will call up replacements. Reports also differ on which knee Bruninha injured and on the exact minute she was hurt.

No official attendance figure from the CBF or the stadium was available. It is also not known how either US club will cover the absence.

What Comes Next

Brazil play Argentina again on Tuesday, 13 October, at Arena Pernambuco in São Lourenço da Mata, near Recife. Kickoff is 8:30 p.m. Brasília time, which is 7:30 p.m. ET, according to Agência Brasil.

Bruninha will stay with the squad until the October window ends and then have surgery. Angelina’s treatment continues with Orlando Pride.

Background: Brazil Tax Reform 2026 Replaces Five Taxes With Two VATs.

Frequently Asked Questions

What was the score of Brazil vs Argentina in the women’s friendly?

Brazil won 3-1 at Estádio Beira-Rio in Porto Alegre on Saturday, 10 October. Luany, Geyse and Angelina scored for Brazil, and Maricel Pereyra scored for Argentina.

Why were Bruninha and Angelina released from Brazil’s squad?

The CBF said Bruninha suffered a complete rupture of a knee ligament and Angelina broke her nose. Both were hurt in Saturday’s match against Argentina.

Which NWSL clubs do Bruninha and Angelina play for?

Bruninha plays for Gotham FC, and Angelina plays for Orlando Pride. Both clubs compete in the US National Women’s Soccer League.

When do Brazil and Argentina play again?

The second friendly is on Tuesday, 13 October, at Arena Pernambuco near Recife. Kickoff is 8:30 p.m. Brasília time, which is 7:30 p.m. ET.
