World.title: Iraq’s non-oil revenues hit 8.7 trillion Iraqi dinars by July 2026
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq’s General Commission for Federal Revenues Allocation revealed on Sunday that non-oil revenues reached approximately 8.7 trillion Iraqi dinars (approximately $5.74 billion) by July 2026, compared to about seven trillion Iraqi dinars (around $4.62 billion) during the same period in 2025.

Iraq’s non-oil revenues rose by 1.7 trillion Iraqi dinars (about $1.12 billion) and at a growth rate of 23.5 percent, according to the state-run Iraqi News Agency (INA).

These revenues accounted for approximately 22 percent of total federal revenues for the same period.

The Iraqi Ministry of Finance said last week that the country’s total revenues reached approximately 39.09 trillion Iraqi dinars (nearly $30 billion) until the end of July 2026, with oil revenues accounting for about 78 percent of total state resources.

During the first seven months of 2026, Iraq’s total government spending reached 65.42 trillion Iraqi dinars (approximately $43.21 billion).

This massive expenditure, combined with a sharp decline in oil revenues due to disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz, left a major budget deficit of 26.3 trillion ($17.37 billion) to 29.2 trillion Iraqi dinars ($19.28 billion) for the January–July period.

The International Monetary Fund (IMF) and the World Bank project a severe economic contraction for Iraq in 2026, largely due to prolonged disruptions to oil production and export logistics caused by regional conflicts and the closure of the Strait of Hormuz.

However, the two international institutions expect a robust economic rebound in 2027 as energy markets stabilize and trade flows normalize.

World.title: Iraqis submit over 10,000 weapon registration requests within week
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Iraqi Ministry of Interior revealed on Sunday that it received over 10,000 applications from Iraqis requesting to register their firearms during the first week of October.

The step is part of a statewide push to put all armaments under state control.

According to Mohammed Ali al-Hassoun, the ministry’s spokesperson, residents in Baghdad and other provinces submitted 10,222 applications between October 2 and 9.

According to officials, the move demonstrates rising public awareness of the need to limit gun ownership.

Unlicensed guns are often used in tribal confrontations and personal revenge attacks throughout Iraq, weakening the state’s authority over the use of force.

The Iraqi government has initiated a mission to seize all firearms held by tribes and armed organizations. Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi has set June 2027 as a deadline for militias to submit their weapons.

Al-Hassoun said that the ministry maintains its efforts to regulate weapons possession and improve security across Iraqi provinces. He added that the ministry is expediting weapon registration procedures.

The Undersecretary of the Ministry of Interior, Hussein al-Awadi, said in September that the government is proceeding with the decision to restrict the possession of weapons exclusively to security forces.

Al-Awadi noted that Iraqi authorities intend to collect up to six million weapons in the coming months.

World.title: Iraq attends Riyadh energy summit as Saudi minister declares city ‘capital of energy security’
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq attended the 17th International Energy Forum Ministerial Meeting (IEF17) in Riyadh on Sunday, despite fatal strikes on the Saudi capital’s airport, where top energy officials discussed global energy security, oil market stability, and investment.

Iraq’s Oil Minister, Basim Mohammed Khudair, attended the event, which brought together ministers, business executives, and officials from international organizations under the topic “Energy Security and Shared Goals in a New Era.”

The conference went forward despite bombings on Riyadh’s King Khalid International Airport, which Saudi officials blamed on Yemen’s Houthi militia.

The violence heightened security fears in the monarchy, which was hosting key foreign energy executives.

Opening the conference, Saudi Energy Minister Prince Abdulaziz bin Salman presented a message of resilience, stating that the country would continue to meet its energy promises despite the problems it confronts.

“No one can break our resolve, for we are like the phoenix, always rising from the ashes,” Prince Abdulaziz declared, according to an English translation of his Arabic comments.

“We value our commitments and strive to honor them no matter the circumstances,” he continued, referring to Saudi Arabia and its capital as the “capital of energy security.”

The Minister also cited Saudi Arabia’s East-West Pipeline, which distributes crude oil to the Red Sea port of Yanbu, as an example of infrastructure built to ensure energy supplies when regular shipping routes are disrupted.

The problem is especially important to Iraq, one of OPEC’s biggest oil producers, which depends significantly on exports via the Arabian Gulf and has been looking into alternate pipeline routes via Turkey and even Syria.

Iraq’s involvement comes as the country strives to enhance ties with Saudi Arabia and other regional partners in energy investment, infrastructure, and economic growth.

Saudi Arabia, Italy, and Nigeria convened the ministerial conference, which focused on ensuring stable energy supplies, robust infrastructure, diversifying supply chains, and strengthening communication between producing and consuming nations.

Participants expressed solidarity and support with Saudi Arabia after assaults on civilian infrastructure, and the conference welcomed news that the United States will rejoin the International Energy Forum.

The gathering also discussed investments in oil and gas production, refining, transportation networks, and future energy technologies, as well as initiatives to promote market transparency and international collaboration.

World.title: Iraq discusses oil and gas projects with TotalEnergies, ConocoPhillips
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi highlighted on Sunday the importance of recovering associated gas, given Iraq’s significant potential in this sector.

Al-Zaidi’s remarks took place during his meeting in Baghdad with Chairman and CEO of TotalEnergies, Patrick Pouyanne, and President of ConocoPhilips, Andy O’Brien, according to a statement released by the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO).

The meeting addressed strategies for developing oil and associated gas resources at the Bin Umar field in the southern province of Basra. Additionally, they discussed establishing a timeline for increasing oil and gas production from this field and enhancing output at other fields.

Al-Zaidi outlined the government’s plans to fully utilize the country’s gas resources and permanently stop gas imports within the next few years.

Pouyanne and O’Brien expressed their willingness to increase efforts to meet the established timelines for increasing production rates.

The Bin Umar field stands as one of southern Iraq’s most promising oil and gas reservoirs. The Iraqi government seeks to develop the field in partnership with a French-American consortium, an important step to stop gas flaring and achieve energy self-sufficiency.

TotalEnergies is already spearheading the massive “Integrated Gas Growth Project” in southern Iraq, an initiative focused on gas investment and solar power generation.

As a prominent US investment entity, ConocoPhillips is set to develop strategic fields and modernize them with cutting-edge technology.

Former Prime Minister Mohammed Shia al-Sudani said in June 2024 that associated gas recovery in Iraq had risen to over 60 percent, with the ultimate goal of completely ending gas flaring by 2028.

World.title: Iraq PM plans Saudi Arabia and Kuwait visits
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister Ali Falih Al-Zaidi is predicted to visit Saudi Arabia and Kuwait this week for talks on regional security, oil export routes, and long-standing bilateral disputes, according to Iraqi government sources, as escalating attacks on Saudi Arabia raise regional tensions.

The scheduled visit follows a horrific strike on Riyadh’s King Khalid International Airport on Saturday, which killed at least 12 people and wounded over 300.

The international airport was attacked again on Sunday, with Yemen’s Houthi movement claiming responsibility.

Iraq condemned the Houthi strikes on Sunday, expressing support for Saudi Arabia and warning that attacks on civilians and infrastructure endanger regional security and stability.

According to Sabah al-Numan, spokesman for the Commander-in-Chief of the Iraqi Armed Forces, Baghdad rejects further military escalation and instead advocates for an end to hostilities, civilian protection, and a stronger emphasis on discourse to address regional issues.

The worsening security situation has created concerns regarding travel plans, however no official notification has been made that al-Zaidi’s visit has been postponed.

Security cooperation is anticipated to be a major focus in Riyadh, where the Iraqi prime minister will likely address regional de-escalation, particularly the situation in Yemen, as well as attempts to avoid attacks on neighboring nations.

According to a government source reported by Shafaq News, Al-Zaidi is anticipated to underline Iraq’s condemnation of strikes conducted from its territory against Gulf nations, as well as its determination to hold those guilty accountable.

Relations between Baghdad and Riyadh have strained recently, with Saudis claiming that drones fired from Iraqi territory attacked its East-West oil pipeline in September.

The visit will also discuss the possibility of reactivating the long-idle Iraqi-Saudi oil pipeline, which would provide Baghdad with an alternate export route to the Red Sea.

The roughly 1,568-kilometer pipeline was constructed in the 1980s to transport Iraqi oil from the Al-Zubair district of Basra through Saudi Arabia to the Red Sea export terminals at Yanbu.

It discontinued operations in 1990 when Iraq invaded Kuwait, and Saudi Arabia subsequently reused parts of the infrastructure on their territory.

Reviving the route has become more important as the prolonged regional conflict delays shipping across the Strait of Hormuz, exposing Iraq’s dependency on southern oil export ports in the Arabian Gulf.

Al-Zaidi is next slated to go to Kuwait, where discussions would center on maritime boundary delineation, transportation via the Khor Abdullah waterway, and Iraq’s water rights.

The planned Gulf travel follows the cancelation of a previous Saudi visit in July due to increased military tensions between Iraq and Saudi Arabia.

World.title: TotalEnergies CEO visits Baghdad to meet Iraq PM for oil and gas investment talks
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – TotalEnergies CEO Patrick Pouyanné met with Iraqi Prime Minister Ali Falih al-Zaidi in Baghdad on Sunday to discuss growing oil and gas output, as Iraq attempts to improve its energy economy despite impediments to shipments via the Strait of Hormuz caused by the continuing regional conflict.

Pouyanné was joined by ConocoPhillips CEO Andy O’Brien and accompanying delegations for negotiations about investment in Basra’s Bin Umar oilfield, which includes plans to expand crude output and collect associated gas.

According to the Prime Minister’s Office, the conference discussed investment methods and deadlines for increasing production at Bin Umar, as well as prospects to boost output at other Iraqi oilfields.

Al-Zaidi emphasized the necessity of growing Iraq’s associated gas resources, stating the government’s goal of eliminating gas imports in the future years by increasing local production and making better use of gas that is now wasted via flaring.

Despite the lack of fresh investment estimates or strict deadlines, firm leaders stated a desire to speed work and reach production objectives.

The high-level conference comes at a crucial moment for Iraq’s energy industry, as the continued regional violence and disruptions to shipping via the Strait of Hormuz highlight the country’s reliance on southern oil export ports.

Iraq is also looking for other export routes to minimize its dependency on the strait, such as a massive oil pipeline that would link southern Iraq to Syria’s Mediterranean coast via Baniyas.

The planned route might let Iraqi petroleum reach foreign markets without traveling through Hormuz, thus improving export security during times of regional unrest.

TotalEnergies has previously indicated interest in developing alternate energy export routes, including via Syria, but Sunday’s official statement did not say if the planned pipeline was mentioned during the Baghdad conference.

The French energy company is already a big investment in Iraq, with projects aimed at expanding oil output, collecting associated gas, and boosting power generation.

Iraq continues to depend on imported gas for power generation, despite having huge gas reserves generated alongside crude oil.

The meeting with TotalEnergies and ConocoPhillips shows Iraq’s attempts to recruit foreign knowledge and investment while tackling two significant weaknesses in its energy sector: reliance on imported gas and reliance on export routes threatened by regional violence.

Progress in oilfield expansion, gas capture, and alternate export facilities might help Iraq enhance its energy security and preserve its position as a major oil producer in the face of increasing geopolitical challenges.

World.title: Iraq’s oil exports to South Korea hit 38.3 million barrels in eight months
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – South Korea’s state-owned Korea National Oil Corporation (KNOC) announced that it imported 38.34 million barrels of crude oil from Iraq during the first eight months of 2026.

The volume represents a decrease of 45.6 percent compared to the same period in 2025.

Saudi Arabia was the largest oil supplier to South Korea, with 196.21 million barrels between January and August 2026, a 15.65 percent decline compared to the same period in 2025.

The United States was the second-largest oil supplier to South Korea, with 131.09 million barrels, and the UAE followed with 101.55 million barrels.

Iraq’s oil exports to South Korea fell from 70.55 million barrels during the first eight months in 2025 to 38.34 million barrels in the same period in 2026.

Iraq was the fourth largest crude oil supplier to South Korea in the first half of 2026, accounting for 7.4 percent of the country’s total oil imports.

Iraq’s average oil shipments to South Korea totaled 113.7 million barrels in 2025, which is an average of 311,500 barrels per day. This represents a 12 percent increase compared to 2024.

World.title: Iraq, Turkey discuss oil-for-financing deal to fund Development Road project
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq is discussing an oil-for-financing agreement with Turkey to establish a fund for the Development Road project, where Turkish companies will execute construction in exchange for crude oil, while the project’s first phase will be backed by a World Bank loan.

Director of Projects at the General Company for Iraqi Railways, Fadel Abbas, confirmed that a joint financial framework is being shaped to let Turkish firms carry out infrastructure works paid for through oil exports.

The initiative aims to upgrade Iraq’s railway network, connect several provinces, and provide passenger and freight transport services, according to Abbas.

The Development Road’s primary objective is to transport goods from al-Faw Grans Port to Turkey—and onward to Europe—and vice versa.

Work is currently underway to finalize an agreement with Turkey to establish a fund that would finance the project’s implementation by Turkish companies through an oil-for-financing arrangement, according to the state-run Iraqi News Agency (INA).

The $17 billion project, which will connect the al-Faw Grand Port in southern Iraq to the Turkish border by constructing a railway and road network, is anticipated to transform Iraq into a transit center by cutting the time it takes to travel from Asia to Europe.

In addition to pipelines for energy transportation, the project’s railway will significantly assist in the transportation of commodities, with a first-phase capacity of 3.5 million tons and a second-phase capacity of 7.5 million tons.

By connecting the port city of Basra to Turkey via an overland route, the logistics project will compete with Egypt’s Suez Canal and establish Basra as a gateway to Europe.

World.title: Government slams UN rights body for 'practising double standards'
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Amid the clampdown in Delhi, Indian govt for the second time in two days slammed Office of the UN High Commissioner for Human Rights (OHCHR) for raising concerns about mass detentions in the city, saying this constituted an unacceptable interference in India's internal affairs.

While Indian mission to UN in Geneva said Saturday Indian citizens exercise their right to peaceful assembly subject to "reasonable restrictions" in the interest of public order, the ministry of external affairs tweaked the phrasing to "maintenance of public order and safety".

Govt also accused the UN human rights office of practising double standards, alluding to the crackdown in PoK, saying this erodes the credibility of its standing and contributes to loss of faith in multilateralism.

"We also note OHCHR has an approach of extreme selectivity when it comes to public positions. Violent responses to protests in our neighbourhood have gone uncommented, as indeed have law enforcement actions in its own vicinity," said MEA, also referring to action in countries like France, Belgium and Germany without naming them.

The UN body had urged Indian authorities to release all those detained.

The MEA said India is the world's largest democracy, where the right to peaceful assembly is guaranteed by Constitution and safeguarded by robust institutions, an independent judiciary and a free media.





"As in every democracy, Indian citizens exercise this right subject to the maintenance of public order... Our law enforcement authorities act strictly in accordance with the law, and our courts remain available to all for the redressal of any grievances," it said, adding OHCHR's concerns were unwarranted.

World.title: CJI: No meet with Congress, it'll violate 'separation of power'
World.content:
NEW DELHI: CJI Surya Kant Sunday declined requests from

president

and MP

, who wanted to meet him Monday to apprise him about "vote chori" allegations amid protests in Delhi seeking CEC Gyanesh Kumar's resignation.

In an email response, the CJI said similar issues were already pending adjudication before

Supreme Court

and a meeting on the issue raised by the netas would "contravene the iconic principles of separation of power, which is part of the basic structure of Constitution", sources in the CJI office told TOI.

The response said SC was not endowed with any administrative power in this regard and only had an adjudicatory role under Constitution.

It said the party or any of its functionaries could file a petition highlighting their grievances and the court was bound to adjudicate it. The sources said the CJI stated that SC was committed to giving a priority hearing to important issues and serving citizens of the country.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

The sources said the CJI wrote that if so advised, a petition could be filed by the person concerned or the party in SC before 4pm Monday, and would be given priority hearing on the judicial side along with other similar petitions.





Kharge, in a social media post Sunday, said, "We will continue our fight. Tomorrow, we are also going to meet CJI. I have written a letter, and Rahul Gandhi has also written a letter. We have scheduled a meeting between 4-5pm, during which we will apprise him of the situation... Chaos is being created in the country by home minister and PM, and everywhere an undeclared emergency is imposed."

World.title: Congress could reiterate request for meeting with CJI today

NEW DELHI: Congress, which had planned a march to Supreme Court for a meeting with CJI Surya Kant on the SIR-CEC issue Monday, could be forced to engineer another protest programme, with the CJI turning down its request for appointment late Sunday.The Congress brass could reiterate its request for a meeting Monday.Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge had posted on X that a meeting was scheduled, leading many in the opposition, including legal eagles, to express surprise, saying it would be a first-of-its-kind meet, if it happened.Rahul Gandhi cancelled a campaign event in Goa and returned home after "chhatron ki goonj" in Chennai to oversee the preparations for a massive protest that Congress has planned. He issued a general appeal to citizens, opposition parties and civil society to join the march to SC, saying Narendra Modi, Amit Shah, Ajit Doval and Mohan Bhagwat could not "silence India's voice".Rahul said on X that the "March for Democracy - Dilli Chalo" will start from Barakhambha Road, and has asked people to assemble there.Slamming the police crackdown on protests, Kharge said what is happening in the capital under the Modi govt did not happen during the Emergency."We will apprise the CJI of the situation. We cannot demand anything from him, but we will place our concerns before him with folded hands and request his intervention," he had said, adding that he and Rahul have written to CJI.Sources had said the letter to the CJI detailed the key points of the memorandum to be submitted to him, as well as the police crackdown and harassment of protesters by vigilantes.AICC general secretary KC Venugopal asked party workers from all states to converge in the capital for the mega surge. State presidents, including Rao Narender of Haryana, Ganesh Godiyal of Uttarakhand and Govind Dotasara of Rajasthan, issued instructions to party workers to leave for Delhi in large numbers - an indication of the kind of mobilisation the opposition party has set rolling.

World.title: 'Deeply concerning': India condemns attack on vessel carrying Indian crew off Oman coast
World.content:
Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The ministry of external affairs on Sunday condemned the repeated attacks on commercial vessels in the Strait of Hormuz after two merchant ships carrying Indian seafarers came under attack.In a statement, the ministry said the recurring attacks on commercial shipping in the region were deeply concerning and risked further aggravating an already volatile situation."We condemn the attacks on commercial vessels in the Strait of Hormuz region on 11 October 2026. MT PETRO DOLPHIN was reportedly struck by a drone, with two of the 11 Indian seafarers onboard reported missing," it said."MT VALTHERA, a Marshall Islands-flagged tanker, was struck by an unknown projectile, resulting in a fire onboard. All 11 Indian seafarers onboard MT VALTHERA are reported to be safe. The Embassy of India in Muscat is closely monitoring the situation and coordinating with the Omani authorities and respective ship management companies for the rescue of missing Indians and to provide all possible assistance to the Indian crew," it added.MEA also reiterated the need for immediate de-escalation and a resolution to the ongoing conflict between the United States and Iran through dialogue and diplomacy."The safety and security of Indian seafarers remain a priority for the government of India. The recurring attacks on commercial shipping in the region are deeply concerning and risk further aggravating an already volatile situation," it said."India reiterates the need for immediate de-escalation and a resolution to the ongoing conflict through dialogue and diplomacy. Attacks on commercial vessels, seafarers and civilian infrastructure must cease. Freedom of navigation and the safe, unimpeded flow of maritime commerce through international waterways, in accordance with international law, must be upheld," it added.This comes after a vessel carrying 11 Indian seafarers came under a drone attack off the coast of Oman, leaving two crew members missing while nine were rescued.Indians have been facing dangers in the Middle East recently amid renewed tensions. On Saturday, 11 Indians were injured when Riyadh airport came under attack. A day later, the Indian embassy in Saudi Arabia announced that one of them had died.The embassy of India in Riyadh said it had been following up on Saturday's attack and was in touch with local authorities and hospital officials to enquire about the condition of the injured Indians.

World.title: Owaisi urges 'Muslims voters' to build own leadership, takes aim at SP and Congress
World.content:
, the India Majlis-e-Ittehadul Muslimeen (AIMIM) chief, on Sunday widened his party's political outreach in Azamgarh in the poll-bound Uttar Pradesh, where he called for "greater political independence among minority communities".

Targeting both, the SP chief Akhilesh Yadav and his ally the Congress, Owaisi urged voters from the minority communities, to move beyond traditional political loyalties.

During his address, the AIMIM chief spoke about Muslim political representation, the legacy of national leaders and the law governing the appointment of election commissioners.

He argued that minority communities should build their own political strength instead of relying on figures associated with traditional parties.

âWe no longer need a Gandhi or a Nehru; we need our own leaders... No one speaks about our suffering. Yet today, the police detain someone and order them not to stage a protest for a year... I see people from within our own ranks saying, 'Oh Muslims! Support them; the likes of Nehru and Gandhi will emerge from among them'... That is the difference between them and Owaisi. They say, 'Support them'. I say, 'You become the leader'.





We are not slaves to anyone; we will not simply run after someone just because they claim to be the next Nehru or Gandhi... We no longer need a Gandhi or a Nehru; we need our own leaders,â he said.

Since Independence, minority voters have frequently backed the Congress and regional parties such as the SP, Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP) and Rashtriya Janata Dal (RJD). Owaisi argued that such electoral support had not resulted in proportionate representation in positions of power.

Owaisi takes swipe at Congress

Taking a potshot at the opposition, Owaisi referred to the historical relationship between Jawaharlal Nehru, Mahatma Gandhi and Maulana Abul Kalam Azad.

He used the episode to question whether established parties genuinely empower minority leaders or primarily seek their communities' electoral support.

âNehru wrote that if we removed the Maulana [Abul Kalam Azad], it would cause damage.

So, it became evident that only the Muslim vote was desired. Gandhi was saying, 'Do not appoint Azad; appoint some other Muslim instead'... What Gandhi had suggested back then is exactly what Akhilesh has put into practice today...â he said.

Owaisi presented these developments as an example of what he described as the tokenisation of minority representation by mainstream political parties. He linked his criticism to Akhilesh Yadav's distribution of election tickets, alleging that the SP had failed to encourage genuinely independent Muslim leadership.

Targets Yogi's '80:20' political narrative

Earlier in the day, Owaisi also criticised Uttar Pradesh chief minister Yogi Adityanath's frequently cited â80% versus 20%â political formulation, arguing that economic inequality deserved greater attention.

Countering the chief minister's framing, the AIMIM leader described the divide as one between â99% and 1%â, shifting the focus towards disparities between the economically disadvantaged majority and a small, affluent section.

Citing data from the Uttar Pradesh department of economics and statistics for 2024â25, Owaisi said Azamgarh ranked fourth among districts in the state in terms of the number of people living in poverty.

âThe state's department of economics and Statistics acknowledges that Azamgarh ranks fourth among the districts in Uttar Pradesh with the highest number of poor people. This is what the UP government's data for 2024â25 reveals, yet the chief minister speaks of an 80% vs. 20% divide,â the AIMIM chief said.

World.title: Another showdown in Delhi? INDIA bloc to hold protest over CEC; CJP gives 24-hour ultimatum
World.content:
Supreme Court steps in after crackdown

CJP vows to return to streets

BJP hits back at opposition

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The Congress and other opposition parties will march to the Supreme Court on Monday, October 12, demanding chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar's resignation over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. The protest comes a day after a police crackdown on demonstrators in Delhi and amid fresh political tensions over the alleged misuse of force against protesters.Leader of opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi has called on young people, opposition parties and civil society groups to join the march. The Congress has named it "Chalo Delhi - March for Democracy" and said participants will assemble at 1.30pm at the Connaught Place-Barakhamba Road junction.The opposition plans to submit a memorandum to Chief Justice of India Surya Kant, demanding an end to alleged "vote chori", a halt to SIR and Kumar's resignation. However, sources said on Sunday night that the CJI had not agreed to meet Gandhi and Leader of Opposition in the Rajya Sabha Mallikarjun Kharge, who had sought an appointment between 4pm and 5pm on Monday.Rahul, in a post on X, urged people to unite beyond party, gender, caste, community and state."Yesterday, the nation's young came out in Delhi to peacefully protest. They came with love in their hearts, not hatred or anger. They were beaten, both by cops and BJP goons. This is not the India we want," he said."Tomorrow, we will march to the Supreme Court as Indians, united beyond party, gender, caste, community and state. Youth, all opposition parties, civil society groups, all those who believe in democracy and stand by the Constitution of India, will walk with us," he added.The march follows Saturday's police action against protesters demanding Kumar's removal. Several demonstrators, including activists of the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), were detained as security personnel prevented them from reaching the designated protest site.On Sunday, the Supreme Court directed authorities to immediately lift prohibitory orders under Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita around the apex court complex. A bench of Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana said peaceful citizens should not face illegal detention and that movement across Delhi must be allowed in accordance with the law.The court was hearing petitions challenging the police crackdown and detentions, along with a contempt plea alleging disobedience of its orders.Meanwhile, CPI(M) Rajya Sabha MP John Brittas was taken to Ram Manohar Lohia Hospital after he was allegedly manhandled by police during Sunday's protest. He later sought an independent investigation and accountability from the President, the Rajya Sabha chairman and the CJI.Brittas alleged that police personnel dragged him for around 50 metres, forcibly put him in a vehicle and assaulted him inside it before leaving him by the roadside. Congress MP Shashi Tharoor condemned the alleged mistreatment and called for an investigation.CJP activists also vowed to continue their agitation after Abhijeet Dipke, Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka were released following their preventive detention."We will take to the streets again; we will not be intimidated by people like Amit Shah and Modi. Throw us in jail not just once, but a hundred times," Dipke said.Delhi Police DCP Neha Yadav defended the detentions, citing alleged law-and-order violations during previous demonstrations, including stone-pelting, arson and damage to public property. She said prohibitory orders had been imposed in several areas to maintain public safety.Opposition leaders, however, accused the government of suppressing dissent. RJD leader Tejashwi Yadav said "an Emergency has been declared", while Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav alleged that women protesters had been mistreated.The BJP dismissed the allegations and accused the opposition of creating chaos. Union minister Sukanta Majumdar said the opposition "occasionally makes its presence felt, much like a cockroach crawling across one's back."BJP leader Karuna Sagar also challenged Rahul Gandhi and other opposition leaders to follow the constitutional procedure for removing the CEC. He said any evidence of wrongdoing should be presented before Parliament.Union minister of state Tokhan Sahu defended the electoral roll revision process, saying it had taken place under successive governments. Delhi chief minister Rekha Gupta also criticised the opposition protests and praised Delhi Police for maintaining public safety.The latest confrontation follows the opposition's earlier march from Parliament to Vijay Chowk, after which INDIA bloc leaders submitted a memorandum to President Droupadi Murmu. The Congress and its allies are now seeking to take their demands to the Supreme Court as the dispute over electoral rolls and Kumar's position intensifies.

World.title: Less-than-2-lane NH stretches shrink to 8% as high-speed corridors surge
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Barely 8% of the countryâs 1.46 lakh km national highway (NH) network is now less than two lanes wide, compared with 2018-19, when such stretches accounted for nearly one-fourth of the network.

Data shows the length of less-than-two-lane NHs has shrunk by 64% over the past nine years to around 13,000 km.

In contrast, the length of high speed corridors (HSCs) has expanded more than 12-fold, while highways with four or more lanes have grown 1.5 times.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

Officials said the focus of highway development has increasingly shifted towards HSCs, greenfield access-controlled corridors and expressways. As these corridors are at least four lanes wide, their share in the overall NH network is expected to rise further.

They said this would facilitate faster movement of passengers and freight while reducing logistics costs.

However, despite the push for wider and seamless road connectivity, the average speed of trucks and the distance they cover each day remain well below global benchmarks. A truck in India typically covers only 300-350 km a day, compared with 700-800 km in the US and around 550-650 km in China.

Officials said a comparison of truck speeds on two parallel highways illustrates the advantage of access-controlled corridors. On the Ahmedabad-Vadodara Expressway, trucks were found to travel at an average speed of around 80 kmph, compared with about 52 kmph on the parallel NH-64. The study also found that daily truck traffic on the expressway is nearly double that on the existing national highway.

People aware of the govtâs plan to go for more HSCs said that the target is to build around 51,000 km of such network in the next 10 years, including the corridors developed or to be built by state govts.

Indians have been facing dangers in Middle East recently amid renewed tensions. On Saturday, 11 Indians were injured when Riyadh airport came under attack. A day later, the Indian embassy in Saudi Arabia announced that one of them had died.

The Embassy of India in Riyadh said it had been following up on Saturday's attack and was in touch with local authorities and hospital officials to enquire about the condition of the injured Indians.

World.title: Pargat Singh says ‘Congress is united’ as he takes charge of Punjab unit
World.content:
Congress MLA and former Indian hockey captain Pargat Singh, recently appointed president of the Punjab Pradesh Congress Committee, officially took charge on Sunday, asserting that “Congress is united.”

Punjab Congress in-charge and AICC General Secretary Sachin Pilot formally handed over the responsibility to Mr. Pargat. Addressing party workers in Chandigarh, Mr. Singh said the Congress had a responsibility not only to contest elections but also to be the voice of the people and stand firmly for their rights.

“The people of Punjab are waiting for their rights, justice and a secure future. It is our responsibility to meet the expectations of every section, from farmers to young people. The Congress is united, and our struggle is against a system that has failed to secure people’s rightful entitlements,” he said.

He said it was essential to understand the sentiments of people awaiting justice in sacrilege cases and to raise their voice in support of justice. The true test of any government, he added, was the public’s trust and the positive change it brought to people’s lives.

Hitting out at Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann and the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP), Mr. Singh said the government should focus on the problems facing Punjab’s people instead of worrying about the Congress team.

He said the Congress had a strong team of experienced leaders and dedicated workers. Referring to the experience of MP Sukhjinder Singh Randhawa, Leader of Opposition Partap Singh Bajwa and former Chief Minister Charanjit Singh Channi, he said the party would work collectively to safeguard Punjab’s interests.

He alleged that the politics of Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Union Home Minister Amit Shah were weakening democratic values in the country.

Mr. Pilot said the Congress’s objective was not merely to achieve political success but also to win the hearts of Punjab’s people and live up to their expectations. He expressed confidence that the unity of Congress workers and public support would help strengthen the party’s position in the state.

World.title: Community-led model to tackle drug abuse in 300 Haryana villages
World.content:
A community-led initiative to tackle drug abuse and improve rural youth’s access to education, career guidance and skill training was launched in 300 villages of Haryana’s Jind district on Sunday (October 11, 2026) under the “Panchgama Vikas Model”.

Conceived by Chandigarh Director-General of Police Sagar Preet Hooda, the voluntary, non-political initiative has been launched by the Haryana Professional Forum and Jind Social Forum, a network of volunteers with roots in Haryana.

Speaking at the launch event at Chaudhary Ranbir Singh University in Jind, Mr. Hooda said the model sought to mobilise educated professionals, businesspersons and other resourceful people to help rural communities access opportunities in education, employment and skill development.

Under the model, the 300 villages have been divided into 60 clusters of five villages each. Every cluster has a designated lead and a five-member team responsible for identifying local needs, engaging residents and guiding young people towards educational and career opportunities. The lead is preferably a professional, such as a doctor, engineer or professor, from outside the cluster.

“We are not here to offer money or jobs. We are here to give people our time and guide them towards opportunities,” Mr. Hooda said, emphasising that the initiative would rely on voluntary contributions of time, money and skills rather than financial incentives.

The programme will focus on bridging the information gap among rural youth about career options, entrance examinations, educational institutions and skill training. It will also promote sports, fitness and mentorship, besides seeking to address drug abuse and the growing trend of young people taking the illegal ‘dunki’ route to migrate abroad.

The initiative plans to establish smart libraries by upgrading existing government libraries and encouraging communities to set up new ones. Equipped with books, computers and internet connectivity, these libraries will serve as centres for career guidance and lectures by experts.

Mr. Hooda said a network of libraries across the 300 villages could help an expert reach 6,000 children in a single session, with 20 students participating from each village. The teams would approach individuals and institutions willing to donate books and computers and connect them directly with villages that need these resources.

“There is no shortage of resources in our State or country. The challenge is to identify and mobilise them effectively,” he said, adding that the model could be extended to other parts of Haryana once it stabilised in Jind.

Explaining the choice of Jind as the starting point, Mr. Hooda said the initiative sought to move beyond the mindset of restricting social responsibility to one’s own village. Children across villages, he said, should be treated as everyone’s responsibility.

Drug abuse remains a major concern in Haryana, with the problem spreading beyond areas bordering Punjab and Rajasthan. In several villages, residents have resorted to thikri pehras (community vigils) to catch suspected drug users and peddlers.

Jind Deputy Commissioner Vaishali Sharma was also present at the launch. Members of the cluster teams held meetings in their respective villages earlier in the day.

World.title: Sporadic protests break uneasy calm in Delhi
World.content:
Hundreds of protesters, including Rajya Sabha MP John Brittas and All India Students’ Association (AISA) president Neha Bora, were detained as sporadic protests against the special intensive revision (SIR) of electoral rolls and Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar continued across Delhi for the second consecutive day on Sunday (October 11, 2026) amid heavy security deployment and barricading across central Delhi to prevent protesters from reaching Jantar Mantar.

With shops in Connaught Place reopening after 24 hours and metro services resuming at stations shut on Saturday (October 10, 2026), normalcy returned in the morning. Shoppers trickled into the market, but the relative calm was disrupted as student organisations and other groups attempted to march through the commercial hub, only to be detained by the police. The heavy deployment of police personnel and barricades at key junctions appeared to make visitors hesitant to venture further into the area, as people walked past rows of shops but paused to assess the security arrangements.

The protests, called by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), continued despite restrictions on gatherings and movement in New Delhi. With demonstrators unable to assemble at Jantar Mantar, several groups attempted to mobilise at different locations across the city and the Outer Circle of Connaught Place became the epicentre.

Representatives of student and youth organisations, including the All India Students’ Federation (AISF), the Students’ Federation of India (SFI), the Democratic Youth Federation of India (DYFI) and the Krantikari Yuva Sangathan (KYS), attempted to take out a march in the morning.

Around noon, 60 to 70 protesters began marching from Gate 1 of Rajiv Chowk Metro station towards Gate 6 of Palika Bazaar with banners and placards, and raising slogans of “vote chor, gaddi chhod (vote thieves, leave the chair)”. They demanded the rollback of the SIR exercise and the resignation of Mr. Kumar.

The police and the Rapid Action Force (RAF) detained the protesters, and tense scenes unfolded as several demonstrators lay on the road, refusing to leave. Police personnel forcibly lifted some of them and shoved them into a bus. Some protesters sustained injuries and a man was seen bleeding from his forehead.

By 12.30 p.m., barricades had been erected and access to Janpath Road was cut off, further restricting movement through the area.

Around two hours later, a few AISA representatives gathered near Ramakrishna Ashram Marg Metro station and attempted to march towards Connaught Place. The police quickly moved in to stop them, and the ensuing chase halted traffic.

Police personnel, Central Reserve Police Force personnel and RAF members converged on the junction and detained protesters. Journalists covering the demonstrations were also rounded up. Neha Bora and other AISA representatives managed to cross a barricade and run towards Panchkuian Road before being intercepted and detained by a large contingent of police personnel.

Around 4 p.m., nearly 350 people associated with the Revolutionary Workers’ Party of India, Disha Students’ Organisation, Naujawan Bharat Sabha and Stree Mukti League began a rally from Connaught Place’s outer circle. The protesters moved along the inner circle before being picked up by the police near the Pind Balluchi square.

Later in the evening, women activists of the SFI were detained after 6 p.m. while taking out a ‘Tiranga Yatra’.

Protesters return

Several protesters said they returned on Sunday (October 11) because they did not want to abandon the cause, even though they were unable to reach Jantar Mantar.

“I was here yesterday, but the police did not allow me to cross even the first barricade, so I had to stand outside the entire day. Today, they at least let me till here. I will come tomorrow, I do not want to give up,” said a protester who had travelled from Mumbai.

Sarthak Mishra, a student at Central University of Haryana and who hails from Jharkhand, arrived in Delhi on Saturday night. “I had an exam on Saturday, which is why I missed yesterday, but I made sure I am here today. But no one else has arrived and the protest is not happening,” he said.

Questioning the scale of the security deployment, Mr. Mishra said the protesters were ordinary citizens who had come to raise concerns about voting rights. “We are unarmed normal civilians and the police are having the most dangerous weapons, batons for us. Is this needed for us? This is for terrorists, murderers or rapists and not for commoners like us,” he said.

“If the government is taking away our basic right to vote, it is a waste to call ourselves a democratic country,” he added.

Fanning out

As police action continued in central Delhi, KYS organised demonstrations outside the Supreme Court and on the Yamuna River, saying its activists were being prevented from protesting.

Several KYS activists staged a protest outside the Supreme Court against alleged police brutality. Minutes later, the participants, mostly women, were dragged away.

In a separate demonstration, KYS activists took boats and protested on the Yamuna, describing the river as the “new Jantar Mantar”. The organisation said it would continue its mobilisation against the CEC and the Election Commission.

Meanwhile, some detainees were allegedly taken to a community centre in Pandwalan Khurd, around 40 km from Connaught Place, and left there without adequate medical assistance or transport.

Lawyer Disha Verma alleged that peaceful protesters detained in Connaught Place were taken to a location near the LIC office, where police personnel made them kneel in a row, frisked them and took away their phones after deleting photographs and videos.

Some detainees were subsequently moved in buses with cramped compartments and inadequate ventilation and were allegedly beaten severely, she claimed.

According to Ms. Verma, the bus travelled through the Kapashera and Najafgarh areas before reaching Pandwalan Khurd around 7.30 p.m., with the detainees taken into a community centre by 8 p.m. She alleged that several detainees had sustained serious injuries, four minors were among them, and lawyers were prevented from entering the premises.

She also claimed that a crowd had gathered outside the centre, leaving the detainees vulnerable.

World.title: Anti-CEC protest Highlights, October 11: CJI Surya Kant declines to meet INDIA bloc leaders; Delhi Police detain women protesters in the evening
World.content:
A day ahead of the Opposition’s planned march to the Supreme Court on Monday (October 12, 2026), Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant on Sunday (October 11, 2025) declined a request by the Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha, Rahul Gandhi, for a meeting. The CJI’s office confirmed to The Hindu that the request for a meeting was “declined with reasons”.

Also read: Four Hindu Raksha Dal members arrested after video shows man, woman assaulted during Delhi protest

Rajya Sabha MP John Brittas and All India Students’ Association president Neha were among several protestors allegedly injured by security forces as they were being detained in the capital on Sunday (October 11, 2026), the second day of a protest called by youth organisations demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar.

In the evening, women SFI activists doing a ‘Tiranga Yatra’ were detained from Connaught Place after 6 p.m. and taken away in a bus by security forces. The SFI termed the detention of women post 6 p.m. as illegal and alleged that the women activists were beaten by male officers.

Also read: Many detained near Shivaji Park as Mumbai Police prevent protest against CEC

After getting released from detention, CJP co-convenor Ashutosh Ranka said he and other leaders of the outfit would approach Delhi Police on Monday (October 12, 2026) to seek a date for holding a peaceful protest at the Jantar Mantar. CJP leaders, who were set free on a condition that they would not “breach peace” for a year, claimed that their detention was illegal and their protest would continue till CEC resigns.

Also read | Restores people’s faith in justice system: Sibal after SC’s directions to government on protests

In a special sitting, the Supreme Court directed that people gathering peacefully should not be illegally detained and asked authorities to ensure that Delhi Metro functions normally, and that there is no disruption to internet services, subject to law and order conditions.

World.title: Central Delhi returns to normal life, but protests and heavy security keep city on edge
World.content:
Connaught Place began finding its way back to its familiar weekend rhythm on Sunday (October 12, 2026), but the return to normalcy was hesitant. Shoppers and diners trickled into the market after a day of closure, Metro services resumed and a few more establishments reopened. Yet, the sight of police personnel lining the roads, barricades narrowing access and detention buses moving through the Inner and Outer Circles remained a reminder that the protests against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar were far from over.

On the second day of protests, the easing of restrictions brought some movement back to central Delhi. But the market, usually packed with shoppers, visitors and people waiting outside popular restaurants and cafes, remained unusually quiet. Several shops and eateries stayed shut, while those that opened periodically closed their doors when protests flared at different points in Connaught Place.

“We came here to eat at a restaurant we really like. It is usually fully booked, and there is hardly any space to walk on the roads, with so many vendors and people taking up space. Today, CP does not even feel like CP,” said Aarti, a Lajpat Nagar resident who had arrived for lunch with her husband.

The contrast was difficult to miss. On a typical Sunday, the market’s colonnades draw families, shoppers and groups of friends, with queues spilling out of cafes and people moving between the shops.

Large contingents of the Delhi Police, Central Reserve Police Force and Rapid Action Force remained stationed across the market. Rows of buses and detention vehicles occupied one or two lanes along stretches of road, leaving less space for regular traffic. Vehicles continued to move, though temporary congestion built up when police personnel chased protesters and ushered them into waiting buses.

For onlookers, the detention vehicles became a spectacle of their own. Some stopped to watch as detainees shouted slogans from inside the buses, while others slowed down, pulled out their phones to capture the scene before moving on. Police personnel quickly cleared the crowds that gathered around such incidents, preventing them from blocking the roads.

Visitors appeared more cautious than usual. Some walked through the market, looking around before deciding whether to stay, while others continued towards the restaurants and shops that were open. Even with Metro stations operating again, the footfall remained well below what the market typically sees over a weekend.

The difference was not limited to Connaught Place. Although Metro services had resumed and the internet was functioning around Jantar Mantar, barricades remained at several points leading into central Delhi. On the road from Nizamuddin towards the city centre, concrete barricades were still in place on Sunday afternoon. At several checkpoints, even journalists were asked to show their identity cards before being allowed through.

The approach to the Jantar Mantar protest site from Ashoka Road was largely deserted by Sunday evening, apart from security personnel. After multiple protests in Connaught Place during the day, the deployment around the site remained heavy. Security personnel said there had been few attempts by protesters to enter the designated protest area on Sunday.

There were, however, small signs of activity returning to the neighbourhood. The Kerala House canteen, located close to Jantar Mantar and shut on Saturday, was functioning on Sunday, according to security staff. Its reopening offered a glimpse of ordinary life resuming even as the surrounding streets remained under close watch.

The Supreme Court’s directions and the reopening of Metro stations marked a change from the previous day, when restrictions had severely disrupted movement in central Delhi. Yet the continued police deployment and the possibility of fresh demonstrations meant that the easing was limited. For those who came to shop or spend their Sunday eating out, the market was accessible, but the sense of ease that usually accompanies a weekend visit was missing.

World.title: 1,854 voters submit Form 6 for inclusion of names in Assembly constituencies of Chennai district
World.content:
Assembly constituencies of Chennai district have registered poor turnout at the special camps for electors who intend to submit forms for inclusion of names on the electoral rolls.

According to Chennai District Election Office, 3,364 forms were issued during the special drive conducted on October 10 and October 11 while 2,483 forms were received from the voters.

Thiru Vi Ka Nagar (SC) registered the highest number of forms received with 379 residents submitting forms at the special camps while 493 forms were issued during the two days of the special drive. A total of 404 Form 6 were issued and 289 were received. As many as 90 voters submitted applications in Form 8 for shifting of residence and correction of entries in the constituency.

Anna Nagar registered the lowest number of forms submitted with officials receiving just 48 applications in Form 6 from residents for inclusion of names.

Voters in Virugambakkam have submitted 294 applications in Form 6 for inclusion of names, Dr. Radhakrishnan Nagar 92, Perambur 110, Kolathur 215, Villivakkam 57, Egmore 80, Royapuram 86, Harbour 76, Chepauk Thiruvallikeni 100, Thousand Lights 155, Anna Nagar 48, Virugambakkam 200, Saidapet 70, Thiyagarayanagar 100, Mylapore 120 and Velachery 56.

A large number of names were reportedly deleted from the rolls during the special intensive revision ahead of the Assembly elections and many electors who visited polling booths could not vote during the recent Assembly elections because their names were removed from the rolls. However, fewer voters were found at the special camps for inclusion of names on the rolls in the city on Sunday.

World.title: Protests will happen not just in Delhi but whole country: CJP
World.content:
The Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) on Sunday (October 11, 2026) vowed to intensify its agitation against Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar, even as around 200 people were detained. Protests were held at several places in the New Delhi area, which remained under a security chokehold.

The Supreme Court on Sunday (October 11, 2026) directed that people gathering peacefully should not be illegally detained, and asked the authorities to ensure the Delhi Metro functioned normally and that there was no disruption of Internet services, subject to the maintenance of law and order.

Keep track | Anti-CEC protest LIVE: CJI Surya Kant declines to meet INDIA Bloc leaders on October 12; Delhi Police detain women protesters after 6 p.m.

In a special sitting, a Bench of Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana also issued notice to the Centre while hearing a plea seeking contempt proceedings for the alleged violation of the court's direction to ensure there was no "complete prohibition" on metro and train services in Delhi due to the protest.

Earlier in the day, CJP leaders Abhijeet Dipke, Ashutosh Ranka and Saurav Das were released on the condition that they would not "breach the peace" for a year.

At a press conference, Mr. Das alleged that the government had turned the state against its own citizens, and said the authorities could have invited a delegation for talks instead of restricting protesters seeking to demonstrate at a designated site.

Delhi Police officials had taken away their phones during their detention without issuing any seizure memo, Mr. Das claimed, raising concerns that the devices might have been hacked or cloned.

"We suspect that, as alleged in similar cases involving activists in the past, phones could have been hacked or cloned to plant documents or other material that might later be used as evidence against us," he told media persons.

The CJP's agitation was continuing, he said, adding that protests would take place not just in Delhi but across the country.

"The protests are on... Protests will happen not just in Delhi but the whole country," Mr. Das said.

"This protest will not stop till Gyanesh [Kumar, Chief Election Commissioner] resigns," CJP co-convener Ashutosh Ranka said.

Referring to the condition imposed on their release, Mr. Das said they had been told there should be no breach of peace for one year.

"The breach of peace has been caused by Narendra Modi, Amit Shah and Gyanesh Kumar," Mr. Das said.

Protest at a designated protest spot is not disturbing the peace, Mr. Ranka said.

Delhi Police has registered 20 FIRs in connection with Saturday's CJP protest against the CEC over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, officials said on Sunday.

Early this morning, Abhijeet Dipke, Ashutosh Ranka and Saurav Das, who were put under preventive arrest following their detention at the Delhi airport a day earlier, were released after being produced before an executive magistrate.

In a statement, the CJP called the release of the three leaders a "major legal victory".

The CJP said the "arbitrary detentions" had sparked severe criticism and legal challenges amid an intense security clampdown across the capital over protests against the CEC.

"Finally Delhi Police is forced to release Abhijeet Dipke, Ashutosh Ranka and Saurav Das. Cockroaches never die," it posted on X.

World.title: Emergency, governor's rule imposed in KP as president approves cabinet decision
World.content:
Key developments:

Emergency imposed under Article 232, governor’s rule under Article 234

Cabinet recommended move due to KP govt’s ‘deliberate disengagement from the fight against terrorism’

Technocratic council formed; Fakhr Alam appointed as KP chief secretary

PTI’s Gohar condemns decision as undemocratic, says peace cannot be established by weakening provincial autonomy

Governor Kundi calls for unity for ‘new chapter’ in KP’s development

ISLAMABAD: The federal government on Sunday imposed an emergency and governor’s rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa following the president’s approval of the recommendations by the federal cabinet.

The measures have been approved under Articles 232 and 234 of the Constitution, the President House said in a statement. The two provisions pertain to the proclamation of emergency and governor’s rule.

Following the imposition, internet disruptions were being reported from parts of Peshawar, with Dawn unable to contact its correspondents there.

According to sources in the telecom sector, mobile network and data services have been slowed or shut down in selected areas of some cities. However, there is no province-wide shutdown of mobile data or internet.

Internet watchdog NetBlocks said network data showed a major disruption to internet connectivity in parts of KP as emergency was imposed.

The federal government also authorised the deployment of Pakistan Army troops and assets in aid of civil power in KP. On the ground, shipping containers were placed around the city of Peshawar to block several roads, with heavy police deployment.

The decision to impose the emergency provisions came during an emergency meeting of the federal cabinet chaired by Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, where he was briefed on the security situation in KP.

A statement issued by the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO) said cabinet members reviewed the situation and took note of the “provincial government’s deliberate disengagement from the fight against terrorism”.

The members proposed, given the “gravity” of the situation, that the PM advise the president to exercise “his constitutional authority and impose an emergency in the province under Articles 232 and 234 of the Constitution”.

The emergency imposition comes a day after PM Shehbaz met President Zardari and discussed the country’s overall security situation.

That meeting came amid heightened tensions between the PML-N-led federal government and the KP government led by the PTI — which is in opposition in the Centre. They have been at odds over various issues, particularly on the counterterrorism policy, which was one of the main reasons behind the breakdown of their Oct 3 talks .

The PTI has said it was being left out of security decisions concerning KP, which the Centre has denied . It also calls for reviewing the counterterrorism policy and opposes military operations.

On the other hand, the Centre has been criticising the KP government’s efforts to combat terrorism in the province and objects to its stance on dialogue with the Afghan Taliban.

It may be recalled that in July 2024, when Afridi’s predecessor Ali Amin Gandapur was the chief minister, the KP Assembly passed a resolution urging the federal government to consult with it and the provincial government before launching a new military operation.

The resolution, passed by a majority vote, cautioned that proceeding without provincial consent could hinder the offensive’s success and result in adverse consequences, for which the federal government would be responsible.

In December that year, the assembly voted unanimously against a potential military operation in parts of Khyber and Bannu districts.

About a year later, after Afridi became the KP CM, the provincial assembly convened a grand jirga with Governor Faisal Karim Kundi and other parties in attendance. The moot unanimously demanded that the Centre prioritise negotiations with Afghanistan and consult the KP government over Afghan policy.

Constitutional provisions

Emergency

Article 232 of the Constitution provides for the proclamation of emergency in a province.

It says, “If the president is satisfied that a grave emergency exists in which the security of Pakistan, or any part thereof, is threatened by war or external aggression, or by internal disturbance beyond the power of a provincial government to control, he may issue a Proclamation of Emergency.”

However, invoking this article “due to internal disturbances beyond the powers of a provincial government to control” requires a resolution from the provincial assembly of that province.

In case the president “acts on his own” — which is not currently the case — the Proclamation of Emergency is to be placed before both houses of Parliament for approval by each house within 10 days.

According to this provision, parliament “shall have power to make laws for a province, or any part thereof, with respect to any matter not enumerated in the Federal Legislative List” during the time of the proclamation of an emergency.

Nothing in this Article shall restrict the power of a provincial assembly to make any law which the Constitution empowers it to make, but if any provision of a provincial law is repugnant to any provision of an Act by Parliament, the latter would prevail and the provincial law would be void as long as the parliamentary Act is in effect.

Governor’s rule

On the other hand, Article 234 deals with the imposition of the governor’s rule “in case of failure of constitutional machinery in a province”. For imposition of the governor’s rule, the president simply requires a request from the provincial governor, it says.

“A proclamation issued under this Article shall be laid before a joint sitting and shall cease to be in force at the expiration of two months, unless before the expiration of that period it has been approved by resolution of the joint sitting and may by like resolution be extended for a further period not exceeding two months at a time,” the Constitution reads.

However, it adds that no such proclamation shall in any case remain in force for more than six months.

Article 233, which provides powers to the president to suspend certain fundamental rights during the emergency period, was not mentioned in the summary signed by President Zardari.

Where is Sohail Afridi?

A couple of hours after the imposition of emergency was announced, KP Information Minister Shafi Jan, who had been accompanying now dysfunctional KP Chief Minister Sohail Afridi on the PTI’s long march, claimed that the he had been taken into custody.

Dawn contacted police for a confirmation soon after Jan’s claim, but there was no response.

Meanwhile, MNA Shahid Khattak also claimed Afridi’s “arrest”, as well as MNA Junaid Akbar and others from there party.

He also said he would be leading the march now.

Later, the PTI issued a statement, condemning the “arrest” of Afridi and other and describing it as an act of “political victimisation and an attempt to weaken the province’s elected leadership and democratic institutions”.

It quoted PTI spokesperson Sheikh Waqas Akram as saying that Afridi’s “arrest” could not be viewed in isolation from the federal government’s decision to impose emergency and governor’s rule.

“The developments reflect a broader effort to bypass elected institutions and undermine the constitutional authority of the province.

“The arrest of Chief Minister Sohail Afridi and Junaid Akbar has exposed the political nature of the federal government’s actions. These measures are not directed at addressing security challenges; they are intended to weaken PTI, undermine the elected government of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and disregard the democratic will of its people,” he said.

Akram demanded the “immediate and unconditional release” Afridi, Akbar and “all other political detainees arrested in connection with the ongoing action against PTI”. He also demanded that the federal government publicly disclose the “legal grounds, specific charges and procedural basis for the arrests of the chief minister and the PTI provincial president”.

However, he sounded less certain while speaking on Geo News programme ‘Naya Pakistan’. He said they had received reports of Afridi and Akbar’s arrest, and adding that they were unable to confirm whether Jan and Khattak, too, had been taken into custody.

“We are unable to contact some people […] Because the internet has been suspended in several areas, we are unable to contact. You do not know the havoc they have created in KP. People are escaping and going into hiding,” he said.

In a clip shared on PTI’s official X account, Salman Akram Raja, the party’s secretary general, said, “We do not know where Sohail Afridi is, in what condition he has been kept. Junaid Akbar is also missing.”

When Minister of State for Interior Tallal Chaudhry was asked about reports of Afridi’s arrest during ‘Naya Pakistan’, he said some individuals had been detained in view of the law and order situation but did not confirm whether they included Afridi.

He said those who did not have a criminal record or were not wanted would be released.

Council, chief secretary appointed

Following the imposition of emergency, the federal government formed an 11-member technocratic KP Advisory Council to assist the governor with running the province.

Later, Governor Kundi also chaired the first meeting of the council, vowing to restore peace in the province.

Earlier in the day, the federal government appointed Dr Muhammad Fakhr Alam Irfan as the chief secretary of KP, according to an official notification, a copy of which is available with Dawn.

The appointment will take effect immediately and remain in place until further orders, it said.

Dr Irfan, a Grade 22 officer of the Pakistan Administrative Service (PAS), was previously serving as secretary of the Power Division in the federal Ministry of Energy. He hails from Mardan.

In a separate notification, the federal government also placed Muhammad Yahya Akhunzada at the disposal of the KP government with “immediate effect and until further orders”.

Akhunzada, a Grade 20 PAS officer, was serving as an additional secretary at PMO.

He hails from Charsadda and has also served as additional political agent for North and South Waziristan, secretary of health, information and education in KP, and commissioner of Dera Ismail Khan.

‘Peace cannot be established by weakening provincial autonomy’

PTI Chairman Gohar Ali Khan strongly condemned the imposition of emergency in KP and “completely rejected” it.

“This is an extremely alarming and grave political mistake and an undemocratic measure — the people will never accept such actions against their rights,” Gohar wrote in a post on X.

He stated: “There is still time; this decision can be withdrawn in a few days. Let the federation set aside its ego, understand the ground realities, accept legitimate demands, respect the sentiments and emotions of the people, and save the country from further political and economic damage and from pushing back the democratic process.

“Revisiting political decisions is not a sign of weakness but of wisdom in the national interest — otherwise, great damage will be done.”

Stressing that the mandate of the people of KP was their constitutional and legal right, the PTI chairman said: “Peace cannot be established, nor stability brought, by ignoring this mandate, weakening provincial autonomy, and creating conflict between the federation and the province.”

He asserted that there was “no disagreement on eliminating terrorism, but the fight against terrorism cannot be used as a justification to suppress the people’s voice, achieve political objectives, or limit the province’s constitutional authority”.

“Terrorism can only be combated through national unity and a joint strategy,” Gohar maintained.

“The federation cannot be strengthened by weakening the provinces. The solution to problems lies not in force, confrontation, and extraordinary measures, but in political wisdom, supremacy of the Constitution, and meaningful negotiations and practical steps.”

The PTI chairman said his party will raise the matter on “every constitutional, legal, and democratic forum for the protection of the people’s mandate, provincial autonomy, and constitutional and democratic rights”.

Later in the day, Gohar said PTI would challenge governor’s rule through the courts, assemblies and public forums.

The PTI parliamentary committee held a meeting and categorically rejected the imposition of an emergency and governor’s rule in KP. In a statement issued afterwards, it termed the development “a direct assault on the public mandate and an unacceptable move”.

“In a three-hour-long meeting of the PTI parliamentary party, the imposition of an emergency and governor’s rule in KP was strongly condemned and unanimously rejected. The meeting declared this step contrary to facts, unconstitutional, undemocratic, and a blatant insult to the public mandate of the province,” the statement said.

“The parliamentary party made it clear that measures to render the elected provincial government ineffective and usurp its constitutional powers could pose grave threats to the federal system and democratic traditions. Such decisions will increase political instability and public unrest in the province, while already existing tensions between the federation and the province will further intensify,” it added.

The statement added that the solution to political differences should be found through constitutional and democratic procedures and mutual consultation, rather than through force and coercion.

It also raised serious questions regarding the conduct of the federal government.

“The parliamentary party took the stance that if terrorism and the deteriorating law and order situation are the primary justification for the imposition of emergency, then why is the situation in Balochistan being ignored?” the statement asked.

The meeting also made it clear that Afridi was the elected chief minister and a member of the provincial assembly.

“Measures regarding his arrest, detention, or the usurping of his constitutional and democratic powers were strongly condemned. The meeting termed such actions an insult to the public mandate and a dangerous precedent for democratic traditions,” it said.

The Tehreek-i-Tahafuz-i-Ayin-i-Pakistan (TTAP), of which PTI is a part, termed the move a violation of the Constitution.

In a statement, the opposition alliance particularly assailed President Zardari’s PPP, claiming that the “most undemocratic actions and the imposition of governor’s rule” had been the hallmark of the party in the country’s history.

“On the one hand, despite the extremely dire administrative and law and order situation in Balochistan, no such step has been taken, while on the other hand, this province — whose assembly and government stand on the true and real mandate of the people — has been targeted,” it contended.

TTAP said it would convene a meeting on the matter and announce a joint course of action.

Governor Kundi urges unity for ‘new chapter’

Meanwhile, Governor Kundi said the decision was made for “establishing peace in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, the prosperity of its people, and the development of the province”.

“I am your governor, but beyond that, I want to play my role as a servant of this soil and a protector of your rights. Let us come together to bring peace to Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and begin a new chapter of our province’s development,” he said in a statement.

Kundi assured the public that it was his responsibility to raise their issues on the relevant forums.

Recalling the sacrifices made in the fight against terrorism, he said, “Now the time has come that we do not let these sacrifices go to waste and together establish lasting peace in our province.”

The PPP leader urged the public to set aside their political differences and unite for the province’s peace, the protection of its people, and the future of the coming generations.

“We must not let our differences become an obstacle in the path of our province’s common interests.”

Cannot allow PTI to destabilise the economy: PM tells cabinet

Addressing the cabinet meeting, the premier said the PTI-led KP government cannot be allowed to derail the stabilising economy amid tensions between the two sides.

“I will not allow them (PTI) to destabilise the economy,” he said during the meeting.

On terrorism in KP and Balochistan, the premier said, “The way common citizens are being martyred, the way police officials and security officials, children and mothers [..] there can be nothing more heart-wrenching.”

He recalled that Pakistan has repeatedly urged neighbouring Afghanistan to rein in the terrorist elements; however, “they still do not understand it”.

PM Shehbaz also reiterated his condemnation of the recent deadly Houthi attack on Saudi Arabia, noting the long-standing fraternal ties between Saudi Arabia and Pakistan.

“Our only goal is that peace should be restored in the region,” he said.

“Pakistan expresses solidarity with Saudi Arabia and stands with it. We will not tolerate any aggression against Saudi Arabia,” he said, adding that it was a “red line” for Pakistan.

During his address, PM Shehbaz also spoke of the recent staff-level agreement reached with the International Monetary Fund (IMF).

“It is hoped that we will unlock the $1.2 billion tranche within this year,” he said, recalling a meeting with the IMF’s Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva at the sidelines of the United Nations General Assembly (UNGA) last month.

He commended the political and military leadership for “working together day and night” in bringing fiscal discipline to Pakistan.

The premier recalled his visit to London last month, where he had met with senior executives from leading global financial institutions.

He also spoke of Pakistan’s diplomatic efforts in the international community, taking note of the appreciation Pakistan has received for mediation in the Middle East conflict.

“Pakistan continues to play its role with hard work and sincerity,” he said, particularly lauding the role of the Chief of Defence Forces and Chief of the Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir.

Additional input by Ikram Junaidi, Kalbe Ali

World.title: Info minister alleges 'nexus' between PTI-led KP govt, terrorists
World.content:
Information Minister Attaullah Tarar on Sunday alleged that the PTI-led government in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa had a “nexus” with terrorist groups, as the Centre explained that the province’s security situation necessitated the imposition of emergency there.

The press conference by government ministers — Tarar, Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi, Law Minister Azam Nazeer Tarar, and Minister of State for Interior Tallal Chaudhry — came shortly after the Centre imposed emergency in KP, citing the provincial government’s lack of efforts to combat terrorism.

The Centre and the PTI — which was in power in KP — have been at odds over various issues, particularly on the counterterrorism policy, which was one of the main reasons behind the breakdown of their Oct 3 talks .

Addressing the media in Islamabad, the information minister said all cabinet members who attended Sunday’s meeting were of the view that the “PTI government in KP is hand in glove with terrorists and has an unholy alliance with terrorists”.
